chapters.title: Chapter 202: Soren’s Tale [6]
paragraphs: ’As for my sister,’ Soren continued, his mental voice softening, ’she had recovered enough by the time of our wedding to be moved. I remember them taking her straight to the Temur Empire.’
Ethea let the piece of information settle, the memory of that day finally making sense. ’So that’s why she wasn’t at the wedding.’

’Mm. And actually, only a handful of people from the family attended it, mostly because of my father’s orders. He wanted to keep the whole affair as quiet as possible. And I think the same went for your family.’

Ethea remained silent for a moment. Her thoughts drifted back to their very first meeting, recalling the sheer shock in his eyes when he had looked at her. Back then, she had misread his expression entirely.
’...Did you find out who your bride was only on that day too?’ she asked.

’...Yeah,’ Soren admitted, a chuckle echoing through the link. ’And to be honest, I was completely lost. I couldn’t believe my eyes. I was the dud, the embarrassment of the family, yet there I was, marrying the most beautiful woman in all of Oros. It was hard to process, let alone accept that it was actually happening.’

Ethea felt her pulse quicken. The sudden praise caught her completely off guard, sending a warmth straight to her cheeks. But she quickly realized what was happening. He was, as usual, letting his raw thoughts leak without any filter.
’...Idiot,’ she thought, her mind scrambling to regain its usual composure.
Soren paused, sensing the sudden spike of flustered emotion through the bond. ’Huh? Did you say something?’
No response.

Soren cleared his throat, rubbing the back of his neck as he tried to smooth over the sudden awkwardness. ’Right... well, as I was saying. I had heard the rumors about your condition, of course. But actually standing there in front of you, seeing you in person... it felt completely surreal. It made me realize that despite everything the family had put me through, I was incredibly lucky to be the one standing by your side. And...’
Soren paused for a moment before letting out a self-deprecating laugh. ’...I was somehow relieved too.’
’...Why?’ Ethea asked, a hint of curiosity slipping into her tone.

’Well, I guess I have my own wild imagination and overthinking to blame,’ Soren replied, his mental voice warm with amusement. ’Before the ceremony, I was secretly agonizing over who they were going to force me to marry. I kept imagining the worst-case scenarios. I thought my father would pair me up with some incredibly terrifying, short-tempered noblewoman who would use me as a punching bag. Or worse, some snobbish, power-hungry lady who would treat me like a servant. I even seriously prepared myself for the possibility that I’d end up marrying an old widow who had bought me from the family.’
’...Pfft.’ Ethea couldn’t stop herself. The image of Soren, terrified and bracing himself to be handed over to an old woman, was too funny.
’A-An old widow?’ she teased. ’Is that really what you thought of your future bride?’

’Hey, can you blame me?’ Soren protested, though the warmth in his voice showed he was glad to hear her laugh. ’My father was smiling weirdly when he offered the deal. Whenever that man smiles like that, it usually means someone’s life is about to be ruined. So, I just assumed the worst.’
He paused for a second, his playful tone softening into something much more sincere.
’But then the doors opened... and it was you.’

At the sudden silence, Ethea found herself pulled back to the memory of their wedding day. At the time, she had been too numb, too consumed by her own ruined state to pay attention to the details of the ceremony. The faces, the vows, and even the man standing next to her had all been a distant blur. But now, a sudden curiosity gripped her.
’...What about my condition?’ she asked softly. ’What... did you think when you saw me like that?’
Soren understood her question instantly. It was a polite way of asking what you thought of a cripple like me.
’Or... were you just relieved because I was beautiful?’

’...’ Soren fell silent, turning her question over in his mind. He knew he had to tread carefully, but since he had decided to be honest, he had to give her a genuine answer without trying to paint himself in a better light.

’I won’t lie to you,’ Soren said. ’Finding out that the woman I was marrying was the most beautiful person I had ever seen... of course, it made me relieved. Honestly, it made me strangely happy, too... Wait... When I put it that way... Well, I guess I’m just pretty shallow.’
He laughed a little at himself, wondering if he messed up just now. (Urgh... Was that really necessary? She doesn’t hate me now, right?)
As the seconds ticked by, the awkwardness began to feed his insecurity, bringing back the nagging doubt that he had somehow ruined everything again.
’...Was that the only reason?’
Ethea’s voice finally came through, her tone unreadable.

’N-No,’ Soren said, wanting to correct the impression he had just made. ’I... I was also incredibly glad that it wasyou. Ethea, The Ice Empress. Actually, I admired you a lot. You were like a true hero, always risking your life to save others, protecting the helpless, and even making those massive donations... Well... What I am trying to say is, you were the perfect partner anyone could have ever asked for.’
’...’ Ethea continued to remain silent.

’But all of those thoughts were just a blur until we finally got home. Because that was when the noise of the day finally died down, and I could actually think properly. After putting you to bed, I lay there for hours, just staring at the ceiling as the reality of our situation gradually sank in. I realized we were both abandoned, essentially cast aside by everyone we knew. And then, I made a promise to myself. I decided that I would support and protect you until the very end, no matter what.’

chapters.title: Chapter 203: Ethea’s Tale [1]
paragraphs: ’But that was just the start,’ Soren said, his voice dropping as he steered them toward the memory of that night. ’I lay there thinking about all of this, and eventually, I fell asleep. It was during that sleep that my Awakening actually happened. My dormant power finally unlocked, though I didn’t even have time to process what was happening to my body. Because the very moment my eyes snapped open, I saw an assassin standing over your bed, their blade already falling toward you.’
Soren paused, letting the memory of that split second settle between them before his tone grew serious.

’Ethea... Before I go any further, I want you to know something. I obviously know you were the actual target of that assassination. But... I also know the incident that left you in this condition was no accident. There is someone powerful, whether it is a single person or a whole organization, behind all of this. I think they are probably your biggest enemies, and they must have been the ones who opened that gate as well.’
The mental link remained still as he let his words sink in, giving her space to process what he was saying.

’But I don’t know who they are,’ Soren admitted. ’I don’t know why they are targeting you relentlessly, or... how your father is involved in all of this. That is why I am hoping to get those answers from you.’
The connection fell into a long, suspended pause. Soren waited as the seconds stretched on, eventually realizing that he might have pushed a bit too far.
However, he had no desire to corner her, so he focused on finishing the food, placing the lid back on the pot to let it simmer.
A minute passed.
’Ethea...’
’You don’t have to answer if you don’t want to,’ he sent through the link, his tone easing to reassure her. ’I only brought it up because—’
’Soren.’
Ethea’s voice cut him off, carrying a freezing edge that made him freeze in place.
’That... wasn’t an assassin.’
Soren blinked. ’Huh? What do you mean?’
Another pause stretched between them. When her voice returned, it sounded incredibly distant, as if she were forcing herself to face a nightmare she had spent so much time trying to ignore.
’...I think... it was my older brother.’
’?!’ Soren froze, his heart hammering against his ribs. The revelation caught him entirely off guard.
’Y-you mean... Calix?’ he asked, his thoughts scrambling.

He immediately thought back to their wedding day. Aside from her parents, Calix was the only family member who had actually bothered to attend. Although they had barely spoken, Calix had left a good impression on him. He had seemed polite, presenting himself with respect. But now, a sudden wave of disgust hit Soren. It seemed the man was just like his father, a two-faced snake hiding his venom behind a pleasant smile.
But Ethea’s next words only deepened his confusion.
’No... it was not him,’ she sent, her tone turning tight. ’Though he might have had a hand in it.’

Soren paused, trying to reconcile her words with what little he knew of her family. As far as he could remember, Ethea only had two brothers. One was Calix, and the other was a younger boy named Roan, who was only about fourteen. There was no way it could be him. After all, he was still just a child. The idea of someone that young attempting to murder his own sister was too absurd to even consider. Not to mention the build of the assassin.
’Wait...’ Soren paused, a sudden chill settling in his chest as he tried to make sense of her words. ’Don’t tell me... you have... another brother?’
The mental link trembled slightly with the weight of her admission, the connection suddenly feeling incredibly fragile.

’...His name is Julian,’ Ethea continued, her thoughts turning tight. ’But you won’t find his name in public data, and you will never hear anyone, even my father, speak of him. To the rest of the world, he doesn’t exist.’
Soren stood completely still by the stove, the wooden spoon in his hand forgotten. ’What do you mean? How can a son of the Morvain family just... not exist?’
’Because...’
She paused, a cold, bitter note echoing through their bond.
’My family is just as rotten as yours, Soren. Perhaps even more so. Beacuse your family did not completely erase you or your sister from the face of the earth at least.’
Soren froze. The parallel struck him instantly, a sharp piece of realization falling into place.
This Julian guy might be both unawakened and an illegitimate child.
As if reading his thoughts, Ethea’s voice returned to confirm his suspicion.
’He’s unawakened like you were, and also a product of an affair... My father’s, to be more precise.’
Soren fell completely silent.

His opinion of his father-in-law, already incredibly low, quickly hit rock bottom and plunged straight into the negative. He then recalled how Darius had acted during their wedding, behaving like a devoted husband. He also remembered when the man had first visited them, speaking with such warmth and acting as if his wife were the center of his universe.
Soren didn’t truly expect Darius to be like his own father.
No, maybe he shouldn’t be surprised anymore. Heck, the man was probably even more depraved than he could imagine.
’Julian was one of my father’s biggest mistakes,’ Ethea’s voice was laced with cold disgust. ’He was the physical proof of his hypocrisy.’
Soren kept his gaze fixed on the stove, listening in silence as the ugly truth unfolded. He didn’t interrupt, sensing that she needed to get these words out just as much as he needed to hear them.

’To protect his public reputation as a flawless leader and a perfect husband, he decided Julian had to vanish,’ she continued, her thoughts sharp and bitter. ’So, he declared the child dead at birth. He hid his existence from the world entirely, ensuring no one would ever find out about his failure.’
The mental link went quiet for another beat. When her voice returned, it sounded smaller, stripped of its sharp edge and replaced by a hollow quiet.
’I only learned it by accident.’

chapters.title: Chapter 204: Ethea’s Tale [2]
paragraphs: ’I don’t know the full story,’ Ethea continued. ’And I only saw him a few times throughout my life. But even during those rare moments, the depth of his hatred was unmistakable.’
Soren kept his gaze fixed on the stove, listening in silence.

’It was written all over his face. In his eyes. I did not need to know the details of his birth to understand that my very existence was a torment to him. And I was probably the person he despised the most.’
A bitter tremor rippled through the mental link.

’Because I was the pure-blooded child,’ she explained, her thoughts turning flat. ’I was the genius, the prodigy, the designated successor of the family. As a result, I received all the cultivation resources, the prestige, and the family’s affection. I had everything he was denied. In his eyes, that made me the living symbol of his misfortune.’
Soren fell silent.
He stared down at the stove, a strange feeling settling in his chest.

In a way, he and Julian shared a similar past. Their circumstances were mostly different, but the core of their experience was the same, as they had both been treated like ghosts, completely ignored by the people who should have cared for them.
He understood that suffocating neglect. He knew exactly what it felt like to exist in the shadows while everyone else basked in the light.
Because of that, he could understand why Julian felt that way. He could understand the deep resentment that built up over years of being treated like a non-person.
Yet, Soren also knew that Julian’s hatred was misplaced. Ethea had nothing to do with their father’s sins, nor did she choose to be born with the talent and status that Julian had been denied.
But to a broken mind locked in the dark, logic often did not matter.

Or perhaps Julian had simply recognized his own helplessness. He could never hope to touch their father; Darius was far too powerful, shielded by both his immense strength and his absolute authority. Ethea, however, had been a target within reach. As the golden child who possessed everything Julian had ever wanted, she became the perfect focus for all of his bottled-up rage. A mind broken by that kind of isolation simply needed someone to blame, and she was the most visible symbol of his misery.
And then, she had lost everything.

When Ethea was crippled and cast aside, Julian must have seen it as his ultimate moment. With her powers gone and the family no longer protecting her, she was finally vulnerable. To a mind that had festered in the dark for so long, it must have been the perfect opportunity to strike, to unleash years of silent torment, and to finally end her life in an act of desperate revenge.

Yet, Soren knew he couldn’t be entirely sure of this theory just yet. Ethea had mentioned that Calix might have had a hand in the attack, which meant Julian wasn’t acting completely alone. Moreover, the lingering suspicion in the back of his mind wouldn’t quiet down — he still suspected that Darius was the one ultimately pulling the strings behind everything.

’I wasn’t sure at first.’ Thankfully, he didn’t have to wait for long as Ethea soon continued her tale. ’When the assassin came, my condition was... terrible. I was in no state to process anything clearly, though those eyes... the hatred in them... they had seemed familiar to me even then.’
The mental link wavered, carrying a strange sense of vulnerability that Soren had never felt from her before.

’...And while I couldn’t move, I still could have called out for help, but the truth is, I didn’t even try to,’ she admitted. ’I simply stared up at the falling blade, utterly consumed by the feeling that this was my fate, and that perhaps I even deserved it.’
She paused, a soft tremor passing through their connection.
’But then... then you woke up and threw yourself at him. You saved me when I had already given up.’
Soren felt a tight ache in his chest. He hadn’t realized how close she had been to letting go entirely that night. He kept his gaze lowered, allowing her the space to pull herself back together.
The silence stretched for a few seconds before her voice returned, sounding much softer.
’I never had the chance to say it. And I know it is far too late now. But thank you, Soren. For saving my life... no... for bringing me back to life.’
Another pause followed, gentler this time.
’And I want to apologize. For how I treated you back then. I was cold, indifferent, and probably rude. You... did not deserve that.’
Soren gripped the handle of the wooden spoon, caught off guard by her sincerity.
’You don’t need to apologize for that,’ he quickly reassured her. ’Given everything you were going through, it was completely understandable.
In truth, he had never cared that much about her cold attitude or her lack of gratitude back then. He had only cared about keeping her alive.
’I know,’ Ethea replied. ’I... I just wanted to get it off my chest. And now I have said it, I feel a lot better.’
Soren smiled, genuinely glad that she was also being open with him about these things.
’So, when did you figure it out then?’
’...When my father visited us for the first time.’
’I see...’ Soren gave an internal nod, the missing pieces finally falling into place. ’Did he... say anything to you then? Telepathically, I mean?’
’Yes,’ she replied, a hollow note entering her mental voice. ’He told me: Please, forgive that fool.’
Beside the stove, Soren’s hands subconsciously clenched into tight fists.
Forgive? Really?

The guy had come into her room with a blade, intent on carving the life out of her while she lay there entirely defenseless. He had only been stopped because Soren had woken up in time to fight him off. Yet, her own father’s reaction to his daughter almost being killed was to ask her to let it go, brushing it aside to protect the son who had tried to kill her.
The man was truly a scumbag through and through.

Moreover, the lingering suspicion in the back of his mind wouldn’t quiet down — he still suspected that Darius was the one ultimately pulling the strings behind everything.
’I wasn’t sure at first.’ Thankfully, he didn’t have to wait for long as Ethea soon continued her tale. ’When the assassin came, my condition was... terrible.
I was in no state to process anything clearly, though those eyes... the hatred in them... they had seemed familiar to me even then.’
The mental link wavered, carrying a strange sense of vulnerability that Soren had never felt from her before.

’...And while I couldn’t move, I still could have called out for help, but the truth is, I didn’t even try to,’ she admitted. ’I simply stared up at the falling blade, utterly consumed by the feeling that this was my fate, and that perhaps I even deserved it.’
She paused, a soft tremor passing through their connection.
’But then... then you woke up and threw yourself at him.
You saved me when I had already given up.’
Soren felt a tight ache in his chest.
He hadn’t realized how close she had been to letting go entirely that night.
He kept his gaze lowered, allowing her the space to pull herself back together.
The silence stretched for a few seconds before her voice returned, sounding much softer.
’I never had the chance to say it.
And I know it is far too late now.
But thank you, Soren.
For saving my life... no... for bringing me back to life.’
Another pause followed, gentler this time.
’And I want to apologize.
For how I treated you back then.
I was cold, indifferent, and probably rude.
You... did not deserve that.’
Soren gripped the handle of the wooden spoon, caught off guard by her sincerity.
’You don’t need to apologize for that,’ he quickly reassured her. ’Given everything you were going through, it was completely understandable.
In truth, he had never cared that much about her cold attitude or her lack of gratitude back then.
He had only cared about keeping her alive.
’I know,’ Ethea replied. ’I...
I just wanted to get it off my chest.
And now I have said it, I feel a lot better.’
Soren smiled, genuinely glad that she was also being open with him about these things.
’So, when did you figure it out then?’
’...When my father visited us for the first time.’
’I see...’ Soren gave an internal nod, the missing pieces finally falling into place. ’Did he... say anything to you then?
Telepathically, I mean?’
’Yes,’ she replied, a hollow note entering her mental voice. ’He told me: Please, forgive that fool.’
Beside the stove, Soren’s hands subconsciously clenched into tight fists.
Forgive?
Really?
The guy had come into her room with a blade, intent on carving the life out of her while she lay there entirely defenseless.
He had only been stopped because Soren had woken up in time to fight him off.
Yet, her own father’s reaction to his daughter almost being killed was to ask her to let it go, brushing it aside to protect the son who had tried to kill her.
The man was truly a scumbag through and through.

chapters.title: Chapter 205: Ethea’s Tale [3]
paragraphs: ’Ethea. I think your father might have been behind the entire thing from the very start. And I believe he is the one who forced the police to drop the investigation.’
The link fell quiet for a moment, as if she were weighing his words against her own deep understanding of the man who ruled their family.

’I am not sure if he was fully involved in planning Julian’s plot,’ she replied. ’But I highly doubt he was completely ignorant of it. My father is a man who insists on controlling everything. There is no way Julian could have acted without his tacit permission. But you are right about the police part.’
So I was right about that much.
Soren thought and decided to strike while the iron was hot.
’What do you think of him, Ethea? What kind of person is he, in your opinion?’

’I... I can’t read him,’ she admitted, her thoughts carrying a rare note of frustration. ’I never could. To the world, and even to us most of the time, he perfectly embodies the role of a loving parent and a devoted husband. But there are rare moments when the mask slips. Just for a fraction of a second, you catch a glimpse of something entirely hollow, as if the warmth he displays is nothing more than a carefully rehearsed act. And honestly, I suspect even those slips are deliberate, perhaps to show us who he really is or to make us think he is like that.’
She paused, organizing her thoughts.

’He projects benevolence, yet he is utterly ruthless when required, especially when anyone threatens anything he treasures, including the family. Beneath all that, he is incredibly scheming, calculating every move three steps ahead. It is impossible to ever truly feel safe around him.’

’I see...’ Soren squinted his eyes, his own opinion matching hers. Since she had no trouble talking that way about her father, he decided to lay his cards on the table. ’Ethea. There is something else you should know. Before you woke up... I had a confrontation with your father. Do you want to hear it?’
Ethea agreed without hesitation as she had already suspected it.

Soren took a deep breath, sorting through the memory of that tense meeting. He then relayed the conversation to her, piece by piece, explaining why Darius had abandoned her, his deliberate choice to designate Soren as her partner, and the chilling reason he had allowed both the assassination attempt and the latest attack to occur. However, he carefully omitted the parts where he had admitted his feelings for her and how he discovered Darius’s true nature thanks to Advanced Appraisal.
’...That is everything,’ Soren finished detailing the exchange. ’...What do you think? Knowing him... how much of what he told me do you think was actually true?’
Ethea remained silent for a long moment as she processed everything Soren had shared.

’As I mentioned earlier, he is truly benevolent when he wants to be. He doesn’t hesitate to bestow favors or gifts when it suits him. So the things he gave you, most of them, should be genuine. It aligns with how he maintains his image.’

’As for why he ’abandoned’ me, I also don’t know what to believe. In the past, whenever he told me to make more friends and live a simpler life, I always took it as a test. I assumed he was challenging my resolve, so I only pushed myself harder to become the perfect successor. Hearing what he said to you, though, makes me think that perhaps I might have misread those moments. But even that doubt could be exactly what he wanted to plant in my mind. He is entirely capable of predicting that we would have this conversation, and he might have tailored his words to make me question my own memories.’

Soren nodded slowly while his eyes squinted. ’What about your past, then? How much of what he told me was actually true? And... If you are comfortable sharing, I want to hear it from you. Your real past.’
’...’ A relaxed ripple passed through the link, suggesting she was smiling.

’Most of what he said was true,’ she admitted. ’For as long as I can remember, I have always been incredibly curious. I was drawn to books before I could even read them, fascinated by how letters combined to form words. Once I figured out how to piece those symbols together, it felt like unlocking a game, and the process of learning became genuinely fun. I absorbed everything around me.’

’But to the adults in the family, that must have been pretty shocking. They praised me constantly, calling me a genius before I even knew what the word meant. As a child, I naturally loved that positive attention and wanted to keep seeing those proud looks. I pushed myself as hard as I could to keep impressing them, wanting to meet every new standard they set. And perhaps, my father was right in that regard. I did end up trapped in a cycle of striving to be the perfect successor. But...’
Her mental tone grew a bit firmer.

’He was wrong about one important thing. While my upbringing differed from what most people envision as a typical childhood, it was the only normal I knew. I had fun. I genuinely enjoyed what I did, and I never hated my life back then.’
She paused, the mental connection carrying a faint trace of nostalgia before it quickly faded.

’But that simple joy was bound to end eventually. As I grew, the praises slowly became expectations, and those expectations turned into rigid demands. I started to notice how the warmth in my relatives’ eyes depended entirely on my performance. If I excelled, they smiled. If I struggled, their expressions chilled.’
The link grew cold as her thoughts turned practical.

’With that realization, my perspective shifted. I slowly began to understand the real world, the family politics, and the true nature of the relationships around me. Studying and training were no longer just a hobby. They transformed into a necessity for my survival, so I pushed myself even harder, eventually becoming the so-called ’Ice Empress’ everyone knew. Though, obviously, all of that effort was not enough to prevent me from ending up in this state.’

chapters.title: Chapter 206: Ethea’s Tale [4]
paragraphs: ’Ethea...’ A sharp ache tightened in Soren’s chest, but he forced it down, steeling his resolve to push into the dark corners they had both been avoiding till now. ’Ethea... What exactly happened back then? Who did this to you? Is it... connected to the Zero Circle organization?’
The relaxed atmosphere vanished instantly. The mental link went completely rigid, the lingering warmth from her childhood memories snapping shut like a heavy vault door.
’Where did you hear that name?’ she asked, her voice dropping to a sharp, defensive whisper that seemed to echo directly in his mind.

’The Emperor and President Craig,’ Soren replied, keeping his focus steady. ’They told me about it when I asked who the enemy might be. I heard you fought with them a few times before, and they excel at manipulating gates.’
’I see...’
The connection fell still again as Ethea went silent for a few minutes, gathering her thoughts before finally deciding to reveal everything.

’...The truth is... I can’t recall anything about that day. There are only a few blurry fragments left, but they make absolutely no sense when I try to piece them together. It is as if my memory of those exact moments has been completely hollowed out. I don’t know whether the people who planned the incident did it to protect their identities, or if someone else altered my mind.’
She paused, a detached, almost clinical tone taking over as she analyzed her own tragedy.

’Perhaps it was just a natural consequence of the trauma. Considering the state they found me in, wiped clean of mana and on the verge of death, it was a miracle that I even survived long enough to fall into that coma. And...’
She paused, a sharp knot of tension tightening the connection as she brought up a detail that had been quietly conflicting with her view of her father.
’And... I think the one who actually saved me... was my father.’
’Actually... my father is a spirit master.’

’And... In one of those blurry fragments, right as I was losing consciousness, I remember falling into pitch-black darkness. But it wasn’t the natural darkness of losing consciousness or dying. It felt... alive. It felt like something was intentionally wrapping around me to pull me away from the brink.’
The connection pulsed with uneasiness.

’That must have been one of his contracted spirits. It must be the one who kept me alive until I was rescued. That’s exactly what makes me so conflicted. Because it doesn’t make sense. If he truly wanted me dead, or if he was entirely indifferent to my survival, he shouldn’t have saved me in the first place. He could have just let me die right there.’
So that’s why...
Soren clenched his fists even tighter, as everything was starting to line up.

’After a lot of thinking, the only logical conclusion I can come up with is that he used me as bait. As I told you before, he absolutely loathes it when someone messes with his treasured things. To him, the family’s reputation and my value as his successor were his ultimate possessions. He would never tolerate outside forces trying to destroy what he built. And, perhaps realizing they didn’t want me truly dead, he must have deliberately allowed the attack to happen just to lure out the ones operating behind the scenes. He must have used that opportunity to try and catch them, or at the very least, force them to leave a clue.’
’I see,’ Soren replied, his mental voice steady despite the dark realization settling in his gut. ’It finally makes sense now.’
Everything Darius had done aligned perfectly with the actions of a man who calculated every move based on risk and reward.

’But that is just my theory,’ Ethea added, a flicker of fresh doubt rippling through the connection. ’And to be honest, I am not so sure about it since his visit today, suddenly wanting to take us with him. Or... perhaps he had already uncovered whatever he was looking for and judged he would be able to protect us from now on, and changed his plans accordingly.’

’...What about that Julian guy then?’ Soren asked, squinting slightly as he turned the problem over in his mind. ’That is the only thing that doesn’t click. If your father controlled the entire sequence, why did he let that happen?’

’Perhaps my father simply made a mistake,’ Ethea replied, her thoughts drifting into a more contemplative rhythm. ’Or... it must be a part of his schemes that I haven’t figured out yet. But at least, we can rest assured that he doesn’t want us dead now.’
Soren remained silent.
Well, shemight be safe, buthewas probably not included in that calculation. To Darius, he was just a pawn thrown into the equation to see how the board shifted.

Fortunately, she seemed unaware of this distinction for now, still grouping them together as a single unit in her father’s eyes, and he had no intention of ruining her fragile peace of mind by pointing it out. So, before she got suspicious, he could only shift the topic.
’Then what about the Zero Circle? Do you think they are connected to what happened to you?’

’Since I have no concrete memories of that day, it is incredibly difficult to say for certain. But they must be involved, at least when it comes to the gate-related matters. An anomaly of that scale couldn’t have been triggered by ordinary means.’
She paused, the connection growing heavy as she weighed the sheer complexity of the past.

’I also suspect they weren’t acting alone. There must have been multiple parties involved in the background. The entire incident was simply too massive and intricate for a single organization to orchestrate without leaving a massive trail.’

Soren frowned, the sheer scale of the conspiracy making his chest tighten. ’That many factions targeted you? Just who exactly were you fighting against? And why did they even do it? Did they want... something from you?’
’...I’m sorry, Soren,’ Ethea murmured, a wave of regret bleeding through the link. ’I cannot tell you. Even if I wanted to, I simply can’t.’
Soren blinked, sensing the abrupt wall she had just put between them. ’Why not?’
’Because...’

chapters.title: Chapter 207: What is An Authority? [1]
paragraphs: ’Because I have sworn a binding oath and have mental restrictions,’ Ethea explained. ’The moment I try to focus on those specific details with the intention of sharing them with anyone unrelated, or even discussing them in unauthorized locations, the restriction activates. It locks down my speech and thought patterns regarding the matter.’
Soren frowned, trying to grasp its severity. ’Is there really no way around it?’

’...It was done by a ninth-circle master,’ she replied after a brief pause. ’Unless the caster themselves removes it, or someone even stronger forces it open, breaking it is impossible. My mind would collapse before the restriction even fractured.’
A ninth-circle master.
Soren was dumbfounded.

While he knew she possessed high-level connections, he never expected her ties to reach such an impossible echelon. After all, the ninth circle represented the ultimate peak of power, the true rulers and protectors of this world. Only a handful of such individuals existed across Etenia, revered as the living legends who had pulled humanity back from the brink of extinction. For someone of that mythical stature to be directly involved in securing her oath shifted the entire paradigm of the situation.
Even so, a pressing concern cut through his shock, prompting him to verify the nature of the restriction. ’Did you take this oath willingly, or were you forced into it?’

’I did it of my own volition,’ Ethea replied, her voice softening slightly to ease his concern. ’You do not need to worry about that aspect. And... I am sorry that I cannot give you the answers you are looking for.’
Soren shook his head inwardly, keeping his voice gentle. ’No, it is alright. I understand.’

Yet, the contradiction bothered him. If she had access to the most powerful existences in the world, the people capable of rewriting history itself, their absence during her tragedy made no sense. ’If you had their backing, why didn’t they help you back then or even after? Aren’t they the most powerful beings in the world?’

’I... I am unable to answer that either,’ she finally admitted, a faint trace of weariness coloring her thoughts. ’However, I can tell you that I have already severed all contact with them. So, let us not speak of them anymore.’
Soren suppressed his growing curiosity, choosing to respect her boundaries. Still, one critical, life-threatening matter remained unaddressed, and he could not let it slide.
’Alright,’ he said, shifting his focus. ’But there is one more thing I need to ask. Ethea... Do you know that you are... cursed?’
’...Yes. However, I only truly realized it after this incident. But... how do you know about it?’

’Well... let’s say I have a hidden appraisal ability,’ Soren replied honestly, deciding there was no point in hiding it from her now. ’And... I have already discovered the curse, but due to circumstances, I couldn’t bring it up till now.’
’I see...’ Ethea hummed, secretly happy he shared his secret with her. ’But how powerful is this ability of yours? Can you see the exact details?’

’It’s pretty advanced. It allowed me to see that it is an eighth-circle curse called Eclipse’s Erosion,’ Soren explained. ’And the reason you almost died back then was due to a strange effect it triggered, though I couldn’t read the specifics of it.’
’Eclipse’s Erosion?’ Ethea repeated, the mysterious name clearly catching her off guard.
’Does it ring a bell?’ Soren asked, a hint of hope rising in his chest.
’...No, unfortunately. I have very little knowledge about curses, especially those at such a high level,’ she paused. ’But who could have done this...’
While Ethea trailed off, Soren focused on the meal; in a few more minutes, it would be ready to serve.
A few minutes passed as the rising aroma of the meal filled the air. Ethea remained lost in her thoughts, probably pondering everything they had just talked about.
"It’s ready."
As Soren whispered and prepared to serve, she finally broke the silence.
’Soren... what else did you see when you looked?’ she asked, her tone carrying a mix of vulnerability and genuine curiosity.

Soren expected the question. He had already decided to be upfront about the practical details, but he carefully filtered out the unique metrics provided by his Investment Authority. He had no intention of mentioning that he could read her exact mental state, gauge her hidden potential, or view her investment value. At least not yet. The risk was too great now. It’s not that he didn’t trust her; it’s just that he completely distrusted the forces acting from the shadows. There were people out there who could easily pry into minds, peel back secrets through strange abilities, or even extract memories through sheer force. Keeping the deepest details to himself was the only way to ensure both of their safety.

’I could see your basic info, detailed physical condition, your current mana capacity, and your affinities,’ Soren replied calmly, keeping his explanation grounded. ’I also saw your abilities, the curse, and something called Authority. And I was actually going to talk about this all with you.’
Ethea seemed to digest this, processing the scope of what he could do.
Before she could dwell on it further, Soren decided to voice a question that had been lingering in the back of his mind for a long time.
’Ethea,’ he asked, his tone shifting to one of genuine curiosity. ’Do you know what an Authority is? And... do you have any idea why yours is ’dormant’?’
’...An Authority?’ Ethea repeated, a brief flicker of surprise passing through her eyes before she caught herself. ’Oh, right. You wouldn’t know about that yet.’
She paused, organizing her thoughts to explain a concept that few in the world ever had the privilege to learn.

’An Authority is a mystical power born from a direct comprehension of the fundamental laws of the world. It isn’t just standard magic; it’s more of a conceptual command over reality itself. For example, a regular cultivator might cast a spell to create and control fire, but someone with an Authority over flames doesn’t need a spell. They simply dictate the concept of heat and combustion, bypassing the natural order entirely. And...’
Her tone turned solemn as she continued.
’To even stand a chance at reaching the pinnacle, becoming a ninth-circle master, one must learn and master an Authority.’

It locks down my speech and thought patterns regarding the matter.’
Soren frowned, trying to grasp its severity. ’Is there really no way around it?’
’...It was done by a ninth-circle master,’ she replied after a brief pause. ’Unless the caster themselves removes it, or someone even stronger forces it open, breaking it is impossible.
My mind would collapse before the restriction even fractured.’
A ninth-circle master.
Soren was dumbfounded.
While he knew she possessed high-level connections, he never expected her ties to reach such an impossible echelon.
After all, the ninth circle represented the ultimate peak of power, the true rulers and protectors of this world.
Only a handful of such individuals existed across Etenia, revered as the living legends who had pulled humanity back from the brink of extinction.
For someone of that mythical stature to be directly involved in securing her oath shifted the entire paradigm of the situation.
Even so, a pressing concern cut through his shock, prompting him to verify the nature of the restriction. ’Did you take this oath willingly, or were you forced into it?’
’I did it of my own volition,’ Ethea replied, her voice softening slightly to ease his concern. ’You do not need to worry about that aspect.
And...
I am sorry that I cannot give you the answers you are looking for.’
Soren shook his head inwardly, keeping his voice gentle. ’No, it is alright.
I understand.’
Yet, the contradiction bothered him.

If she had access to the most powerful existences in the world, the people capable of rewriting history itself, their absence during her tragedy made no sense. ’If you had their backing, why didn’t they help you back then or even after?
Aren’t they the most powerful beings in the world?’
I am unable to answer that either,’ she finally admitted, a faint trace of weariness coloring her thoughts. ’However, I can tell you that I have already severed all contact with them.
So, let us not speak of them anymore.’
Soren suppressed his growing curiosity, choosing to respect her boundaries.
Still, one critical, life-threatening matter remained unaddressed, and he could not let it slide.
’Alright,’ he said, shifting his focus. ’But there is one more thing I need to ask.
Ethea...
Do you know that you are... cursed?’
However, I only truly realized it after this incident.
But... how do you know about it?’
’Well... let’s say I have a hidden appraisal ability,’ Soren replied honestly, deciding there was no point in hiding it from her now. ’And...
I have already discovered the curse, but due to circumstances, I couldn’t bring it up till now.’
’I see...’ Ethea hummed, secretly happy he shared his secret with her. ’But how powerful is this ability of yours?
Can you see the exact details?’
’It’s pretty advanced.

It allowed me to see that it is an eighth-circle curse called Eclipse’s Erosion,’ Soren explained. ’And the reason you almost died back then was due to a strange effect it triggered, though I couldn’t read the specifics of it.’
’Eclipse’s Erosion?’ Ethea repeated, the mysterious name clearly catching her off guard.
’Does it ring a bell?’ Soren asked, a hint of hope rising in his chest.
’...No, unfortunately.
I have very little knowledge about curses, especially those at such a high level,’ she paused. ’But who could have done this...’
While Ethea trailed off, Soren focused on the meal; in a few more minutes, it would be ready to serve.
A few minutes passed as the rising aroma of the meal filled the air.
Ethea remained lost in her thoughts, probably pondering everything they had just talked about.
"It’s ready."
As Soren whispered and prepared to serve, she finally broke the silence.
’Soren... what else did you see when you looked?’ she asked, her tone carrying a mix of vulnerability and genuine curiosity.
Soren expected the question.
He had already decided to be upfront about the practical details, but he carefully filtered out the unique metrics provided by his Investment Authority.
He had no intention of mentioning that he could read her exact mental state, gauge her hidden potential, or view her investment value.
At least not yet.
The risk was too great now.
It’s not that he didn’t trust her; it’s just that he completely distrusted the forces acting from the shadows.
There were people out there who could easily pry into minds, peel back secrets through strange abilities, or even extract memories through sheer force.
Keeping the deepest details to himself was the only way to ensure both of their safety.

’I could see your basic info, detailed physical condition, your current mana capacity, and your affinities,’ Soren replied calmly, keeping his explanation grounded. ’I also saw your abilities, the curse, and something called Authority.
And I was actually going to talk about this all with you.’
Ethea seemed to digest this, processing the scope of what he could do.
Before she could dwell on it further, Soren decided to voice a question that had been lingering in the back of his mind for a long time.
’Ethea,’ he asked, his tone shifting to one of genuine curiosity. ’Do you know what an Authority is?
And... do you have any idea why yours is ’dormant’?’
’...An Authority?’ Ethea repeated, a brief flicker of surprise passing through her eyes before she caught herself. ’Oh, right.
You wouldn’t know about that yet.’
She paused, organizing her thoughts to explain a concept that few in the world ever had the privilege to learn.
’An Authority is a mystical power born from a direct comprehension of the fundamental laws of the world.
It isn’t just standard magic; it’s more of a conceptual command over reality itself.
For example, a regular cultivator might cast a spell to create and control fire, but someone with an Authority over flames doesn’t need a spell.
They simply dictate the concept of heat and combustion, bypassing the natural order entirely.
And...’
Her tone turned solemn as she continued.
’To even stand a chance at reaching the pinnacle, becoming a ninth-circle master, one must learn and master an Authority.’

chapters.title: Chapter 208: What is An Authority? [2]
paragraphs: ’That’s the requirement to reach the 9th Circle?’

’Mm, and this is exactly why Paragons are regarded as myths,’ Ethea explained, a faint sigh slipping past her lips. ’An Authority is an incredibly powerful force, but it is equally difficult to master. It requires a level of enlightenment and comprehension that most cultivators fail to reach in a lifetime. As for why mine shows up as dormant...’
A trace of bitter irony appeared in her voice.

’It is obviously because I haven’t actually mastered it. I only managed to catch a faint glimpse of it due to a fortuitous encounter in the past. It left a seed behind, but without proper training and comprehension, it remains out of my reach.’
Soren nodded inwardly while plating the food, carefully transferring the freshly prepared meal onto the dishes.
’Then... an Authority can’t be innate, right? One has to actively achieve it?’

’...It could be,’ Ethea answered after a brief moment of pondering. ’After all, the universe is vast and contains countless worlds, so it is entirely possible that some extraordinary individuals are born with such power running through their veins. There might be bloodlines or unique souls that naturally inherit these concepts from birth. However, for ordinary cultivators like us, obtaining one through enlightenment is the only viable path.’
Soren fell silent, his mind racing.
Was he... one of those extraordinary individuals then?

He couldn’t know for certain whether the power had been woven into his soul from birth, but the fact remained that he had awakened it during his awakening. That alone heavily implied it was an innate power, a fundamental piece of who he was.
Yet, a lingering doubt tugged at his thoughts.
The timing, the nature, the difference...
Was it truly just his own birthright, or was it really connected to Ethea in some strange, inexplicable way?

And it certainly didn’t operate like the example Ethea had mentioned just now; his power didn’t command elements like fire or ice, but instead functioned through a completely different system of actions and returns.
So... what exactly was it?
Was it a rare type of Authority?
What law governed something as abstract as investment, risk, and return?
Was there a cosmic law of causality that rewarded genuine intent and calculated sacrifice?
Soren couldn’t shake the feeling that his power operated on a scale that completely bypassed standard magical logic.

Were there even specific types or classifications to these forces? Did they possess grades, similar to how monsters or cultivation ranks were divided, or did an Authority exist entirely outside of traditional tier systems?

Realizing he had no answers and that speculating blindly would get him nowhere, he decided to gather whatever scraps of information he could. Thankfully, he had someone who might give some answers right beside him.
’Ethea, could you tell me more about them?’

’Of course, but let me think for a moment,’ she paused, organizing her thoughts to explain a concept that few in the world ever had the privilege to even whisper about. ’From what little I gathered, there are many different Authorities out there. They are all mostly distinct from one another, varying wildly in their applications, their restrictions, and how they manifest.’
’I see.’

’For example... You should know the famous Paragon of the Hollow Flame. I once heard that her Authority allows her to manipulate a specialized form of conceptual fire that burns away the very life force of her targets, rather than just their physical bodies. It even grants her rule over any flame-attributed creatures weaker than herself, forcing them to obey her command without question.’
’So powerful?’ Soren barely stopped himself from showing obvious shock.
’That’s right, and that is just one known application of such a power,’ Ethea explained, a look of deep reverence flashing across her features.

Soren took a moment to process the sheer scale of it before a sudden realization struck him. ’Then... what about the Authority you were trying to comprehend? If I had to guess, it is ice-related and should be similar to hers. Right?’

’...Mmm, it is,’ Ethea acknowledged, her focus turning inward as she recalled that fleeting glimpse from her past. ’And if my understanding is correct, once mastered fully, it would allow one to even freeze time and space.’
Soren fell silent again, his mind entirely blank for a second as he repeated her last words in his head.
’Freeze time and space?!’
Wasn’t that just too powerful? To completely halt the fabric of reality itself sounded like a power that should not even exist.

Detecting his shock, Ethea offered a faint smile. ’It is incredible, but of course, it wouldn’t be for an unlimited duration. There will always be limits, massive mana costs, and perhaps severe consequences for pushing those boundaries.’
’Ah, you’re right,’ Soren replied, nodding as the sheer scale of the concept began to settle in his mind.

He fell back into his thoughts, his focus shifting naturally to his own Investment Authority. He already knew a few of its operational limits and the strict conditions it required, but what about the consequences? Could it even be pushed to its absolute limits, and if so, what would the ultimate return look like?
’...I’ll find out about it in the future,’ he thought to himself, deciding to shelve the questions for now.

"Alright, let’s prepare the table and eat lunch," Soren said out loud, giving her a reassuring look before adding mentally through their bond, ’You can continue speaking. I’ll set everything up while listening.’
’...Soren.’
’What is it?’

’Unfortunately, I only know this much about Authorities. And I cannot even be entirely sure if they are even accurate. Moreover, there is no information available about them, so I cannot give you any more concrete details,’ Ethea communicated back through the bond, her thoughts carrying a distinct note of finality as she watched him arrange the dishes. ’However, if you are really curious, you can ask Teacher Hector; he probably knows more than me, considering his age and experience.’
’Right, I almost forgot about him. And now that I think about it... He had worked with Paragons before too.’
’That’s right. He was even close friends with one. If you want, I will ask him myself later.’
’Oh, that would be great. Thank you, Ethea!’

chapters.title: Chapter 209: Mapping the Future [1]
paragraphs: Soren decided to continue their secret talking later. To avoid making Ethea feel awkward, he just focused on feeding her, keeping things casual.
"How is it? Tasty?"

Ethea chewed thoughtfully, a genuine smile replacing her previous pensive expression as she nodded in appreciation. The savory flavor seemed to instantly bring a bit of color back to her pale complexion.
"It’s amazing. Is this one of those special meals too?"
"It has its benefits, but the one I made for breakfast was the real masterpiece. Have you felt any changes from it yet?"

He didn’t know how fast the effects would show themselves. Even though he had eaten some himself, he wasn’t the one who was injured, so asking the patient directly was the only real way to gauge its success.
Ethea swallowed, considering it for a moment. "...The pain has subsided a bit. But what exactly was its intended effect?"
"That’s good. As you said, it was meant to ease the pain," Soren answered casually.
’Its main effects are to soothe internal burning and heal your damaged pathways,’ he added mentally.
Ethea looked into his eyes, her gaze softening. ’I see. Thank you. I really appreciate it.’
’It’s worth it as long as you can get better.’ Soren smiled and waited until she finished another bite before asking his next question. "Ethea, where do you want to go after we leave here?"
Ethea raised a brow faintly, caught off guard by the sudden shift in topic. "...It doesn’t really matter to me. What about you?
"Actually, I haven’t given it much thought yet," Soren admitted, blowing on the spoon. "I was planning to discuss it with you soon."
"Oh, then, let’s discuss it now." A curious smile appeared on her face. "What’s on your mind?"

"Ideally, I’d like to find a quiet, peaceful place where no one would disturb us," Soren said, a faint longing smile touching his lips as he fed her another bite. "But I know that’s not an option right now. We have to prioritize our safety."

He set the spoon down for a moment, his expression turning serious. "First off, we can’t stay in places like Kalmira anymore. I don’t want a repeat of what happened the other day, and smaller cities just don’t offer the protection we need; we might even end up implicating more innocent people. That’s why I think we should look for a major hub, somewhere with the highest level of security, guarded by powerful figures. Ideally, a place backed by a Paragon would be great."
’A place where your enemies wouldn’t dare to act, or would at least hesitate to try anything,’ he added silently, his gaze locking onto hers to convey the depth of his concern.

Ethea nodded in agreement, though a faint shadow of worry crossed her features. "You’re right, but unfortunately, there are only a handful of places like that in the entire world. Gaining entry to them is incredibly difficult, and staying there is definitely not free."
"Right," Soren said, shifting the bowl slightly. "And the most straightforward option would be returning to the capital, with or without your father."

The capital city, Valorium, was one of the most prominent S-rank hubs on the continent. As the heart of the Grand Kingdom of Oros, it boasted unmatched security, largely because the King himself was an 8th Circle awakened who resided within its walls. Under normal circumstances, it would be the perfect haven, especially given Ethea’s high prestige and status there.

But considering how powerful her enemies were and Ethea’s current state, they couldn’t be certain how they would be treated. The human heart was fickle, and respect was often tied entirely to a person’s strength.

Ethea seemed to reach a similar conclusion. Her expression hardened a fraction before she looked back up at him. "Let’s keep it as a backup option for now. We shouldn’t rule it out entirely, but we should see if we have better choices first."

Soren nodded, placing his spoon back in the bowl and picking up the cup. "I actually looked into a few places myself, but you obviously know the world far better than I do. How about I share what I have in mind first, and then you can give me your thoughts and suggestions?"
Ethea agreed with a slight nod, letting him guide the cup so she could gulp the tea he held to her lips.

"The first place that came to my mind is the Timur Empire," Soren began as he put down the cup. "As one of the largest and most powerful nations on the continent, it boasts an incredible concentration of high-ranking awakened and unmatched military might. On top of that, it houses Etenia Academy, the best institution on the continent."
He paused for a moment to let her swallow. "Since you studied there, you must be pretty familiar with the environment, right?"
"I am," Ethea confirmed quietly. "I spent a good amount of time there."
Soren nodded.

Ethea had been exceptionally famous throughout the empire back then, which meant people would recognize her name, but more importantly, since she had spent years living there, she would have a deep understanding of the region’s layout and politics. That knowledge would make it much easier for them to navigate the area safely.

"Plus," Soren continued, leaning forward slightly, "the empire was founded by the Paragon of Order himself. He’s one of the legendary myths who protected the world during the apocalypse, and he was actually one of the very first cultivators to ascend to the ninth circle."
"Mmm." Ethea nodded slowly, a look of deep recollection entering her eyes. "I’ve actually met him a few times during my time in the empire as well."
"Oh! Can you tell me about it?" Soren asked, his curiosity piqued instantly.

Ethea paused for a moment, visualizing the legendary figure. "The Paragon of Order is exactly as the stories describe. He is majestic and powerful, possessing an aura that commands respect without him ever needing to say a single word. Despite his status, he carries himself with a profound sense of calm, speaking openly and normally with anyone who approaches him rather than hiding behind a wall of arrogance."

chapters.title: Chapter 210: Mapping the Future [2]
paragraphs: "There is also a genuine gentleness to his demeanor, a kindness that makes you forget you are standing before a living myth. But above all else, he values true justice. He treats the common citizens and high nobles with the exact same fairness, which is why the people love him so much."
"He sounds like a genuinely great man," Soren said, a note of sincere admiration in his voice. "It’s rare for someone with that kind of power to remain humble."

"He truly is," Ethea agreed, her gaze drifting back to the cup in his hands as she recalled the scale of the Paragon’s responsibilities. "It is honestly remarkable how he remains deeply connected to his people despite everything on his plate. He actually stepped down from the throne long ago, leaving the daily administration and politics to the current ruling Emperor so he could focus entirely on the greater threats menacing our continent and the world. Yet despite facing dangers of that scale, he still makes it a point to attend important national events. He even visits Etenia Academy once or twice a year just to encourage the students and check on the next generation."

Ethea paused for a brief moment, her expression turning slightly more pragmatic. "But as great as he is, we have to keep in mind that he isn’t always present in the empire. Unless a true crisis emerges that threatens the nation or the world at large, he generally won’t interfere in smaller conflicts. Even so, it still remains one of our best options."
A soft smile finally broke through her serious demeanor. "In fact, if we choose to head there, we could even go and visit your sister."
Soren felt a sudden pang in his chest at the mention of his sibling, but he quickly masked it. "You’re right. We could."

As for the promise he had made to his father about staying away from her, he didn’t give a damn anymore. The moment they had cast him aside, he was no longer a Valmere. They couldn’t dictate his choices anymore. But of course, he still had to be cautious.
’...Even if we don’t choose the Temur Empire, I still want to check on her eventually and ensure she is safe.’

Pushing the thought to the back of his mind, he cleared his throat to focus back on the topic. "I also looked into the Allied Realms Alliance as a third option, considering their collective strength rivals that of Oros and the other grand kingdoms. However, I quickly ruled it out. Because the alliance is fragmented into dozens of smaller kingdoms, the internal politics are messy, and the security structure is far too decentralized.
"I agree with you," Ethea said simply. "It would put them in danger too."

"Alright," Soren nodded, picking up the spoon again. "There is also the Zenith Empire, but it lies on the exact opposite end of the continent. Moreover, the entire region is far too turbulent, and despite their immense strength, they maintain a highly hostile relationship with several nations, including Temur and Oros. And... Even though wars are technically forbidden by international law, the constant border friction and espionage make it a powder keg. On top of all these, the current ruler is the worst tyrant in recent history, so I ruled it out as well."
Ethea let out a derisive breath. "You made the right call avoiding that place. Because I utterly despise that scumbag."
Soren offered a faint smile, knowing full well why the tyrant rubbed her the wrong way.
The man held the official title of Sovereign of Love, but behind closed doors, people truthfully called him the Sovereign of Lust.

He was notoriously lecherous, treacherous, and completely lacking in moral restraint. While polygamy was widely accepted as normal in the current era, the Zenith Emperor had crossed every reasonable boundary, boasting a harem of more than a thousand wives and consorts.

Worse still were the countless rumors regarding his questionable methods of acquiring them, often forcing noble houses and weaker territories to hand over their daughters to appease his endless desires.

And those were just the mildest rumors. The reality behind them was likely far more sickening, which was more than enough reason to stay as far away from the Zenith Empire as possible. Soren also shared her disgust because a man who abused his power to treat women like property was even worse than a monster in his eyes.
’Hm?’
Noticing the mood in the room was worsening at the mere mention of the tyrant, he quickly decided to change the subject. "The last place on our continent I thought of was none other than the URF.
Ethea blinked in confusion, her irritation momentarily forgotten. "You mean the United Races Federation?"
"Yes," Soren replied, feeding her another small spoonful of the warm meal.
"But... They are not even native to Etenia," Ethea pointed out, her tone laced with caution. "Historically, they were invaders."
Soren nodded in understanding.

Under normal circumstances, the Federation would never cross his mind either. It was a massive coalition composed of entirely different species who had originally arrived from separate worlds. Some had come across the dimensional rifts centuries ago seeking a desperate refuge from their own dying realms, while others had crossed over with nothing but conquest and bloody war on their minds.

In fact, their arrival had triggered the War of Convergence, one of the bloodiest conflicts in history. The brutal war ultimately ended with neither side claiming victory, cut short by a sudden catastrophic event that forced both sides to join hands just to survive.

Because of their vital cooperation during the crisis, the federation races were finally accepted into Etenia, and following decades of shifting borders and treaties, they ended up permanently inhabiting a fifth of Meldur, carving out a massive territory on the continent.

More than a century had passed since those dark times. While the federation races were still not fully embraced by the human kingdoms, relations had steadily improved. This was especially true after they stood alongside humanity to help the world survive that catastrophe and subsequent world-ending threats, proving their alliance when it mattered most.
Since then, their cooperation has driven significant advancements worldwide.

chapters.title: Chapter 211: Mapping The Future [3]
paragraphs: The best examples of this progress were the introduction of bonding techniques with magic beasts, the blending of diverse arcane styles, and a sudden leap forward in hybrid technology and weaponry.

Truthfully, the Federation would likely not have crossed Soren’s mind either if not for his recent encounter with Director Elenaria. That unexpected meeting, which made him recall his past, was the reason he was even considering their territory now.
"I thought you had no personal enmity with them," Soren remarked, shaking off his reverie. "Or do you think gaining entry into their borders will be too difficult?"

Ethea went quiet, considering the political and practical implications. Hiding in a place that operated completely outside human jurisdiction had undeniable merits, but it was not without risk. And there were some things she couldn’t share with Soren about them.

"Neither, really," she said, meeting his gaze. "While it is certainly a good option, I think we should treat the Federation strictly as a last resort. Their culture and laws are entirely different from ours, which makes blending in a massive challenge." She paused, tilting her head slightly. "Did you have any other ideas?"

Soren nodded, though his expression offered little optimism. "The only other place left on my list was the floating continent, Avolia. But even I know how nearly impossible it is just to get up there, let alone navigate their strict rules and isolationist restrictions."
Ethea nodded in agreement, opening her mouth to swallow another spoonful of the warm meal. They definitely couldn’t go to that place. Not in the near future.

"Unfortunately, those were all the places I could think of," Soren continued, a trace of fatigue touching his voice as he looked at the mostly empty bowl. "Aside from the basic geography they cram into our heads at school, my knowledge of the other continents is pretty limited. Do you have any suggestions?"
Ethea fell into deep thought, her gaze turning distant as she mechanically accepted another spoonful of the warm meal.

"A few places come to mind," she said softly after swallowing. "But there is one massive obstacle blocking all of them. Traveling to another continent right now is going to be incredibly difficult. While the continent of Xenis is relatively close and by far the easiest to reach, the others are a completely different story. Reaching Vraxius, Nemora, or Khorvath will be a nightmare. Even if we somehow manage to gain access to long-distance teleportation portals, the sheer distance makes it risky.
She paused, her expression darkening slightly.
"Taking a ship across the oceans is an option, but it is a deadly one."
Soren nodded in solemn understanding.

The mere mention of the deep waters sent a subtle chill through him. He knew the terrors of the oceans all too well; beneath those endless waves lay monstrous leviathans and unpredictable mana storms, making them perhaps the most perilous and untamed territories in the entire world. Traversing them without massive military escorts or specialized vessels was nothing short of a death sentence.

Furthermore, any hope of finding sanctuary along the coastlines or within the deep was entirely barred by geopolitics. Vast underwater kingdoms certainly existed beneath the surface, but those realms belonged entirely to aquatic magic beasts who guarded their territory fiercely.

While a baseline of diplomatic contact did exist between the deep-sea dwellers and surface civilizations, the relationship was nowhere near as developed as the public liked to imagine. In fact, humanity maintained far better ties with the foreign races of the United Races Federation, or even with the magic beasts roaming the dry land, than with the isolated rulers of the deep.

"There is also the option of traveling via airships," Ethea added, drawing his attention back to her. "But that route has its own walls. Intercontinental airships are extremely expensive to commission, and because of the dangers in the upper atmosphere, they are never allowed to sail without being guarded by at least a 7th Circle powerhouse or an equivalent security fleet."
Soren nodded in silent agreement. He knew the skies were every bit as treacherous as the deep waters, though the true peril lay in the absolute volatility of nature itself.

The upper atmosphere was plagued by violent storms, unpredictable weather patterns, and vast chaotic zones where mana fluctuated wildly. In those high altitudes, a sudden tempest could rip an unshielded vessel to pieces in seconds or leave it drifting helplessly into uncharted airspace.
Worse still, they risked getting caught in spatial storms that could tear reality open, dropping them directly into the oceans, a Forbidden Zone, or, worse, the barren wastes of the Dead Continent.
"In the end, it all comes down to strength, huh," Soren muttered, staring down at the empty bowl, the reality of their limitations pressing heavily against his chest.

Sensing the sudden shift in his demeanor, Ethea set her thoughts aside and looked directly at him. "Soren... Please, don’t blame yourself. We aren’t out of options yet. And frankly, you are looking at your own progress entirely the wrong way. Given how recently you actually awakened, the speed at which you are growing is already absurd."
She smiled encouragingly.
"If you keep this up, it won’t even take you long to surpass my speed. Stop measuring yourself against the rest of the world when you’ve barely just started."

Soren listened to Ethea as a small smile played on his lips. "You’re right. I shouldn’t be rushing into things and getting discouraged. There is still a long way to go to become truly strong, but I will get there eventually. Thank you for the reminder, Ethea."

"Don’t mention it," Ethea replied with a widening smile. "In fact, now that I think of it, there is a place where our needs could be met and where we would not have to worry about the threats from the world around us."
Soren blinked in surprise before asking curiously. "Where?"
Her expression turned profoundly serious, yet filled with an undeniable thrill.
"It’s... The Tower of Apocalypse."

chapters.title: Chapter 212: The Tower of Apocalypse
paragraphs: Soren repeated the name, his mind immediately searching his memories for everything related to it. He didn’t have to dig deep; the details were practically burned into the mind of every living soul.

The Tower of the Apocalypse was the true origin of their shattered reality. It was the first Gate to open on the planet, ending centuries of peace and starting a disaster that almost destroyed humanity. That’s why it earned its dark name.

It had also gained many aliases over the past two centuries, each reflecting how different factions viewed the monolithic nightmare. To scholars and researchers who dedicated their lives to studying the arcane, it was often called the Tower of Truth. They believed that hidden within its depths lay the ultimate answers regarding the origin of the apocalypse, true power, and even the secrets of the universe itself. Meanwhile, for cultivators, it went by the name Ascension Tower: a brutal testing ground promising unfathomable riches and the rare materials needed to surpass their limitations.

Yet, for the common folk and the weak who lived under its constant threat, those grand titles meant nothing. For them, it was just called the Black Tower, the Tower of Death, or Calamity. These names reflected the many lives it had taken since it appeared, a dark legacy that became more burdensome with each year.
And the structure fully lived up to its fearsome reputation.

As the world’s very first 9th Circle Gate, the survival rate inside was naturally notorious for being brutal. This reputation was forged during the early decades of the apocalypse, when entering the structure was widely regarded as an automatic death sentence. Back then, rumors claimed that barely one out of a thousand challengers ever managed to make it out alive. Over the last two centuries, however, the situation had steadily improved. Thanks to modern advancements, rigorous safety protocols, and the constant regulatory oversight of the International Awakened Bureau, those catastrophic odds had dropped to about two in ten.

It was still a terrifying gamble, but Soren finally understood why Ethea had brought it up. The place really did suit their situation perfectly. The moment they stepped across the threshold, they would be completely cut off from the rest of the world. Because the Tower operated as an entirely independent dimension, no outside threat could ever reach them there. That isolation would leave them with only two things to focus on: surviving the trials and gaining the strength to climb higher.
"You’re right," Soren said, as the realization sank in. "This truly appears to be the best option. Honestly, why didn’t I consider it earlier?"
Ethea offered a faint smile before adding, "And entering it won’t be a problem, either. I have a way to get us inside safely."
"That’s great," Soren responded, experiencing a short moment of relief.

However, his optimism faded rapidly when a major flaw in the plan became clear to him. He fell silent, his face darkening with concern. While he was willing to risk himself, he couldn’t ignore Ethea’s situation.

He knew he could take care of himself in a fight, but what about her? If they stepped through that gate, how would the Tower handle them? Could they challenge it as a party, or would it forcefully separate them upon entry? If it did, her chances of survival would drop to zero almost instantly.

Unable to shake the sudden anxiety, he voiced his concerns directly. "Can we actually enter the Tower together without getting separated? Because if there is even a slight chance it forces us apart, I won’t agree to this option."
"Yes, it’s possible to enter together, but the difficulty will increase tremendously because of it..."
As she spoke, a harsh truth became clear to her. She understood that if they proceeded, Soren would have to carry the entire burden, while she would simply be a dead weight pulling him down.
Yet Soren’s eyes suddenly lit up. "You mean we really can stay together?"

Ethea blinked, caught off guard by the sudden spark of hope in his voice. Realizing the dangerous direction his thoughts were taking, she gave a hurried nod and tried to backpedal. "Soren, let’s just drop this idea. At the very least... we should wait until I get better."

Soren nodded, noticing her emotional fluctuation. He didn’t press the matter further to keep from upsetting her, but his mind was already made up. Despite her warnings, he knew their reality had not changed: the Tower remained their single best shot at survival, and he was already resolving himself to take it.
’I should convince her before we leave.’
"You’re right," he said, shifting his tone to sound as casual as possible. "Besides, we still have time to think about it."
He stood up and began clearing the dishes from the table, stacking the bowls to break the lingering tension. "By the way, what do you want to do next? Do you want to watch a movie, or...?
’I need to cultivate,’ Ethea replied, but out loud, she simply said, "I think I’ll just rest."
"Alright, I’ll finish up here quickly and take you to the bedroom," Soren said, picking up the dishes.
Ethea looked up at him. "Mm. But what are you going to do?"
"Ah, me?" Soren paused, glancing at his phone. "I just received a message from Ryan. I actually had a meeting planned with him today and almost forgot about it."
"Oh, I see," she said, her eyes following him as he moved toward the sink. "Then are you going to leave?"
"Huh? No, of course not. I’ll just call him here," Soren replied, turning back to offer a reassuring nod. "So you can just relax and rest. We can continue the discussion later."

"That’s good," Ethea replied, a small wave of relief easing her tension. She leaned back slightly, her expression softening. "I’ll think about a few more options while you’re busy, just in case we can find a safer alternative."
"Ok, I’ll trust you with that then."
Soren smiled and soon finished washing the dishes and storing the rest of the food in the boundless ring.
Then, he walked over and started wheeling her toward the bedroom, humming softly as he pushed the wheelchair.
’Let’s talk about your condition and the curse later too.’
