paragraphs: "Come on, take a seat," Soren said, gesturing toward the sofa.
"Oh, o-ok," Ryan stammered, clearing his throat before carefully sitting down.

’Even after seeing the grand scale of the Sunless Reliquary, he still reacted like this. I guess he’s still a kid at heart,’ Soren chuckled inwardly, noticing Ryan’s eyes darting around the room. Then again, looking back, Soren knew he hadn’t been that different.
"Brother Soren, have you really recovered completely?" Ryan asked, breaking the silence. "And what about sister-in-law?"

"I’m indeed better," Soren replied with a reassuring nod. "Ethea is resting in the other room right now, but she’s doing fine too. What about you? How are you holding up? We didn’t really get a chance to catch up yesterday."
"I’m doing well. And I already took care of that matter you mentioned. Is that why you wanted to meet up today?"
"Oh, that’s good. Good job on that," Soren said, leaning forward. "But no, I actually called you because there’s something important we need to discuss."
Ryan raised an eyebrow, his curiosity piqued. He shifted in his seat, settling comfortably to listen.
"Ryan..." Soren took a brief breath before laying it out straight. "We’re leaving Kalmira City soon."
"We... as in you and sister-in-law?" Ryan asked, his brow furrowing with doubt.
Soren gave a confirmatory nod.
"Could it be..." Ryan paused for a moment before making another guess. "Does this have something to do with the Gate incident?"
Soren nodded again, his expression turning solemn. "What I am about to tell you is a secret, Ryan. I hope you can keep it between us."
"Of course, I won’t tell anyone without your permission." Ryan nodded immediately, his posture stiffening as his mind began to race with the implications.

"The truth is... That Gate didn’t manifest naturally," Soren started, keeping his voice low. "Some people artificially forced it open, and those people are Ethea’s enemies who’ve been hunting her down. Even the incident that left her crippled in the first place was their doing."

Ryan opened his mouth to speak, but the words caught in his throat. He closed it, his eyes squinting as he tried to grasp the scale of the threat. After a long moment of silence, he looked up, his voice hushed. "...How powerful are they?"
"At least the Eighth Circle," Soren said grimly. "And there are probably a dozen of them."
"I see..." Ryan muttered, his gaze dropping back to the floor as he fell into deep thought.

Watching him, Soren could easily guess what was running through the kid’s mind. Ryan was likely agonizing over whether he even had a place in a conflict of this scale or how someone at his level could possibly offer any support.
Soren’s intuition proved exactly right. A moment later, Ryan raised his head, looking Soren dead in the eye. "Brother Soren, is there any way I can help you guys?"

"Thank you, Ryan. I appreciate that more than you know," Soren said, his expression softening slightly. "But before we get into any of that, there’s something I need to ask you first. It might be a bit personal."
Ryan nodded without a second thought, leaning forward to show he didn’t mind.
"What are your plans for the future?" Soren asked. "What are you aiming for next?"

Ryan hesitated, looking down at his hands as he formulated the words. "Actually... I was planning to apply for a transfer to the Etenia Academy once this semester ends. I even planned to take my family with me. My parents said they would think about it, but only if I actually pass the transfer exams."
Soren watched him closely, noticing the lingering weight in the boy’s posture. "...But?

"But the Gate incident changed my mind," Ryan muttered, his voice dropping as his grip tightened on his knees. "It made me realize just how weak I really am. I know everyone says I’m now a genius, and I’ve been progressing rapidly over the last couple of weeks, but to me, it still feels agonizingly slow. Because... Knowing what awaits me in the future, I just don’t have the luxury of time."
He looked up at Soren, a sudden wave of raw frustration breaking through his usual quiet demeanor.

"Etenia is an excellent place, and I believe I would learn a lot and enjoy my time there. However, it’s still a school that requires years to complete. I feel like I’m wasting my days at my current academy, and transferring might only lead to more of the same. That’s why I’ve begun exploring other options. I’ve even considered dropping out altogether to become a full-time hunter."

"But I know my parents would never agree to that," Ryan added, his shoulders slumping as the frustration gave way to reality. "And I don’t blame them either. They just want me to be safe and enjoy my life. They want me to be happy. Honestly, I’d love nothing more than to just do that, but it feels impossible now. And... If something dangerous happens like the other day, I’m terrified I won’t be able to protect them. That’s actually why I wanted to talk to you, but couldn’t find the chance till now. Brother Soren... I need your help... and your advice on what I should do."
Hearing him, Soren fell silent.

He looked at the boy sitting across from him, the weight of a hidden truth pressing heavily on his mind. Just like him, Ryan was also frustrated by his current pace, but he had no idea what truly lay ahead of him. Ethea’s enemies were terrifying, yes, but Ryan was bound to face an even worse storm. Considering how unfathomable the Sunless Emperor was, and factoring in Ryan’s unique Two-Faced Fortune ability, the hardships waiting for him in the future would likely dwarf anything they were dealing with now.
Moreover, it was an incredibly heavy burden for a kid to carry, and it was also unfair. Yet, the moment Ryan became the successor to the Sunless Emperor, this reality became his inescapable fate.
Soren then recalled the solemn promise he had made to the Sunless Emperor, a vow to help and guide this boy through the shadows ahead. It was a duty he had no intention of breaking.
"Ryan..."

chapters.title: Chapter 214: Mapping The Future [5]
paragraphs: "Ryan, I understand exactly what you’re going through," Soren started, his tone calm yet serious. "In fact, I’m in a similar position myself and have already experienced the terror firsthand. Honestly, I barely made it out alive. If it wasn’t for outside help, I would already be dead, and Ethea would be gone."
He looked directly at Ryan, letting the brutal truth hang in the air for a moment.

"I hope you never have to experience that kind of helplessness. But we both know how indifferent reality is to what we want. I’m not going to sit here and give you false hope or spin some fake comfort just to make you feel better. The truth is, we can’t afford to be caught off guard. We have to be as ready as possible for the absolute worst." Soren leaned back slightly, crossing his arms. "Before I give you my advice, though, I need to know one thing. How much time do you think you have left before things get critical?"
Ryan shifted uneasily, calculating the timeline in his head. "I’m not entirely sure... but if I had to guess, I’d say I have about five or six years."

"That’s a decent amount of time," Soren muttered, though the line of his jaw remained tight. He took a slow breath, thinking. "Five or six years gives us some room to work with. Originally, I had two suggestions in mind for you. But after hearing your situation and the fact that you have a few years to build a foundation, a third option has opened up. Do you want to hear them?"
Ryan’s eyes instantly lit up, his posture straightening as he gave a sharp nod.

"The first option," Soren said, raising a finger, "is to actually go through with what you’ve been considering: drop out of the academy entirely. You could register as an independent hunter, join a party, find a reputable guild, or even join the Bureau. It means throwing yourself completely into the hunter lifestyle. It’s high-risk, it’s brutal, and your parents will definitely hate it, but real combat is the fastest catalyst for growth. You’d be forcing yourself into constant life-and-death situations, which is exactly what triggers rapid adaptation."

"Furthermore," Soren added, "if you choose this path, I’ll leave the management of the Monolith entirely to you. That way, you will continue to cultivate faster, and it’ll keep providing you with a very nice passive income to support your family. Then, once I’ve taken care of my own problems out there, I’ll return. We can team up, face whatever threats come your way together, and make sure both of our families stay protected."
Ryan listened intently, evaluating the proposal, before gesturing for Soren to continue to the next one.

"The second suggestion is actually one I just came up with right now. It’s going ahead with the transfer to Etenia Academy. In fact, if you choose this, I’ll personally help you with it." He paused, letting the contrast sink in. "But once again, we would utilize the Monolith to your advantage, and you would enter that academy with a completely different mindset. Instead of treating it like a standard school path, you treat it purely as a resource and learning hub. You utilize their high-tier library, their secure training facilities, and their elite networks to grow as fast as possible, while completely ignoring the typical social or academic distractions. It provides your parents with the peace of mind they seek, while enabling you to access all the benefits the academy offers."

Soren hesitated before adding, "And honestly, I also have a selfish reason for suggesting this. My sister was supposed to enroll there, and perhaps she is already accepted. So, I thought... well, I was hoping you could help me look out for her."
He realized his mistake and chuckled self-deprecatingly. "I must sound pretty ridiculous right now. Here I am giving you life advice, yet I’m already turning it into a favor for myself. Sorry-"

"No, it’s okay." Ryan waved his hand to dismiss the apology. "It’s the least I could do after everything. Besides, keeping an eye on her wouldn’t be an issue at all. But..." He paused, clearly showing anticipation on his face. "What about the third option?"
"The third option is..." Soren’s expression grew entirely serious, the lightheartedness from a moment ago vanishing completely. "You just have to come with us."
Ryan blinked, caught off guard.

"However, you need to know what you’d be signing up for," Soren continued, his gaze locked onto the younger man. "Our destination isn’t certain yet, and we are guaranteed to face extreme danger, likely far worse than the Seventh Circle Gate from the other day. We will be stepping onto a path where one wrong move could mean the end for any of us."
"If you want, you can also bring your family along, but there is a very real chance they could get swept up in the crossfire and get injured or even worse... perish."
"..." Ryan’s gaze turned ice-cold, and he looked down, his fists clenching so hard his shoulders trembled at the word ’perish’.

"...If you’re willing to take these risks," Soren added softly, breaking the tension, "then you are more than welcome to join us. I will personally do everything in my power to ensure both your and your family’s safety. Furthermore, we will also travel, fight, and grow stronger together."
Ryan remained quiet, the inner storm still raging behind his stoic face.
"You don’t have to give me an answer right now," Soren continued. "Take your time to think it over. We won’t be leaving immediately, so you have until our departure to decide."

Soren leaned back, letting out a soft sigh. "And keep in mind, these three are just the paths I managed to come up with. They aren’t your only choices, and there might be far better options out there suited to your situation. So don’t feel boxed in by what I’ve suggested."

He gestured vaguely with his hand. "For instance, you could choose to step into the spotlight, reveal the true extent of your talent and powers, and draw the attention of the real powerhouses. An Emperor, a Sovereign, or if you’re extraordinarily lucky, even a Paragon could take notice and offer to make you their disciple. Under someone like that, your safety and growth would be guaranteed."
"In the end, the choice is entirely yours."

chapters.title: Chapter 215: Mapping The Future [6]
paragraphs: There was a reason why Soren didn’t bring up the idea of finding a new master first. He didn’t want to undermine Ryan’s bond with the Sunless Emperor. Even though the Emperor might be gone, that connection was still sacred, and Soren refused to disrespect it. He also believed Ryan would ultimately make the right decision himself.

As for why he was planning to leave the Monolith with Ryan if they parted ways, he wanted to test his upgraded Investment Authority. In fact, he had requested something from Ryan yesterday via phone, and since Ryan said he did it, he could test it right away tomorrow.
’Since I will go to the Bureau, I should prepare the compensation I promised as well.’
"Brother Soren," Ryan called out, "can you tell me where you might be going at least?"
"Sure," Soren nodded before explaining the options he discussed with Ethea not long ago.

"...I see." Ryan fell silent for a moment before looking up. "Brother Soren, if you are going to the Temur Empire, I think I will go with the Etenia Academy. And if you end up going back to the capital, I will just transfer to the Oros Royal Academy instead, or drop out and become a full-time hunter. Either way, we can still keep in touch and work together."
Ryan paused as he looked Soren dead in the eye.

"But if you choose the Tower of Apocalypse... then I’m definitely coming with you. Because the best environment to get stronger and prepare for the inevitable future is that place. I will also take my family with me. Even if the trials end up reaching the nightmare difficulties, I won’t back down. I will push through them, survive, and grow stronger."

"...I think I know why you were chosen, Ryan," Soren said, a faint smile breaking across his face. "Your resolve and will are really something else. Alright, whatever path we choose, we’re in it together."
Ryan smiled back, though his expression carried a subtle weight.

"Actually, I was told that the Tower, along with the other Ninth Circle Gates, holds the key to surviving and saving this world from extinction. And out of all of them, the Tower should be the easiest one to clear. I hadn’t considered it yet because I was recommended to at least reach the 5th circle."
Soren’s eyes lit up, the phrasing triggering an instant realization. ’It’s the Sunless Emperor!’

Ryan hadn’t named anyone directly, but there was only one person who could possess knowledge of that caliber, someone who experienced the catastrophic collapse of a world firsthand and possessed the immense wisdom to navigate it.
"Then we need to seriously consider it." Soren clasped his hands together.
Because the truth was simple.

Even if he managed to heal Ethea, protect her from her enemies, and survive, it would mean nothing if the world itself collapsed into ruin. There would be no point in securing a safe haven if there was nowhere left to stand.
"Mm." Ryan agreed. "I will also probe my parents tonight to see how they react to the idea of moving."
"Good, you do that," Soren said, nodding in approval. "And did you bring the list I asked for yesterday?"
Ryan nodded and quickly pulled out his phone. "...I sent the file over to you."

"That works too." Soren unlocked his phone, opened the messaging app, and downloaded the file Ryan had sent. He spent a few moments carefully reading through the contents, his eyes scanning the details before he looked back up at Ryan. "You did a good job on this. I have one more thing to ask, though. Can you bring them to the Bureau tomorrow after your lessons end?"
Ryan nodded, but curiosity flickered across his face. "Why bring them there?"

Soren offered a mysterious smile before laying out the reasoning behind his request, carefully framing the arrangement so Ryan understood the intent without exposing his real motives. "...But of course, you don’t have to force them if they aren’t interested."
Ryan gave Soren a slightly strange look before a light chuckle escaped him. "I’m sure they won’t refuse after getting an offer like that."
"Good, I’ll trust you with that then."
"Right. Leave it to me.
Soren set his phone face down on the table. "After that, let’s go shopping."
Ryan tilted his head, caught off guard by the sudden shift in topic. "S-Shopping?"
"We have to buy new gear and some artifacts," Soren explained, his tone relaxed. "Though we should probably stock up on clothes too while we’re at it."
"That’s a great idea." Ryan let out a short laugh, shaking his head. "Brother Soren, you’re really amazing. You are thinking of everything."
Soren chuckled softly, waving his hand. "You’ll understand once you get married yourself."
Ryan laughed, shaking his head. "I’m way too young for that, and honestly, I don’t have time to be thinking about love right now."
"Oh?" Soren raised his brows, a playful glint in his eyes. "What about that Emily girl from Team 7? I saw how your expression changed every single time her name came up back then."
Ryan’s eyes widened, his cheeks instantly flushing a bright pink as he frantically shook his hands. "N-No! You completely misunderstood! I-It’s really not like that!"
"Pfft—" Soren burst out laughing at the sheer panic on the younger man’s face. "Guess I hit the nail on the head, huh?"
Ryan frowned, a groan escaping him as he realized just how instantly he had given himself away. He quickly turned his face away from Soren, trying to hide the lingering heat on his cheeks.

After a few moments, he managed to recover his composure and turned back with a more grounded look. "Brother Soren... It’s true I used to admire her, maybe even had a crush on her before. But I’m over it by now. Looking back, I think it was probably just because she was the only person who didn’t treat me like trash and actually said a few nice words to me during our small encounters."

He shrugged, a bitter smile touching his lips. "When everyone else is looking down on you, the smallest bit of basic decency feels like a massive deal. But that was in the past. Right now, I’ve got way bigger things to worry about than a childhood crush."
"Mm, I get what you mean," Soren replied softly, his smile mellowing into something more sympathetic before he paused. "...Wait, childhood crush?"

"Actually, I was told that the Tower, along with the other Ninth Circle Gates, holds the key to surviving and saving this world from extinction.
And out of all of them, the Tower should be the easiest one to clear.
I hadn’t considered it yet because I was recommended to at least reach the 5th circle."
Soren’s eyes lit up, the phrasing triggering an instant realization. ’It’s the Sunless Emperor!’

Ryan hadn’t named anyone directly, but there was only one person who could possess knowledge of that caliber, someone who experienced the catastrophic collapse of a world firsthand and possessed the immense wisdom to navigate it.
"Then we need to seriously consider it." Soren clasped his hands together.
Because the truth was simple.
Even if he managed to heal Ethea, protect her from her enemies, and survive, it would mean nothing if the world itself collapsed into ruin.
There would be no point in securing a safe haven if there was nowhere left to stand.
"Mm." Ryan agreed.
"I will also probe my parents tonight to see how they react to the idea of moving."
"Good, you do that," Soren said, nodding in approval.
"And did you bring the list I asked for yesterday?"
Ryan nodded and quickly pulled out his phone.
"...I sent the file over to you."
"That works too." Soren unlocked his phone, opened the messaging app, and downloaded the file Ryan had sent.
He spent a few moments carefully reading through the contents, his eyes scanning the details before he looked back up at Ryan.
"You did a good job on this.
I have one more thing to ask, though.
Can you bring them to the Bureau tomorrow after your lessons end?"
Ryan nodded, but curiosity flickered across his face.
"Why bring them there?"
Soren offered a mysterious smile before laying out the reasoning behind his request, carefully framing the arrangement so Ryan understood the intent without exposing his real motives.
"...But of course, you don’t have to force them if they aren’t interested."
Ryan gave Soren a slightly strange look before a light chuckle escaped him.
"I’m sure they won’t refuse after getting an offer like that."
"Good, I’ll trust you with that then."
"Right.
Leave it to me.
Soren set his phone face down on the table.
"After that, let’s go shopping."
Ryan tilted his head, caught off guard by the sudden shift in topic.
"S-Shopping?"
"We have to buy new gear and some artifacts," Soren explained, his tone relaxed.
"Though we should probably stock up on clothes too while we’re at it."
"That’s a great idea." Ryan let out a short laugh, shaking his head.
"Brother Soren, you’re really amazing.
You are thinking of everything."
Soren chuckled softly, waving his hand.
"You’ll understand once you get married yourself."
Ryan laughed, shaking his head.
"I’m way too young for that, and honestly, I don’t have time to be thinking about love right now."
"Oh?" Soren raised his brows, a playful glint in his eyes.
"What about that Emily girl from Team 7?
I saw how your expression changed every single time her name came up back then."
Ryan’s eyes widened, his cheeks instantly flushing a bright pink as he frantically shook his hands.
"N-No!
You completely misunderstood!
I-It’s really not like that!"
"Pfft—" Soren burst out laughing at the sheer panic on the younger man’s face.
"Guess I hit the nail on the head, huh?"
Ryan frowned, a groan escaping him as he realized just how instantly he had given himself away.
He quickly turned his face away from Soren, trying to hide the lingering heat on his cheeks.
After a few moments, he managed to recover his composure and turned back with a more grounded look.
"Brother Soren...
It’s true I used to admire her, maybe even had a crush on her before.
But I’m over it by now.
Looking back, I think it was probably just because she was the only person who didn’t treat me like trash and actually said a few nice words to me during our small encounters."
He shrugged, a bitter smile touching his lips.
"When everyone else is looking down on you, the smallest bit of basic decency feels like a massive deal.
But that was in the past.
Right now, I’ve got way bigger things to worry about than a childhood crush."
"Mm, I get what you mean," Soren replied softly, his smile mellowing into something more sympathetic before he paused.
"...Wait, childhood crush?"

chapters.title: Chapter 215 Unseen Potential
paragraphs: "...Just how long have you had this ’crush’?"
"..." Ryan froze as the bitter smile vanished from his face, realizing the trap he had walked into. "Brother Soren... that isnotthe main point of what I just said."
"It’s the most interesting point," Soren replied with an insufferable smirk. "Come on. You said ’childhood.’ How far back are we talking here?"

Ryan rubbed the back of his neck, feeling his cheeks flush again. He glanced around nervously, avoiding Soren’s gaze, in a desperate attempt to find an escape before he finally gave up with a sigh of defeat.

"Since middle school," Ryan muttered, his voice barely above a whisper. "We went to the same academy back before we even awakened. She was already popular back then, and I was... well, nobody. After awakening, she became even more popular, while I... remained a nobody."
"I see..." Soren’s grin faded a little, but his eyes remained playful. "So... you’ve been carrying that torch for years."
"I haven’t been ’carrying a torch’!" Ryan protested quickly, throwing his hands up. "I told you, it was just a stupid kid’s admiration! Besides, we’re on completely different paths now."
"Well, paths can cross," Soren noted casually.
"Brother Soren, please," Ryan pleaded, looking completely exhausted by the teasing. "Can we go back to talking about the Bureau, the Tower, or literally anything else?"
Soren let out a chuckle, finally mercy-killing the topic. "Alright, alright. I’ll drop it for now. But once we finish gear shopping tomorrow, you’re buying drinks."
"Fine," Ryan groaned, though a small smile still flickered across his face. "I will even treat you to a meal, just don’t bring it up again, please. And, is there anything we need to cover for today?"

"No, that’s all for now." Soren shook his head, took out a neatly wrapped container, and slid it across the table to Ryan. "Here, today’s meal is on me. I made it a while ago, so it should still be warm. Make sure to share it with your family. It’s useful for ordinary people too, so there should be no problem with your little sister eating it."

"This..." Ryan paused, looking at the container in surprise before a warm expression crossed his face. Then, he reached out into his own storage ring and pulled out a container of his own, setting it down in front of Soren. "Actually, my mother made this for you in the morning after hearing you were in the hospital. She asked me to send her greetings and hope you recover quickly."
"You have a great mother," Soren chuckled softly. "Please, make sure to pass along my gratitude when you get back."
"I will," Ryan smiled brightly before standing up to leave.
Soren saw him off to the gate, waiting till he rode into a taxi, and headed back inside.
’...Gulp.’

His eyes naturally fell to the container on the table, and in an instant, a sudden urge to sneak a few of those dumplings right then and there swept over him. Thankfully, he managed to resist the temptation, because he knew it would taste even better when eating with Ethea later. Smiling, he put it in his inventory and headed to the bedroom.
Inside, he noticed Ethea ’sleeping’ peacefully on the bed. Not wanting to disturb her, he stepped back outside, found a spacious corner, and spread out a big mattress.

Then, he summoned the massive stash of items he received from his father-in-law on top of it. And, for the next thirty minutes, he painstakingly inspected each of them one by one. To ensure nothing was wrong with them or to see if any item had hidden potential, he didn’t forget to secretly use Advanced Appraisal on every single one of them.
When he finally finished, Soren looked over his handiwork with genuine satisfaction.

Ethea’s words proved completely true—Darius really was capable of immense benevolence when he chose to be. Among the haul sat five distinct A-rank artifacts: one powerful offensive piece alongside four high-grade defensive ones. Beside them rested a collection of rare, high-ranking consumable treasures and elite potions, accompanied by two separate storage rings packed to the brim with mana crystals. Best of all, his appraisal confirmed there were no hidden curses or trackers attached to any of it.
"I should sell a few of these tomorrow," Soren muttered under his breath, neatly categorizing the gear before storing it away into separate inventory slots.

With that out of the way, he spent another twenty minutes putting together the compensation he had promised for the incident. He sorted through his funds and resources, setting aside generous monetary compensation for the families of those who had lost their lives, while preparing high-grade healing potions and financial support for those who were injured.
As for the hunters who were critically injured... he held back on their payout, keeping a far more specialized plan in mind for their recovery.

With everything sorted and accounted for, Soren finally rose, stretching his stiff limbs as he let out a long sigh. Feeling pleased with a productive afternoon start, he quietly headed back toward the bedroom.

Making no sound, he pulled out another mattress and set it down quietly beside the bed. Crossing his legs as he sat, he closed his eyes. Instead of beginning his usual cultivation routine, however, he mentally summoned his interface.
’Status, open.’
[PERSONAL INFORMATION]
Name: Soren Everly
Age: 23
Rank: Third Circle (Early Stage)
Mental Cultivation: Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture — Stage 1: Intent Foundation
Potential: ???
Hunter Rank: E
[CORE STATUS]
Mana Capacity: 63,580 / 160,000
Mental Power Capacity: 30740 / 50000
Core Stability: Stable (Recovering)
Pathway Integrity: Recovering (87%)
Affinity: Ice (Grade 7 - S Rank) | Wind (Grade 5 - B Rank) | Darkness (Sealed) | ??? | ???
[ABILITIES]
• Hyper-Recovery (A-Rank)
• Everfrost Tyrant Body (A-Rank)
• Sovereign’s Fortitude (S-Rank)
• Cold Resistance (D-Rank)
• Adrenaline Burst (A-Rank)
• Indomitable Soul (S-Rank)
• Intimidation (C-Rank)
• Fire Resistance (C-Rank)
• Life Force Resonance (B-Rank)
• Core Purge (A-Rank)
[SPECIAL ABILITIES]
• Soul-Binding Symbiosis
• Guardian’s Resolve
• Amplification
[TECHNIQUES & SKILLS]
• Glacial Emperor Scripture (Foundation Stage)
- First Star: Frost Palm Strike (100% Mastery)
- Second Star: Winter’s Barrier (100% Mastery)
• Glacial Edge Spear Arts
- First Form: Frost Piercing Thrust (100% Mastery)
- Second Form: Glacial Sweep (100% Mastery)
- Third Form: Glacial Descent (97% Mastery)
• Heaven-Treading Flash
- Quick Step (100% Mastery)
• Cooking Mastery (Intermediate Lv. 10)*
• Pathfinder
• Perceptive Eye (D-Rank)
• Binding Threads (C-Rank)
[EQUIPMENT]
• Tether Bond (Bound to: Ethea Everly)
• Hunter’s License (Standard - Grade E)
• Ring Of Boundless Void
[INVENTORY]
[CREDITS]
[INVESTMENTS]
’Let’s see what changed after the upgrade,’ he thought, scanning his newly formatted interface.

His eyes swept over the additions, immediately noting the newly unlocked Mental Cultivation category displaying the Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture. But his gaze paused at the line directly below it.
[Potential: ???]
A single eyebrow twitched. ’Question marks again?’

Though a faint flicker of curiosity rose in his mind, he quickly brushed it off. He was practically used to the authority hiding everything like that by now. Shifting his attention downward, his eyes locked onto the Mental Power Capacity line—and he froze.

Soren stared at the number, doing a double take. It was already well over thirty thousand. If he remembered correctly, Ethea’s mental power had hovered around fifteen thousand right after her breakthrough back then. Since he had acquired his mental cultivation through the returns from investing in her, his baseline capacity should have matched hers almost identically. Yet here he was, sitting at more than double her amount.
A heavy silence settled over the room as he processed the gap.

’It has to be from that battle against the curse,’ he realized, the memories of that brutal ordeal surfacing. There was really no other logical explanation. Surviving that nightmare had demanded everything from him, forcing him to execute the Imperial Forge method repeatedly under extreme pressure just to keep his mind intact. Pushing his mind to the limit over and over had clearly forged his mind into something far stronger in the process.
’I guess we can call it a blessing in disguise.’

Honestly, though, he never wanted to experience that kind of torture ever again. Surviving that mental meat grinder felt like nothing short of a miracle. And, looking back, he knew he couldn’t take all the credit — it was largely thanks to Soul-Binding Symbiosis, Guardian’s Resolve, and the grounding anchor of Ethea’s presence that he had managed to push through to the end without breaking.
With an internal sigh, he decided he would dedicate time today to thoroughly understand the mechanics of mental cultivation.
Setting that thought aside for the moment, he continued scanning down the list, only to freeze once more when his eyes landed on the Affinity line.
[Affinity: Ice (Grade 7 - S Rank) | Wind (Grade 5 - B Rank) | Darkness (Sealed) | ??? | ???]
’...So I had a darkness affinity all along?’ He swallowed hard, processing the revelation. ’But it’s sealed... on top of two completely unknown ones.’
His thoughts raced, piecing together the subtle details he might have overlooked until now.
’...Could it be... Could this be all connected to Raine?’

chapters.title: Chapter 216: Raine
paragraphs: ’Could this be all connected to Raine?’

The president mentioned that Malakor might have lied and attacked him in his soul space, but ended up in a pathetic state soon after. That detail made Soren question it even more. He found himself doubting whether Raine was really just an ordinary cat that mutated into some low-ranking magic beast as the director theorized or something far more powerful.

The only logical scenario he could come up with was that Malakor had invaded his soul space but ended up encountering Raine and got defeated. To be able to subdue an S-rank magic beast like Malakor so thoroughly meant she had to be at least at the same rank with bloodline advantages, if not even higher.

Yet, as the memories of the past flooded back, he couldn’t help but doubt that too. Because it was impossible to reconcile the idea of a legendary magic beast with the helpless little creature he had found five years ago, back when he was just seventeen, about two months after he got kicked out of the house.
He still remembered that night with striking clarity.

It was late, with a heavy downpour soaking everything and thunder echoing across the city streets. He was returning from a night shift, utterly exhausted, with his umbrella barely protecting him from the icy wind. That was when he caught a faint, pleading sound beneath the roar of the rain.

Following the noise down an alleyway, he spotted a small cat collapsed beside a pile of soaked trash. It was shivering violently against the concrete. Its dark fur was matted with blood from deep cuts across its body, and its chest rose and fell in shallow breaths. Pausing, it turned to look at him, its striking purple eyes hazy with pain.

Soren approached without hesitation, but the moment he reached out, the cat let out a sharp hiss, trying to scramble backward away from him before its strength gave out completely. The brief display of defiance quickly collapsed into a piteous cry as its body twitched violently. Its eyes slowly lost their luster, and its eyelids fluttered shut.
Moving quickly, Soren dropped to his knees in the downpour, stripped off his jacket, and wrapped the shivering creature before sprinting through the storm toward the nearest vet clinic.

When he arrived, the vet on duty quickly brought the cat onto the exam table. After a rapid assessment to check its fading pulse and inspect the deep cuts lining its body, the man turned to Soren with a grim expression.

He explained that the injuries were far too severe. Even if they stitched up the cuts and stopped the bleeding, the extreme blood loss meant it wouldn’t survive the night. Continuing with emergency care would only waste Soren’s money, so he recommended letting it go.
Soren refused without a second thought. He insisted on treating it regardless, instructing the vet to carry out any emergency procedures needed to keep it alive.
Reluctantly, the vet gave in and got to work.

Soren stood near the corner, his heart pounding as he watched the procedure unfold under the clinic lights. But deep down he knew that the vet was right. He had only just met the cat, and barely had any money to begin with. Spending his savings on a stray creature made no practical sense.

Gazing at its small body on the table, a deep ache clenched his chest. It looked so helpless, its fragile ribs barely moving with each strained breath. He couldn’t look away. The scene took him straight back to his early days on the streets after expulsion from his home. He remembered those cold nights outside, feeling the pain of abandonment, shivering and utterly alone.
More than anything, a strange feeling had taken hold of him. It felt as though turning his back on it would leave him with a regret that would haunt him for the rest of his life.

So, once the vet finished the emergency treatment, Soren paid the bill and carried the little cat back to his apartment with him. Over the next few weeks, he worked without rest, spending every spare moment nursing the creature back to health. Then, against all odds, it finally opened its eyes.
It survived.

When those hazy eyes met Soren’s, they held a mix of confusion and caution, and though it tried to pull away, its broken body refused to cooperate. Bound by weak muscles and injuries, it could only lie there and watch as Soren gently changed its bandages, spoke in low tones, and smoothed down its fur.
However, as the days blurred together, that lingering distrust began to melt away.

The cat slowly accepted his presence, relaxing under his touch and leaning into his hands whenever he tended to her wounds. It was not long before she regained her strength, pushing herself up and roaming around the apartment on her own.

Soren decided to raise her and, to commemorate the stormy night their paths crossed, he named her Raine. Hearing her name, she purred softly, stepped onto his lap, and showered his face with licks, finally accepting him as her person.
And, from that day forward, she became an indispensable part of his life.

She made a habit of waiting by the door for him to return from work, pouncing on whatever loose objects she could find in the small room, and bringing a lively warmth that lifted his mood whenever the world outside grew heavy.
They spent three years together like that, until one day, she simply vanished without a trace.

In the weeks that followed, Soren tortured himself searching for both her and answers. He wondered if she had grown tired of him, if she had wandered off and found another family, or if someone had taken her. Every possible outcome crossed his mind, each one leaving an empty ache in his chest.
Yet, their sudden reunion instantly put those long-held fears to rest. And it also erased any doubt that Raine was something far more than an ordinary cat.
’...But when will we actually meet again?’

He wondered if the ’she’ he had encountered in his soul space was the real Raine, or merely a lingering fragment of her consciousness, much like the Sunless Emperor’s. Perhaps her true self was out there somewhere in the real world, waiting...
’...I should meet the director tomorrow.’

Soren stood near the corner, his heart pounding as he watched the procedure unfold under the clinic lights.
But deep down he knew that the vet was right.
He had only just met the cat, and barely had any money to begin with.
Spending his savings on a stray creature made no practical sense.
Gazing at its small body on the table, a deep ache clenched his chest.
It looked so helpless, its fragile ribs barely moving with each strained breath.
He couldn’t look away.
The scene took him straight back to his early days on the streets after expulsion from his home.
He remembered those cold nights outside, feeling the pain of abandonment, shivering and utterly alone.
More than anything, a strange feeling had taken hold of him.
It felt as though turning his back on it would leave him with a regret that would haunt him for the rest of his life.
So, once the vet finished the emergency treatment, Soren paid the bill and carried the little cat back to his apartment with him.
Over the next few weeks, he worked without rest, spending every spare moment nursing the creature back to health.
Then, against all odds, it finally opened its eyes.
It survived.
When those hazy eyes met Soren’s, they held a mix of confusion and caution, and though it tried to pull away, its broken body refused to cooperate.
Bound by weak muscles and injuries, it could only lie there and watch as Soren gently changed its bandages, spoke in low tones, and smoothed down its fur.
However, as the days blurred together, that lingering distrust began to melt away.
The cat slowly accepted his presence, relaxing under his touch and leaning into his hands whenever he tended to her wounds.
It was not long before she regained her strength, pushing herself up and roaming around the apartment on her own.
Soren decided to raise her and, to commemorate the stormy night their paths crossed, he named her Raine.
Hearing her name, she purred softly, stepped onto his lap, and showered his face with licks, finally accepting him as her person.
And, from that day forward, she became an indispensable part of his life.

She made a habit of waiting by the door for him to return from work, pouncing on whatever loose objects she could find in the small room, and bringing a lively warmth that lifted his mood whenever the world outside grew heavy.
They spent three years together like that, until one day, she simply vanished without a trace.
In the weeks that followed, Soren tortured himself searching for both her and answers.
He wondered if she had grown tired of him, if she had wandered off and found another family, or if someone had taken her.
Every possible outcome crossed his mind, each one leaving an empty ache in his chest.
Yet, their sudden reunion instantly put those long-held fears to rest.
And it also erased any doubt that Raine was something far more than an ordinary cat.
’...But when will we actually meet again?’
He wondered if the ’she’ he had encountered in his soul space was the real Raine, or merely a lingering fragment of her consciousness, much like the Sunless Emperor’s.
Perhaps her true self was out there somewhere in the real world, waiting...
’...I should meet the director tomorrow.’

chapters.title: Chapter 217: Mental Cultivation
paragraphs: With that in mind, he turned his focus back to his status and continued the inspection. He felt satisfied with a long list of his abilities and how much stronger they had become. He was already sharing Sovereign’s Fortitude, Life Force Resonance, Hyper-Recovery, and Cold Resistance with Ethea, so there should be no problem with her recovery these days. Though he would have to be near her to avoid breaking the connection.

Wondering whether to take her with him tomorrow, he scanned the techniques section and noticed he already mastered everything fully except Glacial Descent. But with the promised training session from the Icebreaker Emperor, he was confident he could master it in no time as well. Perhaps he would get to learn a new technique after that.
’Right, speaking of new techniques...’

He still hadn’t learned the third star technique of the Glacial Emperor Scripture. It was called Winter’s Reign, an area-control technique. Once activated, a freeze aura would radiate outward, locking down the surrounding terrain, slowing down the enemies, and boosting all of his ice-based moves. The range was based on mastery. For example, he would start at five meters and slowly expand it while improving his mastery. He already had a similar move called Frost Surge, which he created himself, so it shouldn’t be hard to learn it.

Then, there was the second form of the Heaven-Treading Flash technique, known as Phantom Step. It was more like an upgraded version of the Quick Step, but it suppressed all sound and wind resistance, leaving no trace behind as the user moved. He should learn it too, since the consumption was no different from Quick Step; it would serve as a nice replacement.
Satisfied, he continued the inspection.
’Oh!’

His eyes lit up when he stopped at the Investments tab because a new Ongoing Investments had appeared at the bottom. It showed him his current investments that weren’t completed yet, including Sister Zoe’s and Ethea’s investments. While not powerful, it was certainly a useful addition. Though it would have been even better if it showed when they would finish. But he had to admit that would be way too much.
Not to mention he still had one new ability he had yet to test. But it would require him to enter a Gate.
’...Let’s book one; it’ll be quick with Ryan.’
With everything settled, he finally closed his status window. He sat there silently for a few minutes before deciding to learn about mental cultivation.
He first recalled what he knew about it from the knowledge stored in Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture.
’Hmm... Mental cultivation is certainly different from normal cultivation.’

While standard cultivation revolved around manipulating mana to refine the body and fuel spells, mental cultivation targeted the soul space itself. Instead of mana, it was governed entirely by mental power, also referred to as spiritual energy or soul force. It was the raw force of consciousness, willpower, and intent.

Building physical power increased output, but refining mental power granted true authority over oneself. It heightened perception, improved cognitive processing, built an internal fortress against curses, mental attacks, and illusions, and allowed a person to project their raw intent outward as physical pressure to suppress enemies.
’And Sovereign Soul-Refining Scripture consists of two cultivation methods...’

The core of the technique was Sovereign Soul Tempering, the primary cultivation method used to refine mental power, clear out spiritual impurities, and steadily expand the soul space. The second was the Imperial Forge, that brutal secondary path he had already used to violently hammer his mind during the curse’s attack.
’Where should I start then...’

He had already skipped past the basics and entered the Intent Foundation Stage. In fact, he was currently halfway through the second, Soul Tempered Core Stage. But with no external pressure acting as an anvil, the Imperial Forge was useless. If he wanted to advance any further, he had no choice but to master the primary method.
Taking a deep breath, he sank deep into his consciousness and entered his mindscape.
’...Whoa.’
He soon found himself standing in a pitch-black void that stretched endlessly in every direction. There was no floor beneath his feet, no sky above, no walls — just an infinite abyss of silence.
’Is this my soul space...?’ he wondered, turning around to scan the overwhelming dark. Last time, he had no time to look around, so his reaction was understandable.
’Wait, if it is, then...’ He hesitated for a second before raising his voice into the empty expanse. "Raine?"
Silence.
"Raine?" he tried again, sending the call further into the gloom.
No response came. The dark void remained completely motionless, offering not even an echo.

Sighing in disappointment, Soren sat cross-legged, closed his eyes, and triggered the inner mechanics of Sovereign Soul Tempering. He slowly channeled his willpower according to the scripture’s mental schematics, forcing his vast reservoir of spiritual power to wake.
The void reacted instantly.
A violent contraction rippled through the dark space as an invisible vise clamped down on his awareness. Streams of molten gold erupted through the gloom, carving paths through his mindscape.
Sovereign Soul Tempering forced his own spirit to act as both the blade and the stone.

The golden currents dragged through his internal pathways, burning away subtle mental clutter and grinding against his unrefined spiritual nodes. A searing pressure surged behind his eyes, making his spiritual form tremble. Every inch of progress demanded his full focus, requiring him to maintain a steady grip so the streams didn’t veer off course.
Soren gritted his teeth against the friction, refusing to let his control slip. He guided the golden currents in a precise, looping circuit, forcing the energy to submit to his intent.
As the first full cycle completed, the surrounding pitch-black space began to change.
Where the molten gold swept through, the gloom peeled back. A warm light radiated from the heart of his soul space, illuminating an incomplete, glowing sphere suspended above him.
It was his Spiritual Core, halfway formed and pulsing gently in the dark.
To complete the Soul-Tempered Core Stage, he had to fill the hollow center and temper the interior until it was completely solid.
So, he began guiding the golden streams directly into the core and soon became immersed in the process.
An hour passed.
Soren snapped his eyes open, sensing a presence in reality and immediately pulling his awareness out of his mindscape.
The dark void dissolved, replaced by the familiar surroundings of their room. Uncrossing his legs, he stood up from the mattress and walked over to the door and opened it.
"Welcome back, Sir."
It was obviously Emperor Hector.
"Mmm, I didn’t interrupt your rest, right?" Emperor Hector said, his eyes sweeping over Soren.
Soren shook his head, glancing past him toward Ethea, who had also opened her eyes.
Hector gave her a nod before shifting his attention back to Soren. "Are you ready?"
"Of course!"
"Then, follow me."

chapters.title: Chapter 218: Training With The Icebreaker Emperor
paragraphs: With Emperor Hector leading the way, the three of them arrived at a large training chamber.

It was large, likely built with advanced materials and equipped with a variety of modern functions. Weapon racks lined the far walls, holding everything from practice blades to heavy polearms, while durable training dummies and protective barrier generators were stationed along the perimeter.
’Is this where Sister Zoe trained?’ Soren thought, taking in his surroundings.
"Alright," Emperor Hector spoke up, breaking the silence. "Show me what you can do."
Soren nodded. He carefully positioned the wheelchair so Ethea could watch comfortably. He then walked over to the center of the hall, took a deep breath, and summoned his spear into his hand.
After thinking for a moment, he decided to start with the basics.

Every thrust, guard, and low sweep was clean and precise. He focused entirely on his footwork and weight distribution, letting his body warm up as simple lunges flowed into smooth horizontal slashes. The metal cut through the air with a steady, controlled rhythm.
Once his form was dialed in, he shifted seamlessly into the Glacial Edge Spear Arts.

The air around him chilled instantly. His movements accelerated, the basic thrusts evolving into advanced combinations. Frost traced the path of his spearhead, leaving icy arcs suspended in the air behind every strike as he drove forward with deadly precision.
From the side, Ethea and Emperor Hector watched silently as Soren moved across the hall.

Ethea quickly became immersed in the display. Before this, she had only watched him practice his basic routines and had never seen him handle a weapon with genuine intent. Watching him handle the spear with such natural mastery was a completely new sight to her.

As the cold energy flared around him, she realized just how far ahead he was. Soren was strong, stronger than she had been when she was at his rank. His talent was undeniable, evident in the fluid adjustments of his footwork and the calculated efficiency behind every movement, where not a single ounce of stamina or motion was wasted.
Yet, she knew it wasn’t just raw talent guiding those strikes.
She knew the sheer effort he poured into his training every single day, and the life-or-death struggles he had survived to reach this state.
’Hehe~’
A strange sense of pride surged within her, bringing a smile to her face as she kept her eyes glued to him.
From the corner of his eye, Hector caught her expression.

’She isn’t even trying to hide it anymore, huh?’ he thought, a fleeting amusement passing through him before he turned his attention back to Soren, who was transitioning into the final form of the technique.

’Still, the boy really is good,’ Hector admitted to himself. ’He actually mastered the Glacial Edge Spear Arts in just a month. Even little Zoe took two and a half months to reach this level back then...’
He then shook his head inwardly, a faint shadow passing across his thoughts.
’Alas, such a promising talent. If not for the situation they were in, I would have loved to take him as my disciple...’
Still, circumstances didn’t change what he could offer now. He had already decided to help both of them as much as he possibly could while they were under his roof.
Swoosh!

A sharp burst of freezing energy cut through the air as Soren leaped high into the hall, spinning his spear downward into the execution of Glacial Descent. The blade crashed toward the ground, leaving a trail of sharp frost suspended behind it before landing cleanly.
Watching the flawless execution, Hector let out another small sigh of regret. The sheer potential in front of him was staggering.
"Huff... huff..."
Soren stood upright and exhaled sharply, catching his breath as the cold aura around him slowly dispersed. Lowering his spear, he slowly walked back toward where Hector and Ethea were waiting.
"I have finished."
He looked at the Emperor, standing tall as he waited for his evaluation.

Hector stared at him in silence for a few seconds before turning and stepping toward the open center of the hall. Soren blinked, but followed a few paces behind as a quick guess began forming in his mind.
’Sorry, Ethea. It seems I won’t be able to keep my promise to go easy,’ Hector thought, a brief wave of resolve settling over him.

With a subtle flick of the Emperor’s wrist, a plain wooden spear snapped out of a weapon rack along the wall, soaring across the room and landing firmly in his grip. Without turning around, Hector spun the shaft in his hand and leveled the blunt tip directly at Soren.
"Come."
’I knew it,’ Soren thought. ’He’s really her master.’
"Hmm...
Settling into a low combat stance, Soren blinked once, clearing away all ambient noise and distracting thoughts. His vision locked onto the Emperor, and he exploded forward.

The distance vanished in an instant. Soren drove his spear straight toward Hector’s chest, the strike carrying the full weight of his momentum. Hector leaned back just enough for the cold blade to graze past his tunic, then tapped the side of the steel shaft with his wooden weapon, deflecting the thrust off course.

Using that diverted energy, Soren spun smoothly on his heel, letting the momentum carry his spear into a low, sweeping arc aimed at Hector’s legs. Instead of retreating, Hector simply lifted his front foot, letting the blade glide beneath him, before stepping down firmly to lock Soren’s angle of recovery.
Soren yanked the weapon free without breaking stride, immediately converting the recoil into a series of blistering lunges.
Clang-!
Clang-!
Swoosh-!

From the outside, it looked like Soren was driving the Emperor into a corner. He pressed forward relentlessly, chaining sharp thrusts into rapid horizontal slashes that left faint trails of frost in the air. The chamber rang with the rhythmic crack of wood striking steel.
Yet, as the exchange dragged on, the real balance of the fight became clear.

Hector hadn’t taken a single true step backward. He moved within a tight circle, brushing aside Soren’s complex combinations with short shifts of his wrists. Every defensive move from the Emperor was completely effortless, leaving no room for Soren to find a genuine opening.

When Soren extended slightly too far on a broad slash, Hector took advantage of the exposed gap. His wooden shaft darted forward like a striking viper, slipping right past Soren’s guard and striking him dead center on his left shoulder.

Pain flared through Soren’s arm, but his lips merely curled into a fierce grin. Rather than pulling back, he absorbed the force of the blow, using the impact to twist his torso and drive a quick, sharp jab toward Hector’s blind spot beneath his ribs.
Hector didn’t even look. He casually shifted his weight to the side, letting the jab pass over his shoulder, and brought the butt of his wooden spear crashing into the exposed side of Soren’s ribs.

The strike knocked the breath right out of Soren, forcing him to skid back two paces. But instead of wavering, the fire in his eyes only burned brighter. He reset his footing instantly, taking in the dull ache in his side. Every blocked strike and painful counterattack made it crystal clear where his guard was weak and where his timing lagged. This was the best opportunity he could ask for — a live demonstration of his flaws handed to him by a true master.
’Nice!’
Soren lunged forward once more, his smile widening as he threw himself right back into the fray.
’Let’s keep going!’

chapters.title: Chapter 219: What Is An Authority? [3]
paragraphs: Four hours passed in the blink of an eye.
"Huff... Huff..."

Soren sprawled on the floor, battered, bruised, and utterly exhausted. His body throbbed with pain, and he couldn’t even move a finger. Yet, despite all this fatigue, his face showed the joy of having just experienced the time of his life.
And honestly, he had.

For four straight hours, he had sparred, fallen, and adapted under the direct guidance of the legendary Icebreaker Emperor. It was an incredible lesson, a demanding trial that tested his limits and reshaped his understanding of the spear.
Emperor Hector stood nearby, holding his wooden spear, his grip tightening slightly as his eyes remained fixed on Soren.

Soren’s talent wasn’t quite as impressive as he thought, given how quickly he picked up the technique. But he possessed an absurd level of resilience, an unbelievable pool of stamina for his rank, a relentless fighting spirit, and an astonishing ability to rapidly process feedback even during combat. Every time Hector pointed out a flaw, Soren did his best to correct it, never making the same mistake twice.
It was as if he was born to be forged in battle.
"Good job, Soren. You can rest for now. We will continue it tomorrow."
Hector tossed his wooden spear to the side, ending the session.
"Y-yes, sir," Soren replied weakly from the floor, his voice barely a rasp.

Fifteen minutes later, after catching his breath and shaking off the worst of the lethargy, Soren joined them in the kitchen. He washed his hands and immediately began pulling out ingredients to prepare a meal.
"So you’re a magic chef too, huh?" Emperor Hector commented as he watched the youth handle the utensils with such familiarity.
"Yes, though I’m still just a beginner." Soren offered a sheepish grin. "By the way, is there anything specific you would like to eat, Emperor Hector? I can give it a try if I know the recipe."

Cultivators generally stopped needing food once they crossed the Sixth Circle, as environmental mana supplied all the energy their bodies required. Even so, the simple human pleasure of enjoying a good meal never truly faded, no matter how high one’s rank climbed. In fact, magic meals were specifically created to bridge this gap, offering high-level cultivators a way to enjoy exquisite flavors while absorbing condensed mana that actively nourished their pathways.
"No need to trouble yourself for me." Hector waved a hand in dismissal. "Enjoy it yourselves."
"You should give it a try, Teacher," Ethea chimed in from her wheelchair. "His cooking is really tasty."
Hector glanced between her somewhat eager expression and the busy kitchen workspace. "...Well, if you insist."

Ethea watched Soren move around the kitchen, her mind drifting back to what they had talked about during lunch. Realizing now was a good time, she turned to the Emperor. "Teacher, can you tell me about Authorities?"
Hector blinked, caught slightly off guard by the sudden topic, especially given her current state. But since there was no harm in sharing his knowledge, he agreed.
Ethea thanked him and told him what she knew so he wouldn’t have to repeat it.
"...I see," Hector nodded as he gathered his thoughts. "Since you already know the basics, I will start with how a cultivator actually reaches that peak."
He adjusted his posture, his tone shifting into the measured rhythm of an experienced instructor.

"As you already know, comprehending a fundamental ’law’ becomes mandatory when a cultivator attempts to break through to the Eighth Circle. Because of this requirement, most high-level cultivators plan their trajectory from the very beginning of their journey. When they create their personal domains and study basic laws, they consciously align their foundation toward an Authority they stand a realistic chance of mastering."
He paused for a moment, noticing Soren also listening curiously.

"The vast majority of Authorities fall under elemental classifications, like Hollow Flame, Devouring Earth, or Black Lightning. They are the most common type because they build directly on physical phenomena that cultivators interact with every day. The concepts are tangible and easier to visualize, internalize, and manifest."
Ethea nodded in understanding.

"However, beyond these elements lie rare, more abstract Authorities. These are laws governing concepts like space, time, sound, or even forces like emotions and perception. These do not rely on visible elements, but on subtle truths woven into reality. They are much harder to comprehend, requiring deep enlightenment, but they prove unpredictable whenever they appear on a battlefield."
"Have you seen any of these abstract Authorities yourself?" Ethea inquired. "Could you tell me about one?"

Hector hesitated, considering her question carefully. Sharing the intimate secrets of a cultivator’s power was a breach of ethics, but discussing a famous historical display known across the continent was a different matter entirely.
"You know about Sir Temur, right?" Hector asked.
"Mmm," Ethea nodded.
"Where do you think he got his title as the Paragon of Order?" Hector paused and, seeing the realization cross her eyes, nodded. "Right, it stemmed directly from the nature of his Authority.
"Order... Is it called Authority of Order then?"

"No, I do not know what it is officially called or what it is fully capable of. However, during the Siege of the Red Ridge, I watched him use it with my own eyes. With a single spoken command, his Authority swept across the entire allied army. He snapped hundreds of thousands of panicked soldiers back into formation in an instant. Fear vanished, and every weapon, spell, and technique struck as if driven by a single mind. More than that, his power temporarily elevated their effective strength by one, or in some cases, even two or three full ranks. Foot soldiers fought like hardened captains, and captains pushed past their natural limits without burning out their pathways."
Hector shook his head slowly, the memory still vivid in his mind.
"In that moment, standing amidst the chaos, it felt like he was the true ruler of the battlefield, rewriting the rules of war so that defeat was no longer an option."
"That’s amazing!"
"Indeed."
Silence fell over the kitchen, leaving only the crackle of oil and the rich aroma of food filling the space.
’...So that was his Authority’s power?’ Soren thought, keeping his eyes on the sizzling pan.

He knew about that famous battle against the evil magic beasts. History recorded that humanity was losing badly, facing a devastating disadvantage as the horde pushed them to the brink. But then Emperor Temur arrived, turned the tide of the battle in an instant, and ultimately won the entire war, driving the beasts out of human territory for good.
Like many others, Soren had also assumed the victory came from a massive spell that wiped out the horde. However, hearing Emperor Hector’s eyewitness account changed everything.

"And I am sure that was just the tip of the iceberg because Paragons rarely unleash their Authorities to their full extent." Hector continued. "They save that kind of power for when they face another Paragon or a being of equal threat."
He leaned back, his eyes narrowing as if recalling the terrifying aftermath of those rare encounters.

"Even when forced into a true clash, they have to hold back and calculate every move carefully. The conceptual weight behind a fully unleashed Authority isn’t something normal terrain can endure. If a Paragon goes all out without restraint, they risk wiping out everything around them — allies, land, and the very world they are trying to protect."
Soren gulped inwardly, careful not to let his outer composure slip.

Everyone knew how terrifyingly powerful a Paragon was. They were not called the peak of power for nothing. The Dead Continent stood as a grim reminder of what happened when such beings let loose. Centuries after a clash between such beings had shattered that landmass, the region remained a lifeless wasteland where nothing could grow, and no normal life could survive.

chapters.title: Chapter 220: Dinner
paragraphs: "You’re already on the right track, so I’m not going to dump a bunch of complicated explanations on you," Hector said, giving a relaxed wave of his hand. "Trying to figure out everything right now would probably just make your head spin. Sometimes it’s best to let things come together on their own when you’re ready. Plus, everyone’s journey is different. Sure, you can pick up tips or inspiration from people like the Paragon of Order, but when it comes down to it, you have to walk your own road and make your own choices."
Ethea nodded in understanding, quietly taking his words to heart.
"However," Hector continued, resting his elbows on his knees, "I can tell you the difference between an Emperor, a Sovereign, and a Paragon."
Soren paused his chopping for a fraction of a second, his ears perking up as he listened closely.

"A Domain at the Seventh Circle is merely the entry point for controlling your immediate environment," Hector explained smoothly, raising a finger. "Think of it like building a kingdom on rented land. Within those boundaries, your mana suppresses everything else, but you are still bound by the fundamental laws of the kingdom."
He raised a second finger.

"A Sovereign takes the next step. Reaching the Eighth Circle is about comprehending a fundamental law of reality to further refine your Domain and awaken a true Authority. You stop renting the land and start altering the rules governing it."
Hector raised a third finger, his eyes narrowing slightly.

"And a Paragon? A Paragon has completely integrated that law into their soul. Their Authority doesn’t just bend the surrounding environment; it overrides the laws of the world entirely. Within their domain of influence, what they decree becomes reality."
"Thank you, Teacher," Ethea said softly, bowing her head in sincere appreciation. "That clarifies a lot."
"Do not mention it."
Hector offered a nod, and with that, silence settled over the room once more.

"..." Soren paused mid-stir. For a fleeting second, he contemplated tossing out a light joke or a casual question to break the ice and keep the conversation flowing. But catching the distant look in Hector’s eyes and Ethea’s thoughtful expression, he quickly dismissed the idea.
Instead, he turned his attention back to the stove.

Right now, he was cooking a new dish called Braised Spirit-Beef Stew, one of the recipes that came from the returns. His primary goal was to prepare something deeply nourishing for Ethea, packed with vitality to help her fragile body recover even faster. Even so, considering the high quality of the ingredients and magic beast meat he was using, the dish was bound to carry a subtle benefit for Hector as well. It might be just a faint flow of pure mana combined with a soothing feeling of comfort, but it would still be something.
Watching the thick broth bubble and steam, a sudden thought crossed Soren’s mind.
’Hmm... If meals can nourish the body and replenish energy... are there dishes capable of aiding comprehension? Something that could trigger enlightenment?’

The idea sent a sudden pulse of excitement through him. If such recipes existed, it would open an entirely new path for him. He could use them to invest in high-ranking cultivators, Emperors, or perhaps even higher.
He caught himself and shook his head, pushing the grand ambition to the back of his mind.
’Focus on what is in front of you first,’ he scolded himself quietly. ’I can look into that later when I am stronger and have more free time.’

With the stew left to simmer, Soren spent the remainder of the cooking time mentally organizing what he needed to discuss with Ethea once they were alone. He needed to coordinate their next moves, review her recovery progress, and plan around Hector’s training schedule.
Just like that, an hour passed.

When the meat had softened to perfection and the rich aroma filled every corner of the house, Soren finally dished out the food. Carrying the warm bowls over to the dining table, he served Hector and Ethea first before taking a seat right beside her.
"Please enjoy," Soren said politely, addressing the Emperor before turning his focus entirely toward Ethea.

He scooped a spoonful of the steaming broth and tender meat, blew on it softly until the heat dissipated, and carefully brought it to her lips. Ethea accepted the bite, a faint warmth touching her cheeks as she swallowed the flavorful stew.
"..." Across the table, Hector watched them in silence, a faint smile appearing at the corners of his mouth.
Seeing the young man attend to her with such unhurried care struck a forgotten chord deep within him. Memories of the distant past surfaced in his mind.

Decades ago, he had sat just like this, gently feeding his own beloved wife during the painful days when illness had bound her to her bed. She had lacked the gift of cultivation, remaining a mortal, and time had relentlessly claimed her youth and vitality until her final days arrived.
Hector chuckled bitterly to himself, keeping the quiet sorrow hidden behind his calm eyes. Shaking off the nostalgic melancholy, Hector picked up his spoon and took a mouthful of the stew himself.

To his surprise, the stew was genuinely impressive. The meat was tender, and a subtle trickle of mana seeped into his limbs before vanishing into his vast reserves. Still, to his older taste buds, it felt a little underseasoned. Or perhaps he had simply grown too accustomed to the bitter flavors of his long life.
Despite his personal preference, Hector cleared the bowl completely, leaving not a single drop of broth behind.

"Not bad," Hector said, leaning back in his chair. "The mana integration is clean, and you didn’t overcook the ingredients. But... I think you relied a bit too much on the natural oil of the meat to carry the flavor, leaving the broth slightly underseasoned. Work on balancing your seasonings next time, and it will be far better."
Soren bowed his head respectfully. "Thank you for the feedback, Sir. I will make sure to adjust it next time."

"Mmm." Hector glanced at the table, noticing that Soren was still patiently feeding Ethea her remaining portion. Seeing that they were taking their time, the old man pushed his chair back and stood up. "I will leave you two to finish up. I have a few things to take care of."

chapters.title: Chapter 221: Boundaries of Trust
paragraphs: Hector stopped at the doorway, looking back at Soren. "Get a good night’s rest. We will continue the training early in the morning."
"Yes, sir."

Soren did not bother wishing him a good night, knowing high-level cultivators had long abandoned the need for sleep. In fact, even Soren himself had cut his rest down to just a couple of hours a night.
’...Now we can continue our conversation.’ He smiled, turning back to Ethea.
She blinked. ’Mm.’

’To start, let me explain your physical condition,’ Soren said as he looked at her status window in his vision. ’Hmm... Right now, your core remains ninety-two percent destroyed, with only nine percent of your mana pathways functional. In fact, those numbers have actually improved from yesterday, meaning the consommé and nutrient fluid are already showing their effects. Yet, beyond the paralysis, you are still dealing with severe nerve damage across your body. So, as encouraging as these gains might be, we are still essentially patching up a broken wall.’
’...I see.’ Ethea replied softly.

She had always known her body was in critical shape, but hearing the actual extent of the damage was jarring. It was almost frightening to realize how close to the brink she really was, even with the slight progress he mentioned. Yet, what surprised her even more was the sheer level of detail Soren possessed. She could not comprehend how he was able to diagnose the state of her core and mana pathways with such exact precision. Was his appraisal ability that powerful? Or was it tailored specifically toward diagnostic perception?

At the same time, she noticed something missing from his breakdown. He had not mentioned a single word about her chronic pain. She had also not forgotten how the constant, agonizing burn in her nerves dulled whenever he was near her.
Squinting slightly at him, she decided to finally bring it up.
’Soren... what about the pain?’ she asked, her gaze fixing on him. ’You mentioned everything else, but left that out.’
’Moreover, it has been remarkably manageable lately, especially when you are close to me... Soren. It... has something to do with you, doesn’t it?’
’I see,’ Ethea’s expression relaxed. ’You do not have to explain every detail to me, Soren. I am simply happy that you are sharing this much.’

’Ethea... It was not my intention to hide it from you. I simply could not find the right moment to bring it up,’ he sent back, his tone turning grounded and sincere. ’Actually, it is a shared ability between us, one that represents our bond.’
He met her eyes directly, laying out the details without withholding anything.

’As long as we remain close to each other, a passive effect activates. Both of our strength, speed, and overall resilience are heightened. For you, it also significantly dulls the chronic pain. On my end, my mana absorption and recovery rates increase. Beyond that, there is a hidden layer to it, a state called Synchronicity. It is supposed to trigger whenever our emotions, conviction, or intent completely align. I do not actually know what benefits it gives, only that it must be useful. Though, considering it has not activated once so far, I suppose the conditions are more spontaneous than I thought. Or perhaps it already happened, but we simply did not notice.’
He paused briefly, letting the information sink in before finishing his thought.

’On top of all that, it has another crucial effect,’ he added, his gaze softening slightly. ’It is what allowed me to shoulder the backlash from your curse that time, and it is the exact reason we can communicate like this right now.’
Ethea tilted her head, a flicker of genuine curiosity breaking through her quiet demeanor. ’How does that work?’

Soren hesitated for a moment, the words stalling in his throat. A sudden wave of doubt crept into his mind as he wondered how she might react, or if she already had a grasp on how deep this connection ran. And... What if she realized how to manipulate the bond from her end? If she figured out how to draw the burden back, she might force the pain and the curse’s feedback onto herself the next time he tried to absorb it and...
’...Sigh.’
He caught himself mid-spiral and let out a soft, silent chuckle at his own tendency to overthink. Dispelling the dark thoughts, he cleared his head and laid out the rest of the explanation to her.
’...’ Ethea fell silent, her gaze drifting downward as she suddenly closed her eyes.
Soren did not interrupt her, quietly observing the subtle shift in her expression. He guessed she was trying to probe the bond herself, testing its limits now that she knew it existed.

A few moments passed in total stillness before her eyes opened again. She stared directly at Soren, her gaze carrying a faint trace of confusion alongside a complex emotion hidden deep in her eyes, one he could not quite put a name to.
’...It did not work,’ she sent softly through the bond.
’Huh? What do you mean?’ Soren asked, genuine confusion creeping into his thoughts. ’Could there be something wrong with the connection?’

’No, I could sense the connection clearly,’ she explained, her eyes remaining locked on him. ’However, when I tried to take one of your abilities, the regeneration one, I could not find it on you. Then I realized... I already had it.’
Soren froze, the silence stretching between them for a brief beat before he cleared his throat awkwardly.
’Ah... yeah. I am not injured right now, so I did not need it anyway,’ he replied, trying to downplay the gesture. ’I just passed it over to you. Do not worry about it.’
’...That is not all,’ she continued, her voice taking on a heavier weight. ’I also sensed more. Three of them in fact.’
Soren went still a second time, his mind racing as he searched for a smooth way to explain the rest of his hidden set. Just as he opened his mouth to formulate a careful response, Ethea cut him off.
’Stop. It is better if you keep the rest to yourself,’ she sent, her tone turning firm yet calm.
’Are you sure?’ Soren asked, surprised by her suggestion.
’Yes, I am sure,’ she replied, her gaze softening as she looked at him. ’And please, do not share these secrets with anyone else.’
Soren looked at her eyes, catching the faint flicker of concern and unspoken dread lingering beneath her softened gaze.
’Yes, I understand.’
