So, as encouraging as these gains might be, we are still essentially patching up a broken wall.’
’...I see.’ Ethea replied softly.
She had always known her body was in critical shape, but hearing the actual extent of the damage was jarring.
It was almost frightening to realize how close to the brink she really was, even with the slight progress he mentioned.
Yet, what surprised her even more was the sheer level of detail Soren possessed.
She could not comprehend how he was able to diagnose the state of her core and mana pathways with such exact precision.
Was his appraisal ability that powerful?
Or was it tailored specifically toward diagnostic perception?
At the same time, she noticed something missing from his breakdown.
He had not mentioned a single word about her chronic pain.
She had also not forgotten how the constant, agonizing burn in her nerves dulled whenever he was near her.
Squinting slightly at him, she decided to finally bring it up.
’Soren... what about the pain?’ she asked, her gaze fixing on him. ’You mentioned everything else, but left that out.’
’Moreover, it has been remarkably manageable lately, especially when you are close to me...
Soren.
It... has something to do with you, doesn’t it?’
’I see,’ Ethea’s expression relaxed. ’You do not have to explain every detail to me, Soren.
I am simply happy that you are sharing this much.’
’Ethea...
It was not my intention to hide it from you.
I simply could not find the right moment to bring it up,’ he sent back, his tone turning grounded and sincere. ’Actually, it is a shared ability between us, one that represents our bond.’
He met her eyes directly, laying out the details without withholding anything.
’As long as we remain close to each other, a passive effect activates.
Both of our strength, speed, and overall resilience are heightened.
For you, it also significantly dulls the chronic pain.
On my end, my mana absorption and recovery rates increase.
Beyond that, there is a hidden layer to it, a state called Synchronicity.
It is supposed to trigger whenever our emotions, conviction, or intent completely align.
I do not actually know what benefits it gives, only that it must be useful.
Though, considering it has not activated once so far, I suppose the conditions are more spontaneous than I thought.
Or perhaps it already happened, but we simply did not notice.’
He paused briefly, letting the information sink in before finishing his thought.

’On top of all that, it has another crucial effect,’ he added, his gaze softening slightly. ’It is what allowed me to shoulder the backlash from your curse that time, and it is the exact reason we can communicate like this right now.’
Ethea tilted her head, a flicker of genuine curiosity breaking through her quiet demeanor. ’How does that work?’
Soren hesitated for a moment, the words stalling in his throat.
A sudden wave of doubt crept into his mind as he wondered how she might react, or if she already had a grasp on how deep this connection ran.
And...
What if she realized how to manipulate the bond from her end?
If she figured out how to draw the burden back, she might force the pain and the curse’s feedback onto herself the next time he tried to absorb it and...
’...Sigh.’
He caught himself mid-spiral and let out a soft, silent chuckle at his own tendency to overthink.
Dispelling the dark thoughts, he cleared his head and laid out the rest of the explanation to her.
’...’ Ethea fell silent, her gaze drifting downward as she suddenly closed her eyes.
Soren did not interrupt her, quietly observing the subtle shift in her expression.
He guessed she was trying to probe the bond herself, testing its limits now that she knew it existed.
A few moments passed in total stillness before her eyes opened again.
She stared directly at Soren, her gaze carrying a faint trace of confusion alongside a complex emotion hidden deep in her eyes, one he could not quite put a name to.
’...It did not work,’ she sent softly through the bond.
’Huh?
What do you mean?’ Soren asked, genuine confusion creeping into his thoughts. ’Could there be something wrong with the connection?’
’No, I could sense the connection clearly,’ she explained, her eyes remaining locked on him. ’However, when I tried to take one of your abilities, the regeneration one, I could not find it on you.
Then I realized...
I already had it.’
Soren froze, the silence stretching between them for a brief beat before he cleared his throat awkwardly.
’Ah... yeah.
I am not injured right now, so I did not need it anyway,’ he replied, trying to downplay the gesture. ’I just passed it over to you.
Do not worry about it.’
’...That is not all,’ she continued, her voice taking on a heavier weight. ’I also sensed more.
Three of them in fact.’
Soren went still a second time, his mind racing as he searched for a smooth way to explain the rest of his hidden set.
Just as he opened his mouth to formulate a careful response, Ethea cut him off.
’Stop.
It is better if you keep the rest to yourself,’ she sent, her tone turning firm yet calm.
’Are you sure?’ Soren asked, surprised by her suggestion.
’Yes, I am sure,’ she replied, her gaze softening as she looked at him. ’And please, do not share these secrets with anyone else.’
Soren looked at her eyes, catching the faint flicker of concern and unspoken dread lingering beneath her softened gaze.
’Yes, I understand.’

chapters.title: Chapter 222: Innocent Collateral
paragraphs: ’Now, back to the topic.’ Soren continued while feeding her. ’I have a plan to accelerate your recovery, but we need to address the real problem first.’
’The curse?’

’That’s right. As long as it remains inside you, it will keep interfering whenever we try to push your recovery past a certain point or if you break through again. The best path forward is finding a way to break it completely.’
’You’re right.’ Ethea agreed.

’So, I wanted to ask if you had any acquaintances who might be able to help us.’ Soren said, taking a sip himself. ’Do you know anyone skilled at dealing with curses or a way to find a method ourselves? Otherwise, we could consider asking Emperor Hector for assistance. He probably has a far broader network and experience.’
Ethea paused for a moment, her eyes drifting away as she pondered the question.

’I actually know someone who might have a way to deal with it, as light is her main affinity. However, we are not particularly close, and she is a Sovereign from another continent. Reaching her will be extremely difficult.’
’...’ Soren squinted, searching for his memory, wondering if she was talking about the person he was thinking of.

’Besides,’ Ethea continued, ’curses are among the most mysterious powers in existence. Very little knowledge about them is available to the world, and those who can actually dispel them are rarer still.’
’That makes consulting Teacher Hector our best immediate option,’ Ethea added, her tone settling. ’We can ask him tomorrow.’
Soren felt a weight lift from his chest at her agreement and recalled something.

’Actually, I met a senior a while ago who suggested a few ways that might be able to buy us more time,’ he said, before passing along the methods he had learned during his encounter with the Sunless Emperor.

’...Hmm. That senior is truly wise,’ Ethea replied softly after taking a moment to digest the information. ’The easiest approach is probably securing a steady supply of high-grade life force, though the cost will be astronomical. The second method... strengthening my physical constitution will be difficult right now, even if my spiritual side is stable for the time being. As for finding an artifact capable of tricking the curse... that might be the most challenging one of all.’
’Mmm.’
Artifacts of that grade were extremely rare, almost exclusively kept by Emperors and the higher class.

But he had been lucky to have seen two of them. One was Ryan’s growth-type sword, and the other was the ring Sunless Emperor had given him. Both were of immeasurable value. However, they weren’t suitable for this situation. Although he might be able to hide her if he evolved the ring into a Portable Demi-Plane, he would probably have to become an Emperor at the very least for that to happen.
Thankfully, he had the Life Force Resonance Ability, which had evolved into B-rank, so it should provide some support until they find a good solution.

He had also tried to lend her his constitution, but it was impossible, probably because her current body could not withstand the inherent pressure of his physique, or perhaps the bond simply did not support transferring constitutions.

Shaking his head inwardly, Soren pushed the thoughts aside and brought his focus back to the conversation. ’Let us put that aside for now. There is something else I need to ask. I understand you cannot tell me who your enemies are right now, but do you have any idea why they want you alive? Is there some history between you where they want personal revenge, or do you hold some secret information or mysterious artifact they are after?’

It was a classic trope, at least according to most stories he had ever come across: a hero relentlessly pursued for carrying an ancient secret or a reality-bending artifact. He could only wonder if her life followed the same dramatic script.
’Since I cannot recall anything from that day, I am unsure,’ Ethea replied, her gaze lowering slightly. ’But you are right. They definitely want something from me.’
’Hmm... When do you think they might act again?’

’They likely will not act as openly as before, knowing Teacher Hector is here and fearing that they might be under watch,’ she explained carefully. ’However, they might send people after us directly instead.’
’You mean... assassins?’
’Mm. That is why we must remain extremely careful.’
Soren considered her words for a beat. ’Then... The Tower of Apocalypse remains our best option, right?’
’...Right.’ Ethea reluctantly agreed.
Silence settled between them for a brief moment as the heavy topic ran its course. Soren watched her face, a lingering question finally pushing its way to the front of his mind.
’Ethea.’
’Hmm?’
’Can I ask you something else? A bit personal.’
’Can you tell me... why did you agree to marry me?’
Ethea fell silent, her gaze drifting downward as the unspoken words hung between them.

’...To be honest, it was not for a noble reason,’ she began softly, a trace of self-directed bitterness in her tone. ’In fact, my motives were very similar to yours. And.. I was being selfish... You might even despise me once you hear it.’
Soren stayed quiet, keeping his own guesses to himself as he waited for her to lay out the truth on her own terms.

’You see, two of the people I love most in this world are my mother and little brother,’ she continued, her voice taking on a distant warmth. ’Even though they distanced themselves after the incident, even though neither of them visited after the wedding, I still can’t bring myself to hate them. That is because my mother poured so much love into raising me, shielding me from every hardship as I grew up. And my little brother... I watched him go from taking his very first steps to becoming a cheerful young boy, all while staying his one and only ’big shishter’. They were the sole reason I kept going, the motivation behind every bit of effort I put into my training.’

’...That’s why... That’s why I was so terrified of my enemies targeting them. When my father brought up the proposal, I agreed. Even though I know now that he likely manipulated my fear to get what he wanted, the final decision was still mine.’
Her gaze slowly shifted back to Soren, a heavy weight visible in her eyes.
’I chose to protect them... and in doing so, I dragged an innocent person like you into my mess instead.’

chapters.title: Chapter 223: Overthinkers
paragraphs: Soren watched Ethea closely, sensing the storm of dark emotions brewing just under her quiet exterior. An urge to reach out and comfort her stirred in his chest, but with the bowl and spoon still in hand, he was forced to hold back.
"...Ethea," he called out softly, holding out another spoon toward her. "Here."
"..." As she leaned forward, he spoke the rest directly into her mind, letting his thoughts carry a steady warmth.

’Ethea, you do not have to feel guilty about protecting your family, nor should you keep blaming yourself for my involvement. As you said, our reasons were nearly identical. I agreed to this marriage to save my sister, and you accepted it to shield your mother and little brother. So there is no reason for you to carry all the fault alone.’
He paused, letting his gaze hold hers.
’I do not regret my choice for a second. In fact, I am genuinely glad that I married you. What about you? Do you regret marrying me?’
She swallowed, her answer coming through without hesitation. ’N-No.’
’Good,’ Soren smiled wider, bringing up another portion. ’Then let’s stop dwelling on the past and focus on what lies ahead.’
’...Mm. You are right.’ Ethea replied softly, a subtle tightness in her voice fading away. ’Sorry for making you listen to all that.’
’Don’t be,’ Soren thought back gently, bringing the last spoon forward. ’...Now that I think about it, I have not told you about my visit to the Bureau before the incident, right?’
’No, you haven’t.’
’Good. Let me share it with you then. It is actually important for what we need to talk about next.’
’Okay. I will listen carefully.’

’Hmm... After leaving the house...’ Soren picked up his own bowl and started eating while recounting the events of that morning. He told her about how the President had brought him to a magic beast sanctuary, leading to an encounter with its director, who was an elf, and a cute Aurora Kitsune, which he almost bonded with, before ultimately ending up face-to-face with Kalmira’s Nightmare.
’...Then, I ended up reuniting with Raine.’
’...Raine?’ Ethea caught the affectionate tone in his voice immediately. A strange prickle of curiosity stirred in her chest. ’W-Who is she?’

Soren blinked, then let out a small laugh as he realized how it sounded. ’Ah, right. I haven’t told you about her yet, have I? She is a small black cat I ended up taking in. We lived together for a few years back then.’
’...I see...’ Ethea let out a small breath, an unexpected wave of relief washing over her.’It was just a cat, not a girl...’
The second the thought crossed her mind, a sudden warmth rushed to her face as the truth of her reaction hit her.
She... She had actually been jealous. Over a name she had never even heard until a moment ago.
’What is wrong with me?’
She quickly shifted her gaze down, hoping her burning cheeks wouldn’t give her away.

She stole a quick glance at Soren. He was taking another bite of his own food, completely oblivious to her internal turmoil. The heat in her face slowly began to cool, replaced by a sudden realization as her mind drifted back to the past.
’...I think I understand it now.’

She remembered the morning after the wedding. There was no hesitation in his hands when he calmly helped her wash her face and hands. Later, when he practically forced that first spoon of porridge past her lips, he had casually called her a "good girl" — a phrase that had completely thrown her off back then, but made total sense now.

It was not because he was flustered or overthinking things. He was simply comfortable because he had done all of that before. Between raising his little sister and looking after a pet cat, tending to someone was second nature to him.
Calling her that must have just been a slip of habit. Perhaps he had momentarily viewed her as another little sister or a pet, acting on instinct before he could overthink it.
Or... he had acted that way because he did not want to make things awkward between them.
"Ethea?"
"Huh?"
Ethea snapped out of her thoughts, her eyes refocusing on Soren as the heat in her cheeks flared up all over again.
"Are you alright? You seem distracted," Soren asked, his brow furrowing slightly with concern as he searched her face.
"N-No, I am alright! Do not worry," she replied hurriedly, trying her best to shake her head, though her limited movement only made the panic more obvious.
Soren held her gaze for a beat, his eyes narrowing just a fraction. "Are you sure?
"Mm. Please... just continue eating."
"...Alright. But tell me if something is wrong," Soren said softly.
He turned back to his bowl, scooping up the remaining contents and clearing the rest of his food in a matter of seconds before setting the bowl down empty.
"(っ o - o ς)."
Ethea blinked at him, left speechless by how fast he had just finished.
"Done!" Soren licked his lips before wiping his mouth with a napkin. He set the paper aside and looked at her. "Wait just a moment."

He then quickly cleared the table and washed the dishes. Once the kitchen was tidy, he returned to her side and brought her back to the bedroom. Laying her gently onto the bed, he adjusted the pillows behind her head and looked down at her.
"Are you comfortable now?"
"...Yes," Ethea replied softly before her voice trailed off. "You should... lay down... too... to sleep..."
"Ok." Soren nodded and, recalling he had trained intensely and cooked not long ago, added. "Let me wash up first."
He took a few steps out of the bedroom, only to freeze in his tracks as a sudden realization struck him.
He mentally retraced the timeline of the day: it had been hours since Clara helped her back in the morning, and Ethea had been confined to either her bed or wheelchair the entire time.
Soren gulped inwardly as a knot of worry formed in his stomach. Was that why she had looked so flustered and distracted earlier?
’Ethea...’
She was likely enduring the discomfort in silence, probably embarrassed to bring it up to him.

chapters.title: Chapter 224: Big Decision
paragraphs: Soren glanced back toward the bedroom door. His first instinct was to walk back in and ask her, but his face burned hot at the thought. Putting her on the spot would only make things humiliating for her. And as for assisting her with something so personal himself... neither of them would survive that level of mortification. Furthermore, their current relationship was simply not there yet.
Without wasting another second, Soren pulled his phone from his pocket and hurriedly dialed Aunt Clara.
He held the phone to his ear, pacing a few steps further down the hall to keep his voice out of Ethea’s earshot. The line clicked open after the third ring.
"Soren? Is everything alright?" Aunt Clara’s voice came through, a touch of concern in her tone.

"Ah... Aunt Clara, I am really sorry to disturb you this late," Soren began, rubbing the back of his neck as heat crept up his face again. "Are you... free right now? Could you possibly come over here?"
There was a short beat of silence on the other end, followed by a sigh that was light with amusement.
"...Does Ethea need help?"
"...Yes," Soren muttered, his voice dropping an octave in sheer awkwardness as he stared at the floorboards.

"I thought as much," Clara chuckled softly, not missing the embarrassment in his voice. "I already anticipated this would happen, so I’m already prepared. Just send me the address, and I will head there right away."
A massive wave of relief washed over him, taking a bit of the heat from his face. "Thank you, Aunt Clara. I really owe you one."
"Don’t be silly. Tending to her is my job, and aren’t we like a family by now anyway? Just send the location, and I will be on my way," she replied warmly before hanging up.
"Yes, thank you!"

After hanging up, he immediately sent over the location. Once the message was marked as delivered, he tucked his phone back into his pocket, took a deep breath to steady his nerves, and turned back toward the bedroom.
Returning to the bedroom, he saw her staring quietly up at the ceiling.
"...Everything is going to be fine," Soren offered her a reassuring nod as he approached the side of the bed. "Just stay relaxed for a little while, alright?"
Ethea blinked, a small flicker of confusion crossing her face. "...Is something wrong?"

"No, nothing is wrong," Soren replied, pulling out his phone and tapping the screen while casting a worried glance toward her to gauge how she was holding up. "I... called Aunt Clara. She will be here soon, so please wait until then.
Ethea opened her mouth to speak, but paused as the reason behind his call suddenly clicked. Warmth rushed to her face, and she quickly fell silent, lowering her eyes.
About twenty minutes passed in an awkward silence, with Soren repeatedly checking the time and shooting concerned looks her way, before his phone finally buzzed.
Soren checked the notification, saw Clara’s text confirming she was outside, and met Ethea’s eyes.
"I’ll be back real quick."
Soren soon returned to the room with Aunt Clara, then stepped back outside to give them privacy.
"Tap... Tap..."
He paced back and forth, his arms crossed over his chest. His mind, which had been racing for the past half hour, slowly began to settle and look at the bigger picture.
A cold realization settled in his chest.

Deep down, he knew Aunt Clara could not accompany them on their journey moving forward. She had her own life here, her own family, and this city was her home. Dragging her along into the unknown, effectively putting her in constant danger just to make their lives easier, felt wrong.
And once Aunt Clara was no longer by their side, only he would be left to care for Ethea.

They could try to hire a new caretaker or nurse to travel with them, but the moment that thought surfaced, his stomach turned. His trust in strangers had hit rock bottom after learning that enemies might actively be tracking them down. What if an assassin or a spy disguised themselves as a caregiver just to get close to them and acted when their guard was down? The mere possibility made his throat go dry.

He did have his Advanced Appraisal ability, which could read mental states and expose hidden motives, but relying solely on it was a dangerous gamble. What if the enemy possessed an artifact, a concealment spell, or a mental shroud specifically designed to bypass inspection? Just like his father-in-law Darius.
If that happened, the consequences would be catastrophic.
Soren stopped pacing.

He stared down at his own hands, his mind tracing the harsh reality of their situation. He could not keep depending on outside help to handle the basic necessities of their life. Ethea washiswife. If they ended up traveling alone or eventually entered the tower, there would be no Aunt Clara, and no third party to step in. He would be the only person she could rely on.
"I... I will have to do it myself." He clenched his fists tightly.
If this boundary had to be crossed eventually, it was far better to start now, while someone as experienced and trustworthy as Aunt Clara was still here to guide them through it.
He needed to toss aside his hesitation and step up to be a real husband for her. Nodding to himself, he felt a genuine calm settle over his nerves.
’Mm... Wait...’
A sudden realization hit him, making his posture stiffen: he had been acting as if this entire place was his home this whole time.
’...Gulp.’
A spike of self-consciousness hit him as he wondered what the Emperor would think of him now. ’...’
Trying to look natural, he moved to a chair, sat down, and closed his eyes. He spent the next ten minutes sitting there in complete silence, pretending to be deep in meditation.
He only opened his eyes when his phone vibrated with a message from Aunt Clara, telling him he could come back in.
’Finally.’
He stood up and stretched a little before walking back inside.
"Aunt Clara, is everything—"
The words died in his throat. Soren stopped dead at the threshold, his eyes widening as his mind completely blanked at the sight of Ethea.
’...Beautiful.’

chapters.title: Chapter 225: A Welcome Return
paragraphs: ’...Beautiful.’

Ethea was propped up against the headboard with a few pillows supporting her back. Her damp, raven-black hair spilled over her shoulders in loose waves, framing her pale, porcelain face. Wrapped in a high-collared white nightgown that covered her completely to her wrists and neck, she looked remarkably delicate sitting there.
"Hmm?"
Her eyes shifted toward the doorway, locking directly onto his the moment he entered.
’...Gulp.’
Soren swallowed, his throat suddenly dry.
"...Ahem."
A cough from the side snapped him out of his daze. He spun around, his face heating up as he met Aunt Clara’s amused smile.
"I’ve taken care of everything," she said, her tone light. "She’s bathed, dressed, and ready to sleep. So I am gonna take my leave now and let you two rest."
Soren gave a grateful nod. "Thank you, Auntie. Let me walk you out."

He offered Ethea a nod before turning to lead her outside. While walking, Soren used the opportunity to lay out his thoughts, explaining his decision to take over Ethea’s daily care himself from now on.
Clara listened attentively, her expression softening into a warm smile. "That is good to hear. I will gladly help guide you through it."
"Thank you, Auntie," Soren said, relieved. "Then let’s meet tomorrow morning."
She agreed, and the two soon parted ways at the gate.
He made a quick detour to the bathroom to wash up, letting the water take away the lingering tension of the evening. Once finished, he dried off, dressed lightly, and returned to the bedroom.
"Sorry for making you wait."

He walked over to the bed and leaned down, carefully shifting the pillows to help Ethea lie down flat against the mattress. After tucking her in gently, he reached over to switch off the main lights, plunging the room into darkness.

He slid beneath the covers on his side of the bed, and the sudden proximity instantly made his pulse quicken. Trying to pull his mind away from the chaos in his heartbeat, he quickly initiated a conversation. ’Let’s pick up where we left off earlier, shall we?’
Since Ethea was in a situation similar to Soren’s, she quickly agreed.
Soren smiled into the dark, focusing his thoughts back on track. ’...Actually, I no longer think Raine is an ordinary cat now.’
He went on to explain the rest of the story, before finally asking, ’...What do you think?’

’Hmm... According to the things you pointed out, she is definitely not an ordinary cat. She must be at least an S-Rank. There’s also a chance her rank is lower, but her bloodline is pure and higher, probably Calamity or even Mythical grade. That would explain why she was able to defeat the Kalmira’s Nightmare you mentioned. As for her whereabouts... It’s impossible to know. Unless she had left a clue for you.’
’I thought so too.’ Soren replied and recalled something. ’Ethea... what about your magic beast?’
’She... She sacrificed herself... to save... me.’
Ethea’s voice faltered with each word, the steady flow of her thoughts growing faint.
’And I... I can’t even...’
A surge of grief settled over the connection, laced with guilt.
’I can’t even remember how she died. I... I don’t... remember...’
Soren felt a sharp pang of regret. ’I-I shouldn’t have brought that up. I’m sorry...’
He turned onto his side, his eyes immediately catching the glint of tears escaping the corners of her eyes.
He moved quickly, reaching across the gap to slide his fingers into hers. Holding her hand, he brought his other hand up to gently wipe away the tear tracing down her cheek.
"It’s okay," he whispered, his voice steady. "Please, don’t cry."
She didn’t reply, her chest rising and falling as tears kept slipping past her lashes. Soren stayed close, keeping his grip firm on her hand while gently wiping away the dampness from her cheeks.

Gradually, her posture eased as the tension left her body. Her shaky breathing settled into a steady rhythm, and her sobs faded away. Soon, her weary eyelids fluttered shut as she drifted off to sleep.
’...Guess we’ll continue tomorrow.’
Soren smiled gently before closing his own eyes and sinking deep into his consciousness.

The breeze off the lake rippled across the water, carrying the scent of pine and damp soil. Ethea stood near the edge of the bank, her feet planted on the soft grass as she rinsed a shirt in a wooden tub. Sunlight hit her face as she wrung out the cloth, her movements smooth and effortless.

Not far away, near the shade of an old oak, a majestic white pegasus grazed peacefully, its pristine wings folded gently against its flanks. Atop its back, a small black cat napped under the sun, its tail lazily twitching in the grass.
Ethea glanced over at the pair and shook her head, letting out a faint sigh. "Why are our pets so lazy? They only know how to eat and sleep..."
Perhaps catching the ’false accusation’ in her tone, both creatures snapped to attention, their faces the picture of comical indignation.1
The pegasus froze mid-chew. The cat’s head lifted slowly. Two pairs of eyes locked onto her in silent protest.
Ethea simply held her ground, arms crossing loosely over her chest as she met their gazes with an unyielding look of her own.1
A beat passed. Then another.
Unable to withstand the pressure, and knowing full well just how terrifying she could be, the two hastily looked away, suddenly finding the grass and the lake infinitely more interesting.

A faint smirk touched Ethea’s lips as she shook her head again, turning her focus back to the laundry. As she lifted another shirt to rinse, her thoughts drifted toward the path leading to the house. ’...When is he coming back?’
Almost as if answering her thought, a cheerful shout echoed from the distance.
"Daddy!"
"Daddy is back!"
Ethea quickly turned around, setting the cloth aside.

A short distance away, Soren was walking up the dirt path toward their cozy house. A laugh echoed from his chest as two young boys clung tightly to his legs, dragging their feet through the grass to ride along, while a little girl sat perched atop his shoulders, hands tangled in his hair.
A soft smile spread across Ethea’s face. She stepped away from the tub, wiping her hands on her apron, and walked forward to greet him.
"Welcome back, dear."

chapters.title: Chapter 226: The Beginning and the End
paragraphs: "Welcome back, dear."
No response came.

Soren continued walking forward, the two boys still clinging to his legs and the little girl giggling atop his shoulders. None of them so much as glanced her way. It was as though her voice had dissolved into the breeze before it could reach their ears.
Ethea’s brows furrowed slightly as she quickened her pace, closing the distance between them, and called out again, louder this time.
"DEAR!"
This time, they stopped.
Soren’s steps faltered, the boys loosened their grip, and the little girl’s laughter faded into silence as all four of them turned their heads toward her in a slow, almost mechanical unison.
And the moment their gazes met, something curdled deep in Ethea’s chest.

Their gazes were vacant and hollow, as if they were looking straight through her rather than at her. The warmth she had seen in their faces just moments ago was gone, replaced by an expression so unnervingly blank it made her stomach clench. A chilling dread coiled around her heart, squeezing until her pulse thundered in her ears.
Something was horribly wrong.
"D...Dear?" she called out again, her voice light as a butterfly. "Are you... ok?"
Soren tilted his head to the side, his soulless eyes studying her face.
"...Who... are you?"
"H-Huh?"

His words hit her like a physical blow, driving the air from her lungs. Before she could process anything, before she could reach out and demand what was happening, why he was acting like this, the world around her began to fracture.

The warm sunlight dissolved first, bleeding away like paint washed off a canvas. The blue sky crumbled next, pieces of it falling into an expanding void of nothingness. The dirt path beneath her feet, the swaying pine tree, the gentle ripples on the lake... All of it was devoured by an encroaching darkness that spread from every direction at once.

Within seconds, Ethea found herself remaining alone in an endless black expanse. And there, in the distance, walking away from her, was Soren with their children and pets. They moved further and further into the void, their profiles growing smaller with each step.
"W-Wait!"

Ethea lurched forward, her feet pounding against nothingness as she broke into a desperate sprint. Fear like she had never known flooded her veins, cold and suffocating, wrapping around her throat until she could barely breathe.
"WAIT! PLEASE!"

She ran faster. Harder. Pushed her body beyond its limits. But no matter how desperately she reached for them, no matter how loudly she screamed their names, the distance between them only stretched further. The darkness around her coiled around her ankles like living chains, dragging her back even as she fought to press forward.
"SOREN!"

He still did not turn around, and neither did the children or pets, even as their names tore from her throat in a voice she barely recognized as her own. All the while, their forms grew fainter, swallowed inch by inch by the hungry dark, until only the faintest outlines remained... But soon... even those were gone.
"Please... don’t... leave... me..."
The darkness consumed everything.
"No!"
Ethea’s eyes flew open.
"Huff... Huff..."
Her breath came in ragged, uneven gasps. Sweat clung to her forehead, cold and clammy against her skin.
"Huff... Huff..."

For several seconds, her eyes darted frantically across the darkness, struggling to piece together the shadows swimming before her. Then, little by little, the outline of a face surfaced from the gloom. The soft line of a jaw. The gentle slope of a nose. A sweep of dark lashes resting against skin, the faintest glint of moisture on slightly parted lips.

His name slipped from her lips in a whisper so faint it barely stirred the air. He was still beside her, exactly where he had been when she closed her eyes, undisturbed by the horror she had just been dragged out of.

She fell silent, unable to look away from him. Her gaze traced the familiar lines of his face, anchoring herself to the steady rhythm of his breathing as the last remnants of panic slowly loosened their grip.
’A... nightmare...’
It had been nothing more than a nightmare.

Relief washed through her, and for perhaps the first time since waking in this broken body, she felt something close to gratitude for simply being here. For being back in this room, in this bed, in this imperfect reality. Even paralyzed, even trapped within limbs that refused to obey, this reality was a thousand times kinder than the nightmare she had just escaped.
Because... Because her husband was here... with her...
She squinted her eyes as the nightmare replayed itself before her.

The beginning had been everything she wanted. A peaceful life by a beautiful lake, their children laughing and playing around, their bonded beasts lazing under the sun. She had been standing on her own two feet, washing laundry like it was the most ordinary thing in the world. It... It had felt so blissfully simple.
But...
The ending had been cruel enough to poison the whole memory.

However, it had also shown her something else. A glimpse of what could be waiting on the other side of all this struggle, a future worth every painful step, if only she fought hard enough to reach it. And at the same time, it had shown her what might happen should she falter, should she let her fears consume her, should she fail to grow strong enough to stand beside him.
Her fingers, still intertwined with Soren’s, tightened their grip.

She refused to let that tragedy happen. She refused to become the woman frozen in place, watching helplessly as everyone she loved drifted beyond her reach. If her body was broken, she would mend it. If she was too weak, she would grow stronger. She would keep walking forward, however long it took, until she could stand beside him on her own two feet.
With that resolve burning steady in her chest, Ethea closed her eyes and sank deep into her consciousness, where the first threads of spiritual power were already stirring in response to her call.

She squinted her eyes as the nightmare replayed itself before her.
The beginning had been everything she wanted.
A peaceful life by a beautiful lake, their children laughing and playing around, their bonded beasts lazing under the sun.
She had been standing on her own two feet, washing laundry like it was the most ordinary thing in the world.
It...
It had felt so blissfully simple.
But...
The ending had been cruel enough to poison the whole memory.
However, it had also shown her something else.
A glimpse of what could be waiting on the other side of all this struggle, a future worth every painful step, if only she fought hard enough to reach it.
And at the same time, it had shown her what might happen should she falter, should she let her fears consume her, should she fail to grow strong enough to stand beside him.
Her fingers, still intertwined with Soren’s, tightened their grip.
She refused to let that tragedy happen.
She refused to become the woman frozen in place, watching helplessly as everyone she loved drifted beyond her reach.
If her body was broken, she would mend it.
If she was too weak, she would grow stronger.
She would keep walking forward, however long it took, until she could stand beside him on her own two feet.
With that resolve burning steady in her chest, Ethea closed her eyes and sank deep into her consciousness, where the first threads of spiritual power were already stirring in response to her call.

chapters.title: Chapter 227: The First Lesson
paragraphs: Soren woke up early at four in the morning, and after checking Ethea’s state, he headed straight to the training hall. Emperor Hector was already waiting, so they began the morning session without delay.

By half past seven, the training was finished. Sir Hector left soon after, saying he had some business to attend to and would return later in the afternoon. Soren wondered briefly if the Emperor had overheard their conversation yesterday and so was deliberately making some space for them, but he set the thought aside as he bowed in thanks and hurried off to wash up and prepare breakfast.

Aunt Clara arrived at around eight and found the table set and breakfast ready. Ethea was awake as well, and after Aunt Clara helped her get dressed, the three of them sat down together. Over the meal, Soren and Aunt Clara shared what they’d discussed the night before: Soren was going to start learning how to care for Ethea each day. Ethea flushed at the revelation, but to everyone’s surprise, she just nodded and accepted the idea.
With breakfast done, Soren stayed behind to clear the dishes while Clara guided Ethea back to her bedroom to get ready for the day.

A few minutes later, Clara peeked out and called Soren in. Ethea was already settled in place, and all the supplies were neatly arranged at the bedside. Auntie wasted no time, moving efficiently as she explained each step with the calm, practical confidence born of long experience.

She demonstrated how to lift Ethea correctly, showing him how to support her body weight to avoid putting any unnecessary strain on her back or joints. She walked him through the process of helping her change her clothing safely, as well as handling the more personal aspects of her daily routine without making her feel uncomfortable. She emphasized each small adjustment to ensure Ethea’s comfort, reminding him that patience and gentle movements were far more important than speed.

Although Soren already knew the basics of caretaking, he still paid close attention, unwilling to let a single detail slip past him. Even when his embarrassment made his face hot, he stayed focused, intent on avoiding any mistake that might hurt or upset Ethea.

Ethea kept her eyes lowered, cheeks pink, silent throughout the lesson. The awkwardness was obvious, but she did her best to cooperate, holding still as Soren helped her. Maybe that quiet trust steadied him more than she realized.
Fortunately, the lesson soon came to an end.

"You handled that very well for a first attempt," Aunt Clara said, giving his arm a warm pat as he accompanied her toward the front entrance. "You have a light touch, and that will make all the difference. Keep practicing this way, and it will become a natural habit before long."
"Thank you, Auntie," Soren said, feeling a genuine wave of relief ease the tension in his shoulders. "I truly appreciate your guidance."
"Mmm, see you in the afternoon."
After seeing Aunt Clara off at the gate, Soren walked back into the bedroom.

On the way, the scenes kept repeating in his mind, and he did his best not to let the lingering warmth creep back up his face. But the closer he got to the room, the more stubborn the heat became, spreading to the tips of his ears against his will.
’Urgh. Get a hold of yourself, Soren!’
He shook his head sharply, as if it could scatter the images clinging to his thoughts. It did not work. Not really. But by the time he arrived, he managed to recover some of his composure.
"Eeek..."
He entered, and his eyes landed on Ethea, who was already back in deep ’sleep’. His lips curled up, but since they had plans for the day, he had no choice but to wake her up.
"Ethea." He called out softly.
There was no response.
’It seems like she is cultivating too deeply-’
[Mental State: Embarrassed, Evasive, Pretending]
’...Well, maybe not.’
Soren barely stopped his lips from twitching. But his eyes lit up almost immediately, recognizing the opportunity.
He walked over as silently as possible, gently picked her up, and placed her in the wheelchair.
"Done!"
With a satisfied whisper, he draped a soft blanket over her lap and gripped the handles.
"Let’s go."

Using the car Soren had rented, they quickly made their way to the bureau. Ethea, perhaps realizing she could not keep up the pretense, finally ’woke up’ somewhere along the drive. She then asked him where they were going, and Soren explained today’s schedule.
"Can you get me a mask too?"
Ethea asked as they arrived at their destination. She was already wearing a headscarf, but perhaps fearing people might recognize her, she wanted to cover her face further.

Soren also didn’t want others staring at her or making her uncomfortable, so he nodded without hesitation and quickly pulled a mask from his inventory. He had always kept a few of them ready for situations like this, as it was much more convenient than searching for one last minute.
"Here.
He helped fasten it in place together with the scarf, leaving only her eyes visible.
"Thank you."
"Don’t mention it." Soren smiled. "I actually prefer it this way too."
Ethea smiled behind her mask and nodded, and the two headed inside.

He had already made an appointment with the President yesterday, so they didn’t have to wait. The receptionist recognized him the moment he approached the front desk and promptly directed them toward the upper floors. "The President is waiting for you. Please head straight up."
"Thank you."
The elevator ride was brief, and they soon found themselves inside the President’s office.
"Good morning, President."
Soren exchanged a handshake with Craig, who rose from his chair with a friendly smile.
"Good morning, Soren. And... Mrs. Everly."
Ethea greeted back with a nod.
"It’s a pleasure to meet you. And I hope the journey here was not too tiring."
"Not at all. Thank you for asking, though." Ethea replied calmly. "And please go ahead with your discussion. I will not disturb you."
Craig inclined his head, a flicker of understanding crossing his features. "Then please make yourself comfortable. Can I offer either of you anything before we begin?"
"Thank you, but we just had breakfast," Soren said with a smile as he settled into the chair beside Ethea.
Craig nodded and sat down himself, folding his hands atop the desk. "Good, then shall we begin?"

chapters.title: Chapter 228: The Nightmare’s Request
paragraphs: They spent about half an hour discussing, with most of it centered around the compensation Soren had promised the president. Fortunately, the president had already prepared everything, and it wouldn’t be long before the families got their respective payments.

Then Soren got permission to personally cook meals for the injured hunters, along with a chance to meet with Director Elenaria again. He also revealed his plan to use the exclusive cultivation rooms for the next few days. The president, perhaps, had already expected it, agreed, and gave a list of candidates he had promised previously. Soren also hinted at re-discussing the deal about the monolith, and the president told him they would talk about it when the time comes.
With everything taken care of, the couple left the president’s office and headed to the Magic Beast Sanctuary to meet with the director.
"Good morning, Mrs. Elenaria."
"Oh, it’s you, Mr. Soren. Good morning." The elf director greeted back, and her eyes landed on Ethea. "And this is..."
"She’s my wife." Soren smiled. "And sorry for barging in without prior notice."

Elenaria shook her head, her gaze lingering on Ethea for a moment before she looked back up to Soren. "There’s no need to apologize. I was expecting you to come sooner or later anyway. And it’s a pleasure to meet you, Mrs. Everly."
"The pleasure is all mine," Ethea nodded politely in return.
"Alright then, please follow me."
With her taking the lead, they soon arrived at what seemed to be her personal office.
"Please, take a seat."
Soren positioned the wheelchair close to himself and sat down.
"I assume you are here to talk about your bond and what happened back then?" Elenaria asked as she poured tea into three cups.
"You are right." Soren nodded solemnly. "I wanted to clarify a few things and see if you have discovered something."
"I see..." Elenaria whispered before floating two cups toward Soren. "It’s true we discovered a few things, but before I tell you, can you tell me what happened?"
Soren nodded hesitantly and told her he saw a vision of the past, the day Raine disappeared, to be more exact. However, he left out the part that Raine spoke to him and warned him about the danger.
"Hmm..." Elenaria squinted at Soren, as if seeing through his careful omissions. But she didn’t press on it.
"I appreciate you sharing that much," she said as she took a sip of her tea. "Now, allow me to return the gesture."
Soren shifted slightly.

"As you have probably heard from the president, Malakor ended up in a pretty bad state after that bonding ritual. Fortunately, he recovered just yesterday and... admitted that he attacked you and wanted to devour your spiritual essence. However, he refuses to tell what exactly happened."
"!" Soren’s eyes widened a fraction. "He admitted it?"

"Yes." Elenaria nodded without any reaction. "But it is clear that he got beaten up by your existing bond partner, Raine, or a fragment of her soul residing within you. We are now certain she is no ordinary magic beast."
She paused, lifting her cup for another measured sip before continuing.

"That explains why you failed to form any bond in all of your attempts. Your soul space was actually claimed, and whatever pact exists between you and Raine refused to make room for another. It aligns with several theories we have discussed before." Her sharp eyes settled on Soren, studying him with an intensity that made the air feel thinner. "That ’cat’ of yours, Mr. Soren... she almost certainly carries a legendary bloodline."

Soren fell silent, arranging his features into a mask of cautious disbelief. He let his brow furrow, his lips press thin, as though struggling to process the revelation, while thinking, ’So she thinks so too...’
But before he could give a response, Elenaria set her cup down and added, almost casually, "There is one more thing. Malakor... wants to meet you again."
"W-What?" This time, Soren was genuinely in disbelief. "H-He wants to meet me?"

"...I know it sounds absurd, considering he tried to kill you. But I recommend you hear him out." Elenaria met his gaze evenly. "He has been cooperative ever since he regained consciousness, and whatever he wishes to discuss, he insists it concerns not just you, but your bond as well."

Soren’s jaw tightened. The mention of Raine sent a ripple of unease through his chest. He did not trust Malakor. The creature had invaded his soul, attacked him without warning, and would have done far worse had Raine not intervened. The idea of willingly walking back into that thing’s presence felt like stepping into a predator’s den.
"And if it is a trap?" Soren asked, his voice carefully level.
"Don’t worry," Elenaria replied without hesitation. "He is still bound by the Bureau’s restraints and unable to move. I will be there to protect you too."
Soren held her gaze for a long moment, searching for any sign of deception but found none.

’...Raine,’ he thought, the name echoing through his mind. If Malakor truly knew something about her, about what she was and why she had disappeared, then walking away was not an option. Perhaps Raine had left a clue through him...
He exhaled slowly and nodded. "Fine. I will meet him."

"A good choice." Elenaria smiled, a hint of approval flickering across her features. Then she leaned back in her chair, tapping a finger against the rim of her cup. "Actually, I also discovered something else back then. You... have a remarkably high affinity for darkness. However, it is sealed, probably by your bond."
Soren, who had been about to stand, froze mid-motion.
’She discovered that too?’
"I-Is that really true?"
Elenaria nodded confidently. "I am even certain that it is higher than your ice affinity."
Soren swallowed, a dry lump forming in his throat.
’Elves are truly incredible when it comes to perception...’
To see through a hidden element and identify it so accurately, without even breaching his soul space, was nothing short of extraordinary.
"I see..." he murmured, letting a mix of bewilderment and shock show on his face. "I had no idea..."

"It is understandable. Sealed affinities rarely manifest in daily life," Elenaria said, rising gracefully from her chair. "Whether she sealed it to protect your body from the volatile nature of darkness mana or for another reason entirely, we can only speculate for now. But keep it in mind."
She smoothed her white robe and gestured toward the door. "Now, if you are ready... let us go meet Malakor."

chapters.title: Chapter 229: The Bow and the Blow
paragraphs: Soren tried to convince Ethea to remain above, where it was safe, but she insisted on accompanying him with a firmness that left no room for argument. In the end, he relented, though his grip on the wheelchair handles remained tighter than necessary.
They used the same route from Soren’s previous visit and finally arrived at their destination.
"Eeek..."
The door creaked open, revealing the dark expanse of the chamber beyond.

The air was still just as uneasy, and that enormous tree was still here too. Only the phantom panther that lay beneath that tree had changed in any way — its immense, muscular bulk wrapped tight with coils of chains shimmering softly with suppression magic. Its fur was so immersed in the shadows that it was more an embodiment of the darkness than a living being.
Then its eyes opened.
A pair of violet eyes, sharp and luminous against the gloom, fixed directly on Soren.
For a long moment, nobody moved.
Soren stared back, bracing himself for the wave of illusions or mental attacks he had faced during their last encounter. But none came. Something about the way Malakor looked at him felt... strange.
It... It was like a devoted stray dog looking at a new owner who held a bowl of food.
’...What the hell am I thinking?’
Soren shook his head inwardly, banishing the absurd comparison before it could take root. He was probably still on edge from everything Elenaria had revealed. That was all.
This was Kalmira’s Nightmare after all, a terrifying magic beast that could destroy this city if it wanted, not some needy household pet.
Thankfully, Malakor soon looked away from him, turning to the director instead.
"...Can you leave us alone?"
"Don’t try to play tricks again, Malakor," Elenaria replied, eyeing the beast coldly. "Say what you have to say, or else I will be taking them back immediately."
"...Alright."
A heavy sigh escaped the panther, as though he were surrendering to an inescapable fate. Then, slowly, he rose to his feet.

The chains clinked and rattled with the movement, their runes flaring briefly before settling. Soren tensed before quickly moving in front of the wheelchair. Elenaria also shifted her stance, mana already gathering at her fingertips. Even Ethea, silent until now, drew in a sharp breath.
But Malakor made no move to attack. He simply walked toward them, his steps unhurried and his head lowered.

Soren frowned. That strange feeling he had sensed earlier grew heavier with every inch the panther closed, swelling until it pressed against his ribs like a second heartbeat. However, he knew it was not fear but something else entirely, something he could not name.
A few meters away, Malakor finally stopped.
And then, with a grace that belied his massive frame, he lowered his head and bowed.
"...This lowly slave greets his master."
Silence enveloped the whole chamber.
All three of them were left dumbfounded at the absurd sight unfolding before their eyes.

Elenaria’s usual composure cracked for a fraction of a second, her eyebrows twitching as her gaze darted between the bowing beast and the thoroughly bewildered young man beside her. Ethea blinked rapidly, looking up at Soren with a mix of confusion and surprise.
As for Soren, he simply stood frozen, his brain momentarily short-circuiting.
’Master? Lowly slave?’

He stared at the terrifying creature that, just days ago, had tried to tear his soul apart and devour his spiritual essence. The very same creature was now practically groveling at his feet like a disciplined pup.
"What..." Soren began, forcing his vocal cords to function as he took a cautious half-step back. "What in the world are you talking about?"
Malakor did not lift his head. The heavy chains around his neck clinked against the floor as he kept his nose pressed low to the ground.
"...Master, please don’t make this lowly slave embarrass himself any further."
Soren’s eyelid twitched. "Just answer the question."
Malakor let out a weary sigh. When he spoke again, his voice was tinged with deep humiliation.

"...When I invaded your soul space that day, my intention was not merely to devour your spiritual essence. I sought to place a slave seal upon you. A mark that would bind your will to mine and make you my eternal servant.
The chamber seemed to grow colder.

"But... it backfired." Malakor’s ears flattened against his skull. "Your mental defenses were far higher than I anticipated. And at the most crucial moment, the bond within your soul interfered, tangling itself into the process and disrupting my control over the ritual entirely. The connection twisted. The mark inverted. And as a result... the seal reversed."
He finally lifted his head, those violet eyes meeting Soren’s with something between resignation and bitter acceptance.
"Instead of making you my slave... I became yours."
Soren stared. Elenaria’s lips parted in stunned silence. Ethea’s fingers trembled.
"...You’re telling me," Soren said slowly, "that Raine didn’t defeat you? That it was just... an accident?"

"...Raine?" Malakor’s gaze flickered with something unreadable. "You mean your bond? That sneaky cat hiding in the depths of your soul?" He shook his head. "It barely had the strength to exist, let alone fight me. It was the backlash that left me in this sorry state, not her."
Soren’s chest tightened.
’Does that mean all of our theories were wrong? Then... Raine...’
His eyes narrowed into a cold glare as he fixed them on Malakor, a sharp thread of killing intent seeping into his gaze.
"What happened to Raine? Where is she now?"
Malakor held his gaze for a moment before looking away.
"She... She is... dead."
"...W-What?"
The word barely made it past his lips. His heart stuttered, then seemed to stop entirely, leaving a hollow silence in his chest where warmth used to be.

"Even before I forced my way into your soul, she had been barely hanging on, the edges of her soul already worn thin." Malakor paused briefly before finishing his words. "She... sacrificed herself to save you."
"...Thud."
"...I am sorry."

sentences.text: Soren tried to convince Ethea to remain above, where it was safe, but she insisted on accompanying him with a firmness that left no room for argument.
In the end, he relented, though his grip on the wheelchair handles remained tighter than necessary.
They used the same route from Soren’s previous visit and finally arrived at their destination.
"Eeek..."
The door creaked open, revealing the dark expanse of the chamber beyond.
The air was still just as uneasy, and that enormous tree was still here too.
Only the phantom panther that lay beneath that tree had changed in any way — its immense, muscular bulk wrapped tight with coils of chains shimmering softly with suppression magic.
Its fur was so immersed in the shadows that it was more an embodiment of the darkness than a living being.
Then its eyes opened.
A pair of violet eyes, sharp and luminous against the gloom, fixed directly on Soren.
For a long moment, nobody moved.
Soren stared back, bracing himself for the wave of illusions or mental attacks he had faced during their last encounter.
But none came.
Something about the way Malakor looked at him felt... strange.
It...
It was like a devoted stray dog looking at a new owner who held a bowl of food.
’...What the hell am I thinking?’
Soren shook his head inwardly, banishing the absurd comparison before it could take root.
He was probably still on edge from everything Elenaria had revealed.
That was all.
This was Kalmira’s Nightmare after all, a terrifying magic beast that could destroy this city if it wanted, not some needy household pet.
Thankfully, Malakor soon looked away from him, turning to the director instead.
"...Can you leave us alone?"
"Don’t try to play tricks again, Malakor," Elenaria replied, eyeing the beast coldly.
"Say what you have to say, or else I will be taking them back immediately."
"...Alright."
A heavy sigh escaped the panther, as though he were surrendering to an inescapable fate.
Then, slowly, he rose to his feet.
The chains clinked and rattled with the movement, their runes flaring briefly before settling.
Soren tensed before quickly moving in front of the wheelchair.
Elenaria also shifted her stance, mana already gathering at her fingertips.
Even Ethea, silent until now, drew in a sharp breath.
But Malakor made no move to attack.
He simply walked toward them, his steps unhurried and his head lowered.
Soren frowned.
That strange feeling he had sensed earlier grew heavier with every inch the panther closed, swelling until it pressed against his ribs like a second heartbeat.
However, he knew it was not fear but something else entirely, something he could not name.
A few meters away, Malakor finally stopped.
And then, with a grace that belied his massive frame, he lowered his head and bowed.
"...This lowly slave greets his master."
Silence enveloped the whole chamber.
All three of them were left dumbfounded at the absurd sight unfolding before their eyes.
Elenaria’s usual composure cracked for a fraction of a second, her eyebrows twitching as her gaze darted between the bowing beast and the thoroughly bewildered young man beside her.
Ethea blinked rapidly, looking up at Soren with a mix of confusion and surprise.
As for Soren, he simply stood frozen, his brain momentarily short-circuiting.
’Master?
Lowly slave?’
He stared at the terrifying creature that, just days ago, had tried to tear his soul apart and devour his spiritual essence.
The very same creature was now practically groveling at his feet like a disciplined pup.
"What..." Soren began, forcing his vocal cords to function as he took a cautious half-step back.
"What in the world are you talking about?"
Malakor did not lift his head.
The heavy chains around his neck clinked against the floor as he kept his nose pressed low to the ground.
"...Master, please don’t make this lowly slave embarrass himself any further."
Soren’s eyelid twitched.
"Just answer the question."
Malakor let out a weary sigh.
When he spoke again, his voice was tinged with deep humiliation.
"...When I invaded your soul space that day, my intention was not merely to devour your spiritual essence.
I sought to place a slave seal upon you.
A mark that would bind your will to mine and make you my eternal servant.
The chamber seemed to grow colder.
"But... it backfired." Malakor’s ears flattened against his skull.
"Your mental defenses were far higher than I anticipated.
And at the most crucial moment, the bond within your soul interfered, tangling itself into the process and disrupting my control over the ritual entirely.
The connection twisted.
The mark inverted.
And as a result... the seal reversed."
He finally lifted his head, those violet eyes meeting Soren’s with something between resignation and bitter acceptance.
"Instead of making you my slave...
I became yours."
Soren stared.
Elenaria’s lips parted in stunned silence.
Ethea’s fingers trembled.
"...You’re telling me," Soren said slowly, "that Raine didn’t defeat you?
That it was just... an accident?"
"...Raine?" Malakor’s gaze flickered with something unreadable.
"You mean your bond?
That sneaky cat hiding in the depths of your soul?" He shook his head.
"It barely had the strength to exist, let alone fight me.
It was the backlash that left me in this sorry state, not her."
Soren’s chest tightened.
’Does that mean all of our theories were wrong?
Then...
Raine...’
His eyes narrowed into a cold glare as he fixed them on Malakor, a sharp thread of killing intent seeping into his gaze.
"What happened to Raine?
Where is she now?"
Malakor held his gaze for a moment before looking away.
"She...
She is... dead."
"...W-What?"
The word barely made it past his lips.
His heart stuttered, then seemed to stop entirely, leaving a hollow silence in his chest where warmth used to be.
"Even before I forced my way into your soul, she had been barely hanging on, the edges of her soul already worn thin." Malakor paused briefly before finishing his words.
"She... sacrificed herself to save you."
"...Thud."
"...I am sorry."

chapters.title: Chapter 230: I Couldn’t Even Say Goodbye
paragraphs: ’...Dead?’
Soren stood utterly still, the dark chamber tilting on its axis as the revelation crashed over him.

His mind stopped working, his heart frozen mid-beat as if it had forgotten how to function. The world around him blurred into meaningless shapes. Bowing Malakor, watchful Elenaria, worried Ethea behind him - all of them faded into the background, drowned out by the single word constantly echoing in his chest.
...Dead.
She was dead.
The one who waited by the door every evening, the one who had curled up on his chest every night, the companion who had been his only warmth during the loneliest years of his life...
Gone.
You have to wake up, Soren.
You have someone else to save now.
We will meet again.
Those words, which he had clung to as a promise, now revealed themselves for what they truly were.
’She... She knew.’

The dream, the laughter when he asked how to wake up, the nudge urging him to leave, the way she looked at him before he closed his eyes. All of it had been her way of letting go, and he had been too blind to recognize it. Worse of all...
’I... I couldn’t even say goodbye...’
’...Soren.’
A familiar voice cut through the darkness like a thread of light.
’Ethea...?’
’It’s alright. I’m here...’
’Raine... She... She is...’

Ethea gently wrapped her consciousness around him. She did not offer empty reassurances or tell him the pain would pass. She simply held on, reminding him without words that he was not alone in the suffocating dark.
Slowly, Soren’s breathing steadied, and the reality of the chamber trickled back in pieces.

He turned his head back slightly and found Ethea looking up at him from the wheelchair, her eyes glistening with unshed tears. Her gaze held no pity, only a profound, aching recognition. She understood. Perhaps better than anyone else in this chamber, she understood what it meant to lose a bond. The hollow space that opened in your chest, the guilt that whispered you could have done more, and the memories that played on repeat, each one a small, beautiful wound.
’...Thank you.’

Meanwhile, Elenaria’s gaze remained fixed on Malakor. A subtle shimmer of mana flickered within her irises as she activated a secret spirit magic, one passed down through her elven bloodline. The hidden threads connecting soul to soul unraveled before her sight.
There.
Stretching between Soren and the bowing panther was a bond. Thin as spider silk, pulsing with a faint violet light. And...
’It is real...’
Malakor hadn’t lied.
He really became Soren’s slave...
’Then... what about Raine? Were all of our theories wrong?’
The thought unsettled her more than she cared to admit. Because she had been so certain about it, about Raine being a legendary magic beast. But now...
She glanced at Soren, observing his expression.
’He’s definitely not acting. That grief is genuine.’

The hollow look in his eyes, the way his shoulders had slumped, the tremor in his breath as he turned back toward Ethea. None of it bore the marks of performance. Whatever bond he had shared with Raine, its loss had shattered something in him that no amount of ’acting’ could fabricate.
’What a shame...’

Elenaria sighed inwardly, a rare flicker of regret passing through her. She had built an elegant theory, and reality had dismantled it without ceremony. It was not the first time her conclusions had been proven wrong, but it stung nonetheless.

However, a faint trace of suspicion still lingered at the edges of her thoughts, refusing to be fully extinguished. The slave seal was real, and Soren’s grief was real, but Malakor’s story had too many convenient angles to be accepted without further scrutiny. She would not voice her doubts now, though. There was nothing to be gained by pressing further while emotions ran this high.
’...Let’s keep watching for now.’
A few minutes passed in silence.
Soren took a deep breath, steadying himself and refocusing. The lingering grief over Raine’s absence remained, but he couldn’t afford to break down here.
’Huff...’

Now that he had calmed somewhat, a sliver of clarity pushed through the fog, reminding him that things were rarely as simple as they first appeared. He also realized he might have overreacted a bit without verifying the details himself, letting raw emotion cloud his judgment before he had all the facts.
But when his eyes fell upon Malakor, whatever reason had surfaced was swallowed whole by a fresh wave of killing intent.
’All because of this bastard...’
His fingers curled into fists at his sides.
"...You... You said you’re my slave now, right?"

"Yes, Master," Malakor replied hurriedly. "My life, my strength, my abilities, my knowledge... all of it belongs to you. Should you command me to fight, I will fight. Should you command me to die, I will die."
"..." Soren studied him for a long moment, his expression unreadable. Then he turned toward Elenaria.
"Director, is that really true?"

"...Yes. He is speaking the truth." Elenaria nodded after a brief pause. "Furthermore, he cannot lie to you, go against your interests, or refuse any of your commands. And... The seal ties his life to yours, so he is compelled to protect you at all costs. If you die, he dies as well."
"...I see." Soren narrowed his eyes. "But what if he gets injured or... dies? Does it affect me in any way?"

"...No. Even if he gets killed, you will suffer no harm. That is the fate of a slave." Elenaria’s tone was matter-of-fact, carrying no sympathy for the panther kneeling before them. "The bond is entirely one-sided by design. The master holds all the power, and the slave bears all the risk. It is why the ritual is forbidden across most civilized nations."
"You mean..."

"In the wrong hands, one could build an army of enslaved beings, stripping countless creatures of their will and turning them into disposable tools," Ethea spoke up coldly, surprising both Soren and Elenaria. "It is a vile practice that reduces living beings into hollow husks. They lose their freedom, their choice, their very sense of self. It is a disgustingly cruel magic, no matter who holds the contract."
Elenaria squinted at Ethea for a moment before turning back to Soren.
"...Your wife is right."

chapters.title: Chapter 231: The Rest Is Up to Him
paragraphs: "And beyond the ethical horrors, the ritual also puts the caster at risk. If the target’s soul proves too resilient, possesses some kind of counterattack powers, or if any unexpected interference disrupts the process, they might end up the slave themselves."
Malakor’s situation was a living example.
"...What are we going to do then?" Soren asked, his eyes narrowing at Malakor. "Do I need to take him with me, or should he still stay at the bureau?"

"...Well, we don’t own him, and you are his master now, so you should be free to take him away. However, you should still discuss it with the president and get his permission," Elenaria replied after pondering for a moment.

"I see. Then we will take our leave for now." Soren nodded before reaching the wheelchair’s handles and turning Ethea toward the exit. He paused briefly, glancing back over his shoulder at the bowing panther. "As for you... Stay here until I return."
"...Understood, Master."
Soren’s jaw tightened at the title, but he said nothing more. He pushed Ethea out of the chamber with Director Elenaria following closely behind them.
The heavy door groaned shut, and the locks clicked into place.

Malakor remained motionless, his violet eyes lingering on the door until their footsteps faded. Only then did he raise his head, the mask of submission slipping from his features like a discarded cloak.
’...I did my best, Master. The rest is up to him.’
After leaving the sanctuary, Soren returned to the president’s office to discuss what had happened with Malakor, and they decided to leave the panther in the Bureau’s custody for the time being.

With the matter settled, Soren thanked the president and guided Ethea back toward the bureau’s entrance. The morning had stretched far longer than he had anticipated, and there were still other tasks waiting for him.
His first stop was the central hospital, where all the injured hunters were undergoing treatment.

He left Ethea with Aunt Clara and headed to the kitchen, where he was warmly welcomed this time. The head chef had already been notified, so there was no problem with using the facilities and tools. In fact, the head chef was more than delighted to have him there, having heard what Soren was going to do.
Soren didn’t stand on ceremony either and got into work quickly.

He spent more than four hours cooking non-stop and finally finished preparing meals for all the injured hunters he intended to help. Of course, he didn’t forget about Ethea or Aunt Clara and her husband. He prepared something special for them too.

The only troublesome thing was delivering them. Fortunately, the hospital had already assigned a few staff members to assist him, and with their help, the meals were distributed to the respective patients without much delay.

The work also gave Soren a chance to cool down and sort through everything that had happened. The more he replayed the conversation in his head, the more certain he became that Malakor had held something back, likely because Elenaria had been watching and the panther did not wish to speak freely in front of her. As for Raine’s death, he could not bring himself to accept it. Not without seeing proof with his own eyes.

By the time he finished cleaning up and stepped out of the hospital, a message had arrived on his phone. Ryan was on his way. Soren quickly replied, then picked up Ethea and headed back toward the bureau.

Roughly half an hour later, they reunited at the premium cultivation facility, standing before the same chamber that housed the Monolith of the Primal Axis. Finding Ryan had not been difficult; he was surrounded by a small crowd of teenagers, his schoolmates to be more exact, who were chattering excitedly among themselves as they waited.

After exchanging greetings, Soren led the group inside. It did not take long to divide the students into the cultivation rooms Soren and Ryan owned. And while they settled in, Soren took the opportunity to discreetly inspect each one with Advanced Appraisal. Most were unremarkable, their potential average at best, though a handful stood out with high investment values thanks to their unique traits and abilities.

Once the arrangements were complete, Soren guided Ethea into the closest room to the Monolith. He had a hypothesis he wanted to test, one that had lingered in the back of his mind since he planned all this.
"I will cultivate for a bit; you can take a nap instead of waiting.

’Ethea, let’s try and see if it increases mental cultivation speed too.’ He added mentally as he sat down opposite her. ’Our bond ability already doubles it, and if the Monolith’s effect stacks on top of that, we could potentially reach six times the normal rate.’
"Alright." Ethea nodded and closed her eyes, sinking into her soul space. Soren followed suit a moment later.

It did not take him long to reach a conclusion. The mana around him was dense, almost intoxicating in its richness, but when he turned his focus inward to his soul space, the flow of spiritual energy remained stubbornly unchanged. The Monolith’s influence did not reach there.
’Ethea. Do you feel any difference?’
’...No,’ she replied after a pause. ’The speed is almost the same as before.’
Soren frowned, but before he could voice his disappointment, Ethea continued.
’However... it feels easier to concentrate. The environment here is far more stable than outside.’

Soren blinked, then shifted his attention back to his own cultivation. She was right. While the Monolith did not directly amplify spiritual energy, the sheer density of refined mana in the air created a more conducive environment. His thoughts felt clearer, the usual mental noise quieter, allowing him to slip into a focused state with less effort.
’...At least there is some benefit, no matter how small,’ he thought to himself before suggesting. ’Then let’s cultivate for a few hours before leaving.’
’Mm.’ Ethea agreed.

With that settled, Soren withdrew from his soul space and switched to normal cultivation, drawing in the Monolith’s refined mana to make better use of the time. He had been slacking off on it for the past few days, so this was the perfect opportunity to catch up.
’I should create a better schedule as well...’
