chapters.title: Chapter 232: A Day Off
paragraphs: They spent the rest of the afternoon cultivating and left the facilities only as evening approached. After a brief word with Ryan, they decided to postpone the shopping trip to another day.

After returning to the villa, Soren cooked dinner and ate it together with Ethea and the Emperor. Aunt Clara arrived soon after and wasted no time in pulling him along for his second lesson. This time, Soren moved more confidently, and his face burned less, though Ethea’s cheeks still stayed pink. By the time Clara declared herself satisfied and left, the night had fully fallen.

Soren left Ethea in the bedroom and returned to the training hall, where the Emperor was already waiting. What followed was a late session that pushed his aching muscles well past their limits, every drill and sparring exchange driving the day’s lingering tension out of his body through sheer exertion. By the time he dragged himself through a quick wash and finally collapsed into bed beside Ethea, the clock had already crept past midnight.
He took one last look at Ethea’s sleeping face before closing his eyes and drifting off to sleep.
"Meow~"
"Meow-!"
"Urgh..." Soren shifted under the sheets, subconsciously turning his head away from the persistent nudges. "S-stop it..."
"Meooow!"
Another sharp paw pressed against his cheek, accompanied by an insistent cry.
He reluctantly opened his eyes, blinking through the morning light until his vision cleared. Sitting squarely on his chest was Raine, her purple eyes staring down at him with zero patience.
"Raine..." A smile spread across his face. "Are you that hungry?"
"Meow." The reply came immediately, as if to say, ’What kind of question was that?’
"Alright, I’m awake now," Soren chuckled, sitting up and swinging his legs over the edge of the bed. "Let me get up."
"Meow~" Raine hopped off his chest with a satisfied flick of her tail, padding toward the door while throwing a pointed glance over her shoulder, as if urging him to hurry up.

"Haha." Soren chuckled as he dragged himself out of bed. Then he headed straight to the bathroom, washed his face, and went through the familiar steps of their morning routine. While eating breakfast, his eyes accidentally fell on the calendar pinned to the wall.
"Oh, I’m free today, huh?"
He turned back toward Raine, who was busy happily eating from her own bowl. Soren watched her for a moment, his smile widening.
"Alright, I’ve decided!" he said, tapping the counter. "Let me get dressed, and we can go out and play all day today."
"Meow?"
Raine lifted her head from her bowl, tilting it to the side with a curious glance before returning to her food with renewed focus.

Soren chuckled and walked over to his room to change into a nice t-shirt and jeans. Once she finished eating, he grabbed her favorite shoulder bag, opened the flap, and held it low. Raine hopped right inside, settling into the canvas pouch with her head resting on the edge, ready for the day.

They left the apartment and headed straight into the city. The summer heat was mild, softened by a gentle breeze that swept through the crowded streets. Their first stop was the local amusement park, a place Soren had been meaning to check out for a while.

With Raine comfortably tucked against his side, they spent hours wandering through the colorful park grounds. He bought a giant stick of pink cotton candy, tearing off small, fluffy pieces to feed her while they waited in line for the ferris wheel. They rode the big carousel, played the booth games where Soren managed to win a plush fish key chain, and grabbed lunch at an outdoor café table where Raine thoroughly enjoyed her share of grilled chicken skewers.
The hours slipped by unnoticed.

Soon, the afternoon sun began its slow descent, and the crowds gradually thinned as families packed up and headed home. Soren gathered Raine into his arms and carried her out of the park, her plush fish still clutched between her paws.
They wandered through streets and along familiar paths until they reached the hill of their favorite park, the one with the old bench overlooking the lake.
Soren sat down on that bench, gently lifting Raine out of her bag and setting her down on the slats beside him.

Raine sat up straight, curling her tail neatly around her paws as she looked out over the glowing city skyline. The plush fish lay forgotten beside her now, its stitched smile catching the amber light.
Soren leaned back, stretching his legs out as a tired but content sigh escaped him. "We should do this more often in the future."
Raine’s ear twitched, but she did not turn. Her purple eyes remained fixed on the horizon, where the sun was melting into shades of gold and violet.
For a while, neither of them moved. The breeze stirred the leaves overhead, and the distant hum of the city faded into something softer.
Raine shifted closer until her shoulder pressed against his thigh.

Soren reached down, running his fingers over the soft fur behind her ears. She leaned into his palm, narrowing her eyes in contentment. They sat together on their favorite spot, watching the sun slowly sink toward the horizon. Deep shades of orange and violet spread across the sky, stretching long shadows across the lawn.
"Soren..."
"You knew from the start... right?"
Soren’s hand paused for just a moment before resuming its gentle rhythm.
"...Yeah."
Raine closed her eyes, leaning further into his touch.
"...Don’t you want to ask me anything?"
"...Will you tell me?"
"That’s what I thought."

Soren let his gaze drift toward the horizon where the last sliver of sun was about to disappear. There were a hundred things he wanted to ask. About her disappearance, her true strength, where she was now, or when they would be able to meet again. But in the end, none of it mattered more than the simple truth he already knew.
"I’m satisfied with knowing you are alive. As for the rest, I trust you have your reasons. And you will tell me when the time is right."
Raine’s eyes opened, a flicker of surprise passing through them before softening into something deeper. "...You really have grown."
"...I had no other choice."

chapters.title: Chapter 233: Be Yourself
paragraphs: "I had no choice." Soren chuckled wryly.
Raine let out a melodic laugh, the sound carrying a warmth that reminded him of countless ordinary days spent in each other’s company.
"Then I can rest easy. Because... The road ahead won’t be easy, Soren." Her tone turned solemn. "But as long as you stay true to yourself, you’ll find your way."
Soren kept his smile, though a subtle resolve settled across his features. "I just have to be myself, huh?"
"Always," Raine replied, her expression filled with gentle affection.

She then turned back toward the horizon. Starting from the tip of her tail, her shape started to unravel. Delicate strands of light separated from her outline, drifting softly into the evening breeze and dispersing into the dimming twilight.
Raine looked back over her shoulder one last time, her purple eyes shining brightly against the dimming sky.
"Till we meet again, Soren."

Soren did not reach out to stop her. He remained seated on the wooden bench, his hand resting where her warmth had been just moments before. He watched the faint golden specks float higher and higher, dissolving into the night air until nothing was left.
His smile slowly faded, leaving his face still and composed. He looked down at his empty palm, then slowly closed his fingers into a tight fist.
"Yeah," he whispered into the open air. "Till we meet again."
The next morning.
Hector noticed Soren waking up and heading to the training hall, so he teleported ahead and waited with his arms crossed until Soren pushed open the doors.
"You’re early," he remarked, a faint note of approval in his voice.
"I have a lot to catch up on," Soren replied, rolling his shoulders as he stepped onto the training floor.

Hector studied him for a moment, his eyes catching something different in the young man’s bearing. The usual determination was still there, but the weight behind it had shifted. Something had settled overnight. The old man did not comment on it. He simply nodded and uncrossed his arms.
"Then let us not waste time. Begin."
They trained for two whole hours before the emperor stopped it.
"What’s the matter, Sir?" Soren asked confusedly. It was just 5:30; there was still enough time to train.
"The training is over."
"Huh?" Soren repeated, still struggling to steady his breathing. "But we barely got started."

Hector turned to face him fully, arms folding across his chest. There was no displeasure in his expression. If anything, a faint trace of approval flickered behind his sharp eyes. "You have already mastered the fundamentals, Soren. Your combat skills have improved greatly as well. However, continuing down this same path will only slow your progress."
Soren opened his mouth, then closed it. He had learned to recognize when the Emperor was not finished speaking.

Sure enough, Hector continued. "From this point forward, I will teach you two new things. The first is a spear technique — one that suits your natural style rather than forcing you into forms that do not fit. The second..." His gaze sharpened. "Is how to use your affinity more efficiently. You have raw power, but raw power without control is like a flood without a river. It spreads wide and accomplishes nothing."
Soren listened in silence, absorbing every word. When the Emperor paused, he gave a firm nod. "I understand, Sir."
Hector inclined his head. "Good. Then we will start with your affinity. Since we both share the ice element, it will be easier to demonstrate."
He raised a hand, and a thin wisp of frost curled around his fingers before solidifying into a perfect, gleaming shard no larger than a needle. It hovered above his palm, spinning slowly in place.
"Now you try.

Soren nodded and extended his own hand. He called upon his mana, letting the familiar chill gather in his palm. The first attempt scattered before it could even take shape, frost hissing into the air like steam. Gritting his teeth, he tried again, forcing the energy to condense. A shard slowly crystallized above his palm, but it was jagged and uneven, nearly three times the size of Hector’s, its edges flickering as though struggling to hold itself together.

"..." Hector watched the display without comment, then dismissed his own shard with a flick of his wrist. "Your mana control is decent, likely thanks to your experience with cooking magic meals. But, as you can see, it is far from refined. You are wasting a lot of your mana whenever you’re using your affinity."
Soren let the unstable shard fall apart and lowered his hand. The emperor was right, and he knew it. But there was a reason he ended up this way.

He had learned to cultivate on his own from the start, which meant everything he knew came from trial and error rather than proper instruction. From there, he poured all his focus into raising his rank and training with his spear, simply because those offered immediate, tangible results. Proper mana control demanded years of study, patience, and guidance he did not have, so refining his affinity, learning spells, walking the path of a mage — all of it had felt like a distant luxury he could not afford back then. In fact, his wind affinity had suffered the same neglect for the same reason.
But things were different now. He had resources he never dreamed of. He had time, no matter how little. And most importantly, he had an Emperor standing in front of him, willing to teach.
"What should I do then, sir?"
"We will start from the basics. But first, let us spar again. You can only use your affinity; no weapons allowed. I want to see how you wield it in actual combat before we begin."
"...I understand." Soren shifted his stance, frost already coiling around his fingertips.
"Come," Hector instructed, resting both hands behind his back. "Don’t hold back and show me everything you have."

Soren didn’t need to be told twice. He quickly created a bunch of ice arrows and sent them flying toward the Emperor, their tips glinting sharply as they cut through the air. Without pausing, he dropped to one knee and slammed his palm against the floor.
[Frost Surge!]

A pulse of icy mana exploded outward from the point of impact and shot toward the Emperor in a sweeping wave. The jagged ice rushed forward like a frozen tide, aiming to trap Hector’s feet and limit his movement while the arrows closed in from above.
"...Not bad."

chapters.title: Chapter 234: Not Bad, But Not Good Enough
paragraphs: The Emperor whispered.

The ice arrows hit him but turned into harmless snowflakes upon impact, scattering into the air like dust. At the same time, he casually stepped through the advancing Frost Surge, crushing the frozen spikes under his boots as if stepping on dried twigs.
"I know."

Soren muttered back as he drew fresh mana from his core and seized control of the mist from the broken arrows. He made it freeze midair, forming a frost veil before Hector’s eyes. He then launched a new volley of arrows that curved around the veil in a broad flanking arc.
’Now!’
As soon as the Emperor’s gaze shifted, Soren used Quick Step to disappear from his spot and reappear behind him, his palm already thrust forward.
[Frost Palm Strike!]

His hand connected squarely with Hector’s back. For a brief, exhilarating moment, Soren felt the cold surge from his palm into the Emperor’s body, watched as a layer of frost began creeping across the fabric of his training robes. It spread an inch, then two, then...
It abruptly stopped as if it were facing an invisible barrier. Moments later, it disintegrated completely, leaving the robes pristine.

Soren stared, his hand still outstretched. He had poured genuine power into that strike. In any normal encounter, the freezing would have engulfed their entire torso by now, but against Hector, it hadn’t even left a mark.
[Quick Step!]
He quickly pushed off his back foot and created distance, landing several meters away with his guard still raised.
"That was a good technique." Hector rolled his shoulder once, as though shrugging off a mild chill. "Ethea must have taught you that, right?"
Soren gave a faint nod, already preparing his next attack.
"Thought so." Hector turned to face him again, hands still clasped behind his back. "But you are still pulling your punches. Stop worrying about ’hurting’ me and fight like your life depends on it."

Soren exhaled slowly and nodded again. This time, he didn’t hold back and threw everything he had. He tried layering attacks, creating openings through misdirection and sheer relentless pressure. He used every trick he knew and invented a few new ones on the spot.
Nothing worked.
By the time his mana reserves ran dry and his legs finally gave out, Soren was on one knee, gasping for breath while the Emperor stood exactly where he was, untouched.
"I... yield..."
"Alright, take some rest while I prepare a training plan for you."
Soren replied weakly and spent ten minutes lying on the floor.
Once he recovered enough mana and stamina, he sat up.
"Feeling better?" The Emperor asked.
"More or less." Soren pushed himself to his feet, rolling the stiffness from his shoulders.
"Good. Then listen closely. I have three exercises for you. You will practice them daily until you can perform each one without any mistakes."
Soren straightened, giving the Emperor his full attention.

"First. Form a shard the size of your thumbnail and hold it for ten minutes without letting it flicker, crack, or change shape. If it so much as wavers, you start over. This will help you improve your stability."
Soren nodded. He had already seen how badly his own shard had turned out. Ten minutes of holding a perfect shape sounded grueling, but he would try his best.

"Second. Create three shards of equal size and orbit them around your body without letting any of them touch you or each other. You will start with three and add more as you improve. This will train your divided control."
’...That doesn’t sound easy.’

"Third. You will take one of those shards and fire it at a target, but you will stop it mid-flight before it hits and bring it back to your hand. The goal is not speed. The goal is control. You must be able to halt your own attack at any point and reverse its momentum without shattering it."
"...I see," Soren whispered, already imagining how many times he would fail before getting it right.
"If you don’t understand anything, you can always ask me, or Ethea." The Emperor added. "Now, go and don’t let her wait too much. I will teach you the technique later.
Soren nodded in gratitude and dragged himself out of the training hall, but stopped midway as if recalling something.
"Sir, can I ask something?"
Hector raised a brow before nodding.
"...In private?"

"..." The Emperor squinted briefly before flicking his fingers. In an instant, a translucent barrier spread outward from his feet, enveloping both of them in a shimmering dome that rippled once before settling into near-invisibility. "I have opened my domain; no one can spy now."
Soren looked around in curiosity before coughing and solemnly looking at the Emperor.
"Sir... Do you know about curses?"
"Curses?" Hector’s voice flattened, the word dropping like a stone into still water. A trace of killing intent flickered through his eyes as his gaze locked onto Soren. "Why do you ask?"

Soren froze, the sudden heavy pressure settling on his chest like an anvil. For a brief second, doubt crept in; he questioned whether he’d said something wrong to provoke that reaction or if bringing it up was a mistake. However, recalling they had no one else to ask for help, he steeled his resolve and met the Emperor’s gaze.
"I... I think Ethea is cursed."
"...What?" Hector’s eyes widened, the killing intent quickly dissolving into shock. "What did you say?"
Soren repeated what he said.
"...Can you elaborate a bit more?" The Emperor asked as he recovered his composure. "Why do you think she is cursed?"

"It’s because of her condition," Soren replied. "At first, I thought it was just the backlash from whatever happened to her, but even high-ranked healers were unable to heal her. It was as if something was preventing her from recovering. And..."
Soren explained a bunch of logical details to the Emperor, including how the Gate incident might have happened. But of course he left out his appraisal and other abilities.

"I discussed it with Ethea too, and she also has the same idea. But we don’t have anyone to turn to for this except you. We were hoping you might know something about it, or at least point us toward someone who does..."
"...I actually know someone."

Ten minutes of holding a perfect shape sounded grueling, but he would try his best.
"Second.
Create three shards of equal size and orbit them around your body without letting any of them touch you or each other.
You will start with three and add more as you improve.
This will train your divided control."
’...That doesn’t sound easy.’
"Third.
You will take one of those shards and fire it at a target, but you will stop it mid-flight before it hits and bring it back to your hand.
The goal is not speed.
The goal is control.
You must be able to halt your own attack at any point and reverse its momentum without shattering it."
"...I see," Soren whispered, already imagining how many times he would fail before getting it right.
"If you don’t understand anything, you can always ask me, or Ethea." The Emperor added.
"Now, go and don’t let her wait too much.
I will teach you the technique later.
Soren nodded in gratitude and dragged himself out of the training hall, but stopped midway as if recalling something.
"Sir, can I ask something?"
Hector raised a brow before nodding.
"...In private?"
"..." The Emperor squinted briefly before flicking his fingers.
In an instant, a translucent barrier spread outward from his feet, enveloping both of them in a shimmering dome that rippled once before settling into near-invisibility.
"I have opened my domain; no one can spy now."
Soren looked around in curiosity before coughing and solemnly looking at the Emperor.
"Sir...
Do you know about curses?"
"Curses?" Hector’s voice flattened, the word dropping like a stone into still water.
A trace of killing intent flickered through his eyes as his gaze locked onto Soren.
"Why do you ask?"
Soren froze, the sudden heavy pressure settling on his chest like an anvil.
For a brief second, doubt crept in; he questioned whether he’d said something wrong to provoke that reaction or if bringing it up was a mistake.
However, recalling they had no one else to ask for help, he steeled his resolve and met the Emperor’s gaze.
I think Ethea is cursed."
"...What?" Hector’s eyes widened, the killing intent quickly dissolving into shock.
"What did you say?"
Soren repeated what he said.
"...Can you elaborate a bit more?" The Emperor asked as he recovered his composure.
"Why do you think she is cursed?"
"It’s because of her condition," Soren replied.
"At first, I thought it was just the backlash from whatever happened to her, but even high-ranked healers were unable to heal her.
It was as if something was preventing her from recovering.
And..."
Soren explained a bunch of logical details to the Emperor, including how the Gate incident might have happened.
But of course he left out his appraisal and other abilities.
"I discussed it with Ethea too, and she also has the same idea.
But we don’t have anyone to turn to for this except you.
We were hoping you might know something about it, or at least point us toward someone who does..."
"...I actually know someone."

chapters.title: Chapter 235: The Emperor’s Curse
paragraphs: "...I actually know someone."
"Huh?" Soren’s eyes lit up. "You do?"
The Emperor nodded before looking down. "...I killed him with my own hands."
"...What?" Now, it was Soren’s turn to be shocked. "Y-You killed him?"

"...That’s right." Hector’s gaze grew distant, fixed on something beyond the shimmering barrier of his domain. "He was a notorious villain who specialized in the dark arts. A true master of hexes, soul-binding rituals, and forbidden curses. He could easily cripple a man without ever stepping foot on a battlefield, drive families mad inside their own homes, turn allies against each other with a whisper of dark magic."
Hector paused, looking back at Soren.
"..A few decades ago, he terrorized my homeland, wiping out nearly half the population for the sole purpose of experimenting with one of his curses and letting his name be known to the world."
Soren gulped, realizing just how terrifying a cursemaster was and why he had been killed.

"It took me years to track him down. He was always one step ahead, slipping through every trap we laid and leaving nothing but corpses in his wake. But eventually, I found him, and we fought for three days without rest. On the third day, I drove my spear through his heart."
Hector’s voice dropped.

"But with his dying breath, he laughed and placed a curse on me. He said I would die not by blade or by time, but at the hands of someone who wielded the same dark arts. So when you asked me about curses just now..." He met Soren’s eyes. "It brought back these bad memories. I apologize if I alarmed you."
Soren shook his head. "No, I understand. If I were in your place, I would have reacted the same way."

Hector held his gaze for a moment, then spoke. "Actually, I wasn’t that interested in such matters until that catastrophe. But after witnessing the horrors firsthand, I had no choice but to learn. I spent years researching everything I could about the dark arts. Not to use them, but to understand them. To make sure I would recognize the signs if someone like him ever appeared again.
He paused, his expression darkening.

"I have even seen curses that devour memories, curses that turn love into hatred, curses that trap a soul inside puppets, and even ones that mark an entire bloodline, causing every firstborn to die on their sixteenth birthday no matter where they hide or how well they are protected, generation after generation, with no end in sight. The horrors I witnessed... they are not something I would wish upon anyone."
Soren’s already grim face grew even paler.

While he had researched and read about them online, hearing it from someone who had lived through it made everything feel far more real. The articles, wikis, and forum posts he had skimmed in the past suddenly felt like children’s stories compared to the Emperor’s examples.

"So, while I wouldn’t call myself an expert, I know enough to recognize when I see one. Of course, my knowledge is still limited, and there are probably countless curses I don’t know of or have encountered. However, if Ethea truly is cursed, I should be able to confirm it. But identifying the exact curse and who placed it..." He shook his head. "That is beyond my knowledge."
"...What if we know its name and grade?"
"...That would definitely make things easier," Hector replied before asking curiously. "Do you know them?"
Soren hesitated for a fraction of a second before nodding. "...Yes. It’s an Eighth Circle curse. Its name should probably be Eclipse’s Erosion."
"... An 8th Circle?" The emperor muttered in surprise.

His brows furrowed deeply as he fell into thought, his gaze dropping to the floor. Soren watched him, a flicker of hope rising in his chest. Had the Emperor remembered something related? Some clue that could help them?

But Hector’s silence stretched on, and the furrow in his brow only deepened. The truth was, his knowledge barely extended past the Seventh Circle, with only a handful of Eighth Circle curses he had come across in ancient texts.

Curse masters by nature lived in hiding, guarding their secrets with paranoia, and even the most notorious practitioners rarely revealed their most powerful creations. The catastrophe that wiped out half his kingdom had been the work of a mere Sixth Circle curse that had awakened under specific conditions.
’...An Eighth Circle.’ The thought alone was staggering. ’Is this why they ’expelled’ her?’
"Sir? Do you know something?" Soren asked hopefully, snapping him out of his thoughts.
Hector looked up and shook his head. He explained that he had never encountered this one before.
Soren’s shoulders dropped, the flicker of hope dimming in his eyes.

"...However," Hector noticed that and added, "I have a few acquaintances who might be able to help. I will reach out to them and ask if they know anything about this curse. If they do, I will inform you immediately."
Soren’s head snapped back up, his eyes lighting up once more. "Sir, I... I can’t express how much this means to us. Thank you."
Hector waved a hand dismissively. "Save your gratitude for when we have answers. Now go. She must be waiting."
Soren nodded and turned to leave, pausing at the edge of the barrier to bow once more before stepping through. The shimmering dome rippled as he passed, then sealed itself behind him.
Alone in the silence of his domain, Hector stood motionless for a long moment. Then something occurred to him.
’...I never asked how they discovered its name and grade.’

An Eighth Circle curse was not something one stumbled upon through casual research. Even he, with all his years of study, had never heard of Eclipse’s Erosion. Yet Soren and Ethea knew both its name and its exact circle.

He stared at the spot where Soren had been standing, his expression unreadable. The couple had their secrets. That much had been clear from the start. But prying into them now would only push them away, and Hector had no intention of doing that.
’...I still have to askthemin the end, huh.’ He smiled wryly. ’I just hope she won’t get angry.’

chapters.title: Chapter 236: Shopping [1]
paragraphs: ’...He said that?’ Ethea asked as Soren helped her wash up while explaining his conversation with Emperor Hector.
’Yes, why? Is something wrong?’ Soren asked, sensing the change in her tone.
’No, it’s nothing.’ Ethea reassured him while already guessing who those ’acquaintances’ were. "By the way, what are we going to do today?"
"Today?" Soren smiled as he gently picked her up. "We are going shopping!"
"Shopping?" Ethea raised her brow.

"That’s right. I have to buy a new weapon, a few artifacts for the journey ahead. We also have to stock up on clothes, especially the ones suited for travel." He set her down carefully in the wheelchair and began adjusting the footrests. "Aunt Clara will accompany us after breakfast for the first round. Then we will head to the bureau to cultivate until Ryan arrives, and then finish the rest of the shopping with him."
Ethea nodded, a small smile tugging at her lips. "You planned everything out."
"I try." Soren straightened and returned the smile. "Now let’s prepare the breakfast before Aunt Clara arrives."
[The Legacy Emporium]
’Whoa...’
Soren exclaimed inwardly as they stepped into the grand hall of the establishment.

The store was massive, spanning three marble-paved floors connected by sweeping staircases, with velvet banners hanging from high arched ceilings. Mannequins lined the display cases, dressed in everything from sleek summer shirts and tailored trousers to elegant formal wear, all brightly lit under crystal chandeliers.
Soren’s glance swept across a display of lightweight, short-sleeved jackets, his eyes locking onto a small silver tag attached to the sleeve of a charcoal garment.
[Ten thousand credits.]
’...Damn.’

He had to check twice to make sure his eyes were not playing tricks on him. Twenty thousand credits for a single top. Back in his early days, that amount could have sustained him for months without a care. Reflexively, his old instincts flared, urging him to turn around and walk right out the door.

Yet, he quickly smoothed his expression, keeping his composure intact. He had more than enough money now. He was no longer the broke youth scraping together small change, and he certainly could afford proper clothes.
’...But it’s better to be frugal where I can.’
Just because he had money now didn’t mean he should throw it around carelessly.
"Shall we?" Aunt Clara’s voice broke through his thoughts, and before he could respond, she was already steering them toward the men’s section.
Soren blinked. "Wait, I thought we were shopping for Ethea first?"
"You need proper attire just as much as she does," Clara said without slowing her stride. "We will start with you, and then we will give her the attention she deserves. Fair, no?"
"I agree as well," Ethea added.
Soren opened his mouth to argue but found no grounds to stand on. "...Fine. But I’m only buying a few pieces here. The rest I’ll get in bulk somewhere cheaper."

Clara glanced back at him, her expression softening with understanding. "I understand, Soren, but you must learn to take proper care of yourself too. If we hadn’t mentioned it, you wouldn’t have even gone to the hairdresser."
Soren chuckled awkwardly, running a hand through his newly trimmed hair.
’...I’m a bit self-conscious now.’

Truthfully, he had never cared much about his appearance or how others saw him. Surviving had always taken priority over vanity. But he also understood the importance of presenting himself well, especially now. So he could only nod in agreement.
"Good," Clara smiled, turning toward the racks. "Follow me."
"Yes, ma’am..."
What followed was a relentless marathon of dressing up.

Clara picked out a handful of linen shirts, tailored trousers, and light summer jackets, handing them over in small stacks. Ethea also pointed out a few tops in slate gray and navy that caught her eye.
Soren took the first set and pulled on a charcoal tunic with dark trousers. The fit was clean, snug across the shoulders without pulling, and it suited his lean build.
When he stepped out, Clara nodded in approval. "It fits well. What do you think, Ethea?"
Ethea looked him over, her eyes lingering for a second. "...It looks good on you.

’...I’m buying it.’ Soren noted mentally before heading back inside to try the next set. A few minutes later, he stepped out in a deep navy shirt with rolled sleeves, then a high-collared vest over a white top, and finally a light jacket.
"Good!"
"Mmm. This suits you too."
Once again, he got the instant approval of both women.

He tried a few more sets after that, and surprisingly, almost every combination worked. It was as if the clothes had been tailored specifically for his frame, each piece falling into place with an ease that even Clara remarked upon. Ethea said less with each outfit, though her eyes never stopped following him.

As he turned toward the mirror to check the latest fit, he caught a few glances from other shoppers nearby. A pair of young women pretending to browse a rack of scarves had stopped to watch him. When his eyes briefly met theirs, they quickly looked away, whispering to each other.
Soren paid them no mind and turned back to Ethea. "Should I go with all of them?"
But Ethea was not looking at him. Her gaze had drifted past him, fixed on the two women with an intensity that bordered on a glare.
"Ethea?"
She blinked and refocused on him. "...All of them are fine."
"Alright, but is everything ok? You seem a little distracted."
"...I’m fine," she said, though her tone suggested otherwise.

Before Soren could press further, a tall woman in a silk dress broke away from a nearby group and approached him with a smile. "Excuse me. I hope I’m not interrupting, but I noticed you from across the hall and just had to say... those clothes look wonderful on you."
"Thank you," Soren replied with a brief nod, already turning his attention back toward Ethea.
The woman did not take the hint. She took a step closer, her eyes lingering on his chest before sliding up to his face. "Are you a model?"
"No, I’m not."
"You could be." Her eyes swept over him again, making Soren feel uncomfortable under her lingering gaze. "I know a few people in the industry. If you’re interested, I could-"
"I’m not interested."

chapters.title: Chapter 237: Shopping [2]
paragraphs: "I’m not interested." Soren interrupted the woman coldly, raising his left hand to show the silver ring on his finger. "And I’m happily married."
The woman paused, her gaze dropping to the ring before drifting over to the wheelchair. Her eyes swept over Ethea, a condescending smirk touching her lips. "Issheyour wife?"
Soren noticed the mockery in her gaze, and his expression hardened. "...Please leave while I’m being polite."

The woman chuckled, undeterred by his warning. She took a step closer, shifting her posture to emphasize her voluptuous figure, leaning in so her low-cut dress would draw his eyes straight to her cleavage.

"Come on, handsome~," She whispered, her voice turning into a seductive purr as she extended her manicured hand toward his chest. "Can a girl like that satisfy your needs? A strong man like you needs someone who can actually keep up-"
Soren stepped back before her fingers could make contact, his expression turning icy. "I said get lost."
"...Heh." The woman let out a dry laugh, her smile twisting slightly. "I was just speaking the truth. She’s a cripp-!"
Before the slur could fully leave her throat, the air in the surroundings turned freezing cold.
Soren stepped forward, his hand snapping out to grab her wrist in an iron grip before her fingers could point at Ethea.

A sharp pressure slammed down onto the woman’s shoulders, suffocating the rest of her sentence in an instant. Soren’s eyes locked onto hers, his aura flaring just enough to make blood drain completely from her face.
"Say another word," he said, his voice barely above a whisper, "and I will make sure you regret ever opening your mouth."
The woman’s lips trembled. Her earlier confidence had shattered entirely, leaving behind nothing but wide-eyed fear. She tried to pull her wrist free, but his grip held firm.
"Do you understand?"
She nodded frantically, her breath coming in short, panicked gasps.
Soren released his grip and stepped back, his expression still cold. "Now get lost."
She did not need to be told twice. Stumbling over her own heels, she turned and fled, disappearing into the racks of clothing without a backward glance.
The pressure in the air dissipated. Soren stood there for a moment, forcing himself to calm down before walking toward Ethea. He knelt beside her, holding her hands gently.
"...Are you alright?"

"..." Ethea stared down at him, her chest rising and falling in uneven breaths. The prickling feeling from earlier had vanished, replaced by a sudden warmth that flooded her cheeks. She looked at his grip on her hands, then back to his eyes, processing the intensity of what just happened.
"I’m fine." She squeezed his fingers back. "But... you didn’t have to snap like that."
"Yes, I did," Soren said without hesitation. "I don’t care what anyone says to me, but I won’t let anyone speak to you like that."
Ethea fell silent at his words, her cheeks reddening even further. Thankfully, she had a mask to hide it.

"Good riddance." Aunt Clara muttered, glancing in the direction the woman had fled, then looked down at Soren with a nod of approval. "Some people never learn where the line is until someone draws it for them."
Soren looked up at her.
"You did the right thing." Clara smiled at him. "Now, let’s pay for these and head to the boutique I talked about."
Soren nodded and rose to his feet.
They paid for the clothes at the nearest counter and made their way toward the exit.

The boutique Aunt Clara had mentioned turned out to be a smaller shop a few streets down, specializing in women’s clothes. Unlike the grand halls of the Emporium, it had a cozy, personal feel, with soft lighting and racks arranged by style.
"Now," Clara announced, turning toward Ethea with a gleam in her eye, "it is your turn, dear."
Ethea nodded, her eyes already scanning the nearest displays.
"Pick whatever you like," Soren added. "We’ll buy them all.
Clara turned to him with a knowing look. "You should pick a few as well, Soren. Oh, you’ll be the judge this time."

"Oh. Of course." Soren agreed, perhaps a little too eagerly. He was genuinely looking forward to seeing her pick out clothes she actually liked, not just what was available. But then a thought crossed his mind, and his expression sobered slightly.
"Just don’t overdo it," he said. "If you get tired or feel uncomfortable, tell Auntie or me right away."
Ethea met his eyes and gave a small nod. "I will."

Broad sleeves billowed gently before tapering at the wrists, and a mandarin collar rose to a subtle V-notch at the throat. A fine line of vine and floral embroidery traced its way down the front, repeated in delicate patterns along the cuffs and hem.

"...I like it."

"Of course you did." Clara chuckled, taking the dresses from him. "We’ll go and try them on then."

chapters.title: Chapter 238: Shopping [3]
paragraphs: Soren watched them disappear into the changing area, then found a nearby chair and sat down. A few minutes passed. Then a few more. He found himself leaning forward, elbows on his knees, glancing toward the curtain more often than he meant to.
As the curtain finally rustled and parted, he inhaled sharply, his breath catching in his throat.

Ethea sat in her wheelchair, the white dress flowing around her like morning light. The soft fabric draped over her shoulders and arms, the embroidery tracing delicate patterns down the front. The high collar framed her face, and her dark hair spilled over the pale fabric in gentle waves.
Soren stared, his mind going blank.
"...Beautiful."
The word slipped free before he could stop it.
’...The hell with it.’
He promised himself to be a man, so he decided to go for it.
"Ethea, you look absolutely stunning!"
He said, giving her a thumbs up.
Ethea’s eyes widened at the unexpected praise, her face heating up again, but she quickly recovered, her lips curling. "I’m glad you liked it."

Clara watched the two, a mysterious smile spreading across her face. Their relationship had come a long way from the close yet awkward pair she had first met. And at this rate, they would be ready to confess their feelings properly before long. As their ’Auntie’, she would happily play the matchmaker until the very end.
"Soren," she called out, "should I take a picture of you two together?"
"Oh, that would be great!" Soren’s eyes lit up. "But let me take one of you two first."

He drew out his phone and captured a few photos of Clara standing beside Ethea, both smiling for the camera. Then he stepped back, lens settling on Ethea alone, immortalizing her in the white dress beneath the gentle boutique lights. In that moment, she seemed less a person than a living portrait.
’...I should make this one my wallpaper.’
"Now you two," Clara remarked, taking the phone from him.
Soren stepped to Ethea’s side, his hand settling lightly on her shoulder. Clara snapped several photos, shifting her position with each one, until she finally nodded, satisfied.
"These came out well. We should take one with all three of us.
Soren glanced around and spotted a shop attendant arranging a display nearby. He approached her with a polite smile. "Excuse me, would you mind taking a photo of us?"
The attendant nodded warmly and took the phone. Soren returned to Ethea’s side while Clara stood on the other. The three of them smiled as the attendant counted down and captured the shot.
Soren took the phone back, and they huddled around the screen to look at the photo. The lighting was good, the smiles genuine, and the three of them looked like a real family.
"This one is lovely," Clara said.
"We should frame it," Soren added with a grin.
Ethea nodded, her eyes lingering on the screen a moment longer than necessary.
"Thank you," Soren said, looking up at the attendant. "We really appreciate it."
The attendant waved a hand. "Not at all. You three look wonderful together."

With that, Clara guided Ethea back toward the changing area to try the rest of the dresses. She came out twice more, once in the dark blue piece Soren had picked and again in a soft lavender dress Clara had insisted on. Each time, Soren’s reaction was the same. A brief silence, a stunned smile, and a thumbs up.

By the time they reached the counter, they had accumulated a modest pile. The two dresses Soren had chosen, the lavender one from Clara, and a few more that Ethea picked herself. Soren paid the bill, and they left the boutique in high spirits.
They returned to the villa for early lunch and the next lesson.
The rest of the day went as planned: they returned to the bureau, waited until Ryan and his schoolmates arrived, and went into the bureau’s internal shop to continue shopping.
"What are you planning to buy, Brother Soren?" Ryan asked as they entered the weapons section.
"An A- or B-rank spear," Soren replied. "Preferably suited for ice wielders."
"Ok, then I will look from this side." Ryan moved to the next row and returned a few minutes later. "I found one!"
"Oh, that was quick." Soren chuckled before following Ryan.

They finally stopped in front of a glass case displaying a spear mounted on a dark wooden rack. Its shaft was forged from pale silver metal with a faint blue sheen, and thin veins of frost-colored crystal spiraled down its length like frozen vines. The blade was double-edged, tapering to a needle-sharp point, and a small blue gem was embedded where the blade met the shaft.
"Oh, is this the one?" Soren leaned in closer and activated the Advanced Appraisal.
Skyfrost Spear
Rank: B
Type: Elemental Weapon (Ice)

[Description]: A spear crafted from Skyfrost Silver, a rare metal found in the frozen peaks of the northern ranges. The blade houses a Frost Core, allowing it to channel ice mana with minimal loss. It was forged by a master smith of the Glacial Forge as part of a limited set.
[Current Effects]:
- Frost Conduction: Ice mana efficiency increased by 25%. Ice-based skills cast through the spear require less energy and maintain sharper forms for longer.
- Glacial Edge: The blade naturally coats itself in a thin layer of freezing energy, adding frost damage to all physical strikes.
- Core Resonance: When infused with ice mana above a certain threshold, the spear releases a burst of freezing mist in a small radius around the wielder.

[True Worth]: A solid mid-tier weapon designed for ice affinity users. Its Frost Core can be upgraded by a skilled smith using higher-grade materials, and the shaft can be reinforced with additional Skyfrost Silver to improve durability against heavier weapons.
[Potential]: If the Frost Core is replaced with a higher-ranked variant, the spear can reach A-rank.
"Oh, it’s pretty good," Soren muttered as he pretended to read the details on the glass while reading the status window.
"Right?" Ryan grinned. "It matches you well."
"Mmm." Soren nodded while sharing the details with Ethea mentally.
"It’s within the budget too." He added, glancing at the price tag.
If they used the discount and haggled a little, they could probably buy it for 4,500,000 as well.
"Should we buy it?"

chapters.title: Chapter 239: Shopping [4]
paragraphs: "Let’s look around a bit more first," Ethea spoke up. "There might be something better."
"Good idea." Soren nodded. "No harm in checking everything before deciding."
"Then, I’ll go and take a look at the A-rank section," Ryan said and left the two alone again.

With that, they continued walking, moving from display to display. Soren kept using Advanced Appraisal on every spear they passed, no matter how ordinary it looked or how unremarkable its description sounded. He knew from stories and movies that the most valuable treasures often hid in plain sight, disguised as common items waiting for the right person to recognize their worth.
Unfortunately, this wasn’t a story, and they weren’t the main characters.1

Most of the spears turned out to be exactly as they appeared, with modest effects but no hidden potential. A few were overpriced for what they offered, and one was so poorly balanced that Ethea actually laughed when Soren shared its ridiculous effect called ’Unstable Edge’, which randomly shifted the spear’s weight between the shaft and the blade mid-swing, making it impossible to aim consistently.
Soren guessed it must have been a failed product, or he just didn’t know how to make use of it.
Half an hour passed like that.

They finished inspecting the remaining spears and managed to find three more viable options. Two of them were A-rank while the other was B-rank. After contemplating for a bit, Soren decided to buy the Skyfrost Spear and one of the A-rank spears. It was the best choice among the three, not only because of its effects but also due to its potential to evolve into an S-rank artifact.
Nightfrost
Rank: A
Type: Elemental Weapon (Ice / Darkness)

[Description]: A rare spear forged from Abyss Silver and Glacial Core Stone. Created by a master smith who sought to fuse darkness and freezing energy into a single vessel, its blade radiates a bitter chill while swallowing surrounding light.
[Current Effects:]

- Chilling Void: Each strike embeds a layer of biting cold into the wound, slowing natural regeneration. The effect stacks, and with enough accumulated frost, the target’s ability to heal can be frozen entirely.
- Umbral Veil: The blade absorbs light around the tip, making the trajectory of strikes difficult for enemies to track in combat.
- Glacial Chasm: Unleashes a wave of dark freezing energy that coats the ground in black ice, dealing continuous ice damage and blinding targets trapped within the area.
- Shadowbound: The spear passively absorbs trace amounts of shadow mana from its surroundings, using it to reinforce the shaft and sharpen the blade over time.
[True Worth: ] A rare dual-element weapon that balances ice and darkness without diluting either. Its self-maintaining properties make it a reliable companion for long journeys and extended battles.

[Potential: With enough exposure to combat and a steady supply of high-purity Ice and Darkness mana, the weapon may gradually resonate with its wielder. If that bond deepens over time, it might awaken a Weapon Spirit (Ego) and evolve into an S-rank artifact.]
He didn’t know how long it would take, but since there were no S-rank artifacts to buy, this was the closest thing to one he could get his hands on and control.

Because S-rank artifacts were rare and extremely expensive. The majority of them were already monopolized by higher-rank Hunters, powerful guilds, or institutions like the Bureau itself. They rarely appeared on the open market, and when they did, it was mostly through auctions in the upper districts of major cities, not in places like Kalmira.
They were too small and remote to attract that kind of merchandise. Even if there were, they already had their owners.
The reason for that was simple.
Unlike lower-rank artifacts, every S-rank artifact possessed a will of its own. Or more precisely, to become an S-rank, an artifact had to awaken a fully conscious Weapon Spirit.
A Weapon Spirit was, as its name suggested, a spirit that lived inside an artifact. Just like humans or other races had their souls living in their bodies, these spirits resided within their vessels.

According to Ethea, a Weapon Spirit could manifest in many ways. Some were nothing more than voices echoing directly in the wielder’s mind, offering guidance or warnings when needed. Others took on visible forms, appearing as spectral beasts, their vessels’ shapes, or even humanoid figures. A few were said to be so developed that they could hold full conversations, with their own memories, preferences, and tempers, acting less like tools and more like companions.
Furthermore, there were generally two ways a weapon spirit came into existence.

The first was through long-term cultivation. It was a living consciousness born naturally over time from years of intense resonance between the weapon, its wielder, and the continuous flow of mana passing through both. A spirit formed this way was deeply loyal, tailored entirely to its creator’s soul and fighting style.

The second was through natural awakening. Some artifacts simply developed a spirit on their own, without the influence of a master. Because they possessed an established identity from the moment they gained awareness, they were notoriously difficult to control. They chose their masters based on their own unknown criteria, and an arrogant spirit would readily reject an unworthy wielder, refusing to channel its power or actively draining its user’s mana in defiance.

That was why Nightfrost was the ideal choice. It had not yet awakened a spirit of its own, which meant there was still time. If Soren nurtured it properly, fed it the mana it needed, and fought beside it through the battles ahead, the Weapon Spirit that eventually emerged would be loyal to him.
’All the time spent to find it was definitely worth it. But the price...’
It was ten times more than the Skyfrost Spear. Even with the discount and everything he had saved up, this single purchase would cost all of his available funds.
’I think we should sell things first.’

He had more than enough mana crystals, potions, and items he got from the Sunless Emperor. There were also items his father-in-law gave them the other day. He had set them aside for a moment like this. But now that the moment was here, he found himself unwilling to reach for them.
’...Urgh.’

He had more than enough mana crystals, potions, and items he got from the Sunless Emperor.
There were also items his father-in-law gave them the other day.
He had set them aside for a moment like this.
But now that the moment was here, he found himself unwilling to reach for them.
’...Urgh.’

chapters.title: Chapter 240: Shopping [5]
paragraphs: He didn’t use the money her father gave him, and he never would. That card was still tucked away somewhere, untouched. Accepting it felt like forgiving what that family had done, and he was not gonna do that. But those items were different. They had been given for Ethea’s recovery and protection, not as hush money. If he sold them now and used the credits to buy a weapon that would protect her, wasn’t that still serving their original purpose?
’...Urgh. It feels like a convenient excuse that way.’
If he used them, he would be going back on his words, but if he didn’t, he would be letting his pride get in the way of protecting Ethea. So, neither option sat right with him.
He looked at the Nightfrost, then turned back at Ethea, who was watching him quietly, waiting to see what he would decide.
’...Forget it. I’ll sell my own things first.’

He had plenty of resources from the Sunless Emperor. Enough to cover the cost without touching a single item from her father. However, he was definitely going to keep and use those A-rank items as they were suitable for Ethea’s protection. Darius must have taken that into mind too. As for the offensive one, it was more like a counterattack item, so it would be left for Ethea too.
"Let’s go and talk with the president."
Soren finally decided.
Ethea and Ryan nodded, and they headed to the president’s office.

Thankfully, the president was in his room and welcomed them without delay. He gestured for them to take a seat, and although he was already monitoring their movements and knew almost everything, he still played along with a friendly smile. "What brings you here today?"
Soren quickly stated his purpose.

"Oh, that’s easy. I’ll arrange it right away." Craig reached for his phone and made a quick call. A few minutes later, a young staff member with short black hair knocked on the door and stepped inside.

"Luke, take them to the exchange hall and make sure they get a fair price for their items," Craig instructed. "After that, you will assist them with the rest of their shopping today. Guide them to wherever they need to go and apply the Bureau’s special discount."
"Understood, President." Luke turned to the group with a cheerful grin. "Please follow me."

Soren thanked Craig, and they followed Luke out of the office and straight to the exchange hall on the second floor. The process was smooth, and the credits were transferred into his account without any issues.
They returned to the shop and finished purchasing the two spears for 50 million. It was as if they got the Skyfrost Spear for free.
"Sir," Luke said, turning to face them. "What else are you planning to purchase?

"We both need armor," Soren replied, gesturing toward Ryan. Soren explained the kind of armor he was looking for, and Ryan added his own requirements after him. Luke listened with a nod before disappearing down the aisle. They all exchanged a glance and started browsing on their own.
Luke came back a few moments later with a sleek tablet in hand, the Bureau’s logo faintly glowing on the back.
"Everything available is listed here," he explained, swiping through the screen. "I’ll filter by your requirements. It’ll save us time."

From there, things picked up fast. Luke scrolled through the tablet, they picked what looked decent, and he took them straight to the display. Soren checked the details with Appraisal, then they tried things on and decided whether to buy, and Luke handled the payments.

They moved through the armory section in stages, working from light vests to reinforced jackets, then cloaks, boots, gloves, and everything in between. Luke knew exactly which ones offered the best durability and where the Bureau discount could stretch furthest, saving them both time and credits.
By the time they finished loading the last of their purchases into storage, Soren felt like they had bought enough to outfit a small party.
"Thank you, Mr. Luke. You saved us a lot of time," Soren said, turning to Luke.
"It’s nothing," Luke waved his hand. "I was just doing my job."
Soren nodded, then paused as an idea came to him. "Mr. Luke, if you’re interested, I can offer you a spot in one of the premium cultivation rooms."
Luke blinked, his cheerful expression faltering for just a moment. "I... that’s very generous, but—"
"Free of charge," Soren added before he could finish. "You helped us a lot today. Consider it a thank you."
Luke hesitated, glancing between Soren and the others, then bowed his head slightly. "...Thank you. I’ll make good use of it."
"I’ll let the facility know. You can use it after your shift ends."
With that, they parted ways. Luke headed back toward his work while Soren, Ethea, and Ryan turned toward the exit.
They got into the rented car, with Soren carefully putting Ethea in the back seat while Ryan sat beside him.
"So, what are you going to treat us, Ryan?" Soren smiled as he started the engine. "Or should I cook something myself?"
"Don’t worry, Brother Soren," Ryan threw a thumbs up, "I’ve got everything planned. First, we are going to this place."
He leaned forward and showed Soren the address on his phone. It was a dessert café near the city center, not too far from where they were. Soren glanced at the name but didn’t recognize it.
"A dessert café?
"Not just any café," Ryan said with a grin. "They’re famous for their honey-glazed pastries and iced cream. People line up for an hour just to get a table."
Ethea’s eyes flickered with interest from the passenger seat.
’Sweets...’
"Alright then." Soren pulled the car out of the parking lot and slowly merged into the evening traffic. "Let’s see if it’s worth the hype."

The drive was short, and Ryan directed him through the side streets until they reached a cozy-looking building with lights spilling from its windows. A sign hung above the entrance, painted with curling letters that read Honey & Glaze.
"Is this the one?"
"Yes, it is."
"Not bad," Soren praised as he helped Ethea out of the car and into her wheelchair before the three of them headed inside.

The café was small but lively, filled with the smell of fresh pastries and something sweet baking in the back. Soft music played overhead, and the tables were packed with couples and small groups chatting over colorful plates.

Ryan had made a reservation, so they were seated quickly near the window. The waitress adjusted the table to make room for Ethea’s wheelchair, and Soren positioned her comfortably before taking his seat beside her. A moment later, menus were handed out, but Soren barely glanced at his before setting it down.
"We’ll all have the honey-glazed pastry with iced cream," he said. "That’s what we came for."

Ryan nodded and gave the order to the waitress. Once she left, they started talking. Ryan regretted not being able to accompany them in the morning shopping. Soren chuckled and told him to just go with his family and buy them a lot as well.
Ethea listened quietly, noticing how different Soren was with Ryan. He acted and talked more freely with him around.
’They are like real brothers...’
Her lips curled up faintly. She felt happy for Soren, especially after knowing how tragic his past was. He really deserved a ’little brother’ like Ryan. Speaking of which...
’I should investigate his little sister too...’

chapters.title: Chapter 241: A Thread of Return
paragraphs: "Sir, here are your orders."

The waitress placed three plates on the table, each holding a honey-glazed pastry with a scoop of ice cream slowly melting on the side. The sweet smell drifted up with the steam, and Ryan was already reaching for his fork before the waitress had even finished setting them down.
Soren shook his head at Ryan’s eagerness while getting prepared himself.
"Enjoy your meal." The waitress smiled as she finished. "Please let me know if there is anything else you need."
"Actually, can you prepare five more, but for takeout?" Soren asked, looking up. "We will take them with us when we leave."
"Of course, sir," the waitress replied politely, "I will have everything packaged and ready for you at the counter."
"Thank you."
With that, the waitress took her leave, leaving three of them to enjoy their treats.
"Let’s dig in then, shall we?"
Soren said as he took a small spoonful of ice cream and gently held it to Ethea. She swallowed it gracefully.
"How is it?" Soren asked, noticing Ryan’s anticipated stare.
"...Tasty." Ethea smiled. "You try it too."
Soren nodded and ate another spoonful himself.
"It’s really good."
"Told ya." Ryan grinned, satisfied with both of their reactions.
"Ok, I admit it." Soren chuckled as he continued to feed Ethea. "You really picked a great place."

Ryan puffed up with pride and dug into his own plate with renewed enthusiasm. Soren and Ethea ate at a relaxed pace, savoring the pastries. By the time their plates were clean, the crowd had begun to thin.
Ryan paid for three of them and three of the take-outs, while Soren paid for the two. Taking the boxes, they headed out.

Next, they went to a family restaurant where they ate Kalmira’s best dumplings. Obviously, Soren enjoyed it the most. And as a thank you for treating them today for their favorite meals, Soren drove Ryan to his home.
"Goodbye, brother Soren." Ryan waved as Soren turned the car. "Goodbye, sister-in-law. Have a good night."
"You too. Say hello to your family." Soren smiled. "Then, see you tomorrow."
"Yes, see you tomorrow."
With that final farewell, Soren and Ethea headed back home.

After returning to the villa, Soren accompanied Aunt Clara for the next lesson. Fortunately, he was starting to get a little better at handling himself when helping Ethea. By the time they left, he should be able to take over the task fully.
However, the Emperor didn’t return, so Soren could only train by himself, repeating the exercises he was taught in the morning.
His focus was disrupted when he heard a familiar sound ring in his head.
[Ding!]
"..." Soren barely stopped himself from reacting and stopped the exercise as naturally as possible, collapsing backward to the floor and closing his eyes.
’Let’s see...’
[Investment Detected]
[Target: Nick Vil]
[Analyzing Investment...]

[Investment: You covered the full cost of the target’s father’s medical treatment when no one else would, lifting a burden that had crushed the target’s family for weeks. Additionally, you provided the target with access to a premium cultivation room at no cost, allowing him to cultivate in an optimal environment during a critical phase of his recovery and growth.]
[Analyzing Target Response...]

[The target has successfully broken through to the 2nd Circle, Early Stage. The weight lifted from his shoulders, combined with the optimal cultivation environment, allowed him to push past his limits. The target is unaware of your direct involvement but carries a deep, subconscious sense of gratitude for you. He has resolved to work harder than ever, uncover the identity of his benefactor, and repay the kindness shown to his family.]
[Evaluating Investment Significance...]
[Evaluation Complete.]
[Investment Grade: High]
[Calculating Returns...]
[Calculation complete.]
[Applying Authority Modifier: Amplification (Passive) (Baseline bonus applied. Reward tier scaling upgraded.)]
[Returns Granted:]
[1. Permanent Mana Capacity Expansion (+5,000)]
[2. +3000 Refined Mana]
[2. Advanced Health Potion x10]
[3. High-Grade Mana Crystal x100]
[Integration initiated...]
[Integration complete!]
’Oh, he finally succeeded, huh?’
Soren’s lips curled up faintly as he read the messages.

Actually, he had asked the president to help find Nick at that time as well. The other day, he learned their situation: Nick’s father, Sir Moro, was still bedridden, and they didn’t have enough money to cover the remaining treatment costs.

He also heard Nick had dropped out of the academy to work as a Hunter and find money. But... since he was just a 16-year-old boy with no experience, well, bad experience, and only at the 1st circle, he was rejected by almost all the parties he applied to. And the ones that accepted him only used him as a porter.
Anyway, Soren helped him secretly, and now the results were finally showing.
’I guess he cultivated non-stop to be the first one to break through.’

Nick’s potential was 5th circle, and he had around seven thousand mana, while some of the other candidates the president recommended and three of Ryan’s classmates had 6th circle potential. So that was the only logical explanation.
’Returns are good too.’
While he expected the capacity expansion, getting refined mana as a return was a surprise. As for the potions and crystals, they were a welcome bonus.
[Ding!]
’Hmm?’
[A Thread of Return has formed.]
[Target: Nick Vil]
[Active Threads: 0 / 5]
[Would you like to bind this thread?]
[YES] [NO]
’Oh! Is this it?!’

Soren’s heartbeat sped up. This was one of the new features he had been waiting to test. If he understood it right, this was exactly what he had hoped for when he started lending out cultivation rooms for free.
He selected [YES] without hesitation.

The thread bound itself somewhere deep in his awareness, a faint pulse of connection that hadn’t been there before. It was subtle, like a strand of spider silk stretched across a great distance, but he could feel it. Nick was on the other end, unaware, and through that thread, a tiny trickle of refined mana would flow back to him every day. Fortunately, the thread had no effect on the target, or else it would have been no different from stealing.
’With this, I can increase my cultivation even faster!’
Soren tightened his fists in satisfaction.
’And tomorrow, I will put the new ability to the test.’

chapters.title: Chapter 242: The Frostfen Hollow [1]
paragraphs: [The Frostfen Hollow - 3rd Circle Gate]
"Are you feeling ok?"
Soren asked Ryan as they stepped through the portal into the frozen marsh beyond. The temperature dropped instantly, their breath fogging the air as their boots sank slightly into the bush.
"Yes, don’t worry about me," Ryan replied while brandishing his sword. "But this place is really vast."
"Indeed," Soren whispered as he looked at their surroundings.

The marsh stretched out in every direction, a flat expanse of brittle ice and muddy water, broken only by the skeletal remains of dead trees. Their branches clawed at the pale gray sky like frozen veins, offering no shelter and casting no shadows in the dim, directionless light. Thick patches of fog drifted between them, rolling through in slow waves that swallowed the landscape whole before releasing it again.

Thanks to his high Ice Affinity, Soren could easily see even in this fog. He didn’t feel any cold or discomfort either. In fact, he felt a lot stronger than usual in this environment. Even his senses felt sharper, picking up the faint vibrations in the slush.
"Get ready; we have company."
Soren barely finished the words before the slush beneath them exploded.

He threw himself sideways as a massive jaw snapped shut where he had been standing. He hit the ground, rolled, and came up with Nightfrost already in hand. Before he could fully regain his footing, a second shape burst out to his left. Then a third. Then more. He counted at least ten ripples moving through the ice around them, pale blue bodies sliding in and out of the slush with barely a sound.
"Ryan, on me!"
"Coming!"

Soren thrust his spear through the closest one as it lunged, the blade punching clean through its open mouth and out the back of its skull, and before the creature could even begin thrashing, he had already sidestepped a second strike and swept Nightfrost in a wide arc that opened a gash across another Lurker’s throat.

Ryan fought at his back, sword flashing as he hacked at anything that got too close. One Lurker shot past his guard, and he had to drop to a knee to avoid the bite, the creature’s scales scraping against his shoulder pauldron as it sailed over him.
"They’re too fast!"
"Keep moving. Don’t give them a target."

Soren formed a spike of ice and hurled it into a Lurker that was circling toward Ryan’s blind spot. The spike caught it in the side of the head, and the creature veered off course with a shriek, crashing into the slush a meter short of its target as two more surfaced behind it and slithered over its thrashing body without slowing.

He swept his spear low, catching one across the underside and flipping it onto its back before driving the blade down through its belly. The other lunged for his leg. He stepped into it instead of away, slamming the butt of his spear into its snout and following up with a thrust through the neck.

The remaining Lurkers paused, their heads swiveled as they sensed the vibrations of the dying thrashing around them. Then, one by one, they sank back beneath the slush, and the ripples retreated into the fog.
"They ran away?" Ryan muttered in disappointment.
"Seems like it." Soren chuckled. "However, stay on your guard; there might be more of them lurking around. Perhaps they left to bring the rest of the pack."
"Then we should pick up the pace.
Soren nodded and knelt beside one of the corpses, quickly storing its body before the slush could swallow it. Ryan followed suit and stored some in his own storage ring.
[Ding!]
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Frostscale Lurker]
[Stake: 82%]
[Dividend: +120 Refined Mana]
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Frostscale Lurker]
[Stake: 100%]
[Dividend: +140 Refined Mana]
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Frostscale Lurker]
[Stake: 100%]
[Dividend: +130 Refined Mana]
’Woah!’
Soren’s eyes widened in disbelief as a series of notification windows appeared in his vision.
’Is this how Equity Stake works in reality?’

According to what he learned after the authority advancement, Equity Stake allowed his attacks to accumulate a stake in the target proportional to the damage he dealt. When the target died, the stake was liquidated, granting him a dividend of refined mana based on his contribution. There was also a small chance of extracting one of the target’s abilities, with higher stakes improving the odds.
But he never expected it to be this powerful.
’That was almost a thousand mana from one skirmish.’

Coupled with his investments, passive returns from the threads, and now this ability, his cultivation speed was about to take a sharp turn upward. The road ahead was still dangerous, and the enemies still lurked in the shadows, but for the first time in a long while, the future didn’t feel quite as bleak.
’If I keep this up... I might actually be ready when the time comes.’
"Brother Soren, is something wrong?" Ryan asked from the side.
"Huh?" Soren blinked while dismissing the windows. "No, I was just a little distracted. Don’t mind it."
"If you say so," Ryan nodded. "Shall we go then?"
Soren nodded, and the two pressed deeper into the marsh.

The next hour was a blur of frost and steel. Frostscale Lurkers hunted them relentlessly, drawn by the vibrations of their footsteps through the slush. Soren lost count of how many they killed. Some came alone, others came in packs of ten or even twenty, coordinating their strikes with the eerie intelligence of creatures that had evolved to hunt in perfect silence. Their speed and abilities made them dangerous, and more than once, Soren felt jaws snap shut inches from his ankle as he twisted out of the way.

Ryan adapted quickly, learning to read the ripples in the ice and strike preemptively. His sword flashed again and again, and by the time they cleared the worst of it, his arms were streaked with black blood up to the elbows.
They also fought with Rotbeak Stalkers a few times.

They were a bit trickier to deal with because they could read surface memories of anyone who entered their territory, pulling out voices and faces to use as lures. Even though they had already researched them beforehand, Ryan almost ended up getting himself killed.
The monsters imitated his family’s voices and made an illusion of them being dragged away by monsters.
It looked so real that even Soren was caught up in it for a moment.

Soren asked Ryan as they stepped through the portal into the frozen marsh beyond.
The temperature dropped instantly, their breath fogging the air as their boots sank slightly into the bush.
"Yes, don’t worry about me," Ryan replied while brandishing his sword.
"But this place is really vast."
"Indeed," Soren whispered as he looked at their surroundings.
The marsh stretched out in every direction, a flat expanse of brittle ice and muddy water, broken only by the skeletal remains of dead trees.
Their branches clawed at the pale gray sky like frozen veins, offering no shelter and casting no shadows in the dim, directionless light.
Thick patches of fog drifted between them, rolling through in slow waves that swallowed the landscape whole before releasing it again.
Thanks to his high Ice Affinity, Soren could easily see even in this fog.
He didn’t feel any cold or discomfort either.
In fact, he felt a lot stronger than usual in this environment.
Even his senses felt sharper, picking up the faint vibrations in the slush.
"Get ready; we have company."
Soren barely finished the words before the slush beneath them exploded.
He threw himself sideways as a massive jaw snapped shut where he had been standing.
He hit the ground, rolled, and came up with Nightfrost already in hand.
Before he could fully regain his footing, a second shape burst out to his left.
Then a third.
Then more.
He counted at least ten ripples moving through the ice around them, pale blue bodies sliding in and out of the slush with barely a sound.
"Ryan, on me!"
"Coming!"

Soren thrust his spear through the closest one as it lunged, the blade punching clean through its open mouth and out the back of its skull, and before the creature could even begin thrashing, he had already sidestepped a second strike and swept Nightfrost in a wide arc that opened a gash across another Lurker’s throat.
Ryan fought at his back, sword flashing as he hacked at anything that got too close.
One Lurker shot past his guard, and he had to drop to a knee to avoid the bite, the creature’s scales scraping against his shoulder pauldron as it sailed over him.
"They’re too fast!"
"Keep moving.
Don’t give them a target."
Soren formed a spike of ice and hurled it into a Lurker that was circling toward Ryan’s blind spot.

The spike caught it in the side of the head, and the creature veered off course with a shriek, crashing into the slush a meter short of its target as two more surfaced behind it and slithered over its thrashing body without slowing.

The other lunged for his leg.
He stepped into it instead of away, slamming the butt of his spear into its snout and following up with a thrust through the neck.
