chapters.title: Chapter 243: The Frostfen Hollow [2]
paragraphs: Soren wanted to warn Ryan but noticed something and held back.
The illusion had one flaw, and Ryan had seen it: his parents would never cry for help like that; they would have told him to run away and save himself.
"Damn you!"

Ryan’s roar of anger shattered the trance as he charged straight at the fog, his sword cleaving into the real Stalker hiding inside. It died before it could even make a sound. Soren also joined the battle, and they quickly took care of them.

From then on, it became easy as they figured out the trick. The Stalkers always attacked from a different angle than where the voice came from, so they learned to watch the fog itself rather than the illusions. Ryan especially became fired up, cutting them down with a ferocity that left no room for tricks.
As for the Gloomwisps, they were the easiest to deal with.
Soren and Ryan knew how troublesome these ’cute’ monsters were if you got close, so they simply avoided them whenever they spotted those pale lights drifting through the haze.
But it was the Frostbound Husks that they struggled with the most.

It wasn’t that they were powerful; in fact, they could have been the weakest monsters in the Gate. A single solid strike was usually enough to put them down. But the problem was what they were. They shambled out of the fog in ones and twos, their bodies preserved by the endless cold, and every single one of them had once been a... living person.
They were hunters who had entered the gate and never made it back.
...That was one of the reasons why most hunters avoided this Gate. Because it felt like killing another human being, even though their appearance had already changed and their souls were long gone.

However, this was the exact reason why Soren had chosen this gate. Deep down, he knew they would eventually face other humans and races in the future, and there would come a time when killing was the only option. It would be either kill or get killed, and their enemies would certainly not hesitate. Neither could they. Especially Soren, as he already had enemies he wanted to cut down.
So, this gate was the perfect chance to get ready for that reality while the stakes were still manageable. However...
"...You don’t seem affected at all," Soren muttered as they finished a group of them.
"Ah, it’s probably because I am already used to it." Ryan smiled awkwardly. "I fought with countless people in the trial back then, so this is nothing compared to that.

"I guess this isn’t gonna help you then," Soren muttered. He still felt uncomfortable every time he struck one down, that brief hesitation before the blade connected, the nagging sense that something was wrong even though he knew it wasn’t.
"Those weren’t real people." Ryan shook his head. "Well... I hope not. And I still have a lot to learn. My heart was racing the whole time, so I need this just as much as you do."
Soren studied him for a moment, then nodded. "Alright. Let’s finish clearing the rest and find the boss."
"Roger."
The two of them continued through the marsh, cutting down the remaining Husks with mechanical efficiency. The hesitation never fully went away, but it got easier to push through.
"By the way, just what happened in those trials?" Soren asked after a while. "You mentioned fighting countless people."
Ryan’s steps slowed. For a moment, something flickered in his eyes, there and gone before Soren could name it.
"...I’d rather not talk about it." His voice was calm, but the usual cheerfulness had drained out of it entirely.
Soren held his gaze for a beat, then nodded. "Understood."

They trudged on in silence, the fog swallowing the space where the question had hung between them. Ryan would tell him what he’d been through when he was ready. And if he never was, that was okay too.
Another half hour saw the last of the Husks cleared out, with the final ones collapsing into the slush as the marsh fell silent around them.

Soren stretched, rolling his shoulder and looking out over the fog. His mana reserves were steady thanks to his abilities and the dividends from every kill. Ryan looked a little tired but alert, sword still in his grip.
"Think that’s the last of them?" Ryan asked.
"Probably." Soren squinted into the haze. "Which means the boss should be close."

They went further into the marsh, the ground beneath them changing from slush to hard ice, the dead trees becoming less common, until there was only open fog. The temperature fell further, enough that even Ryan’s breath began to mist in uneven bursts.
And then the fog parted.
"Is that the boss?" Ryan asked.

A massive figure stood in the center of a frozen clearing, motionless as a statue. Layers of rusted plate armor covered its body from head to toe, fused together by veins of black ice that pulsed faintly like frozen arteries. A single blue flame burned inside its helmet where a face should have been, casting pale light across the ice at its feet. In one hand, it gripped a greatsword made of frozen bone, the blade taller than Soren and twice as wide.
"Yeah," Soren replied, "it’s the boss, the Hollow Warden. And I think it noticed us."

As if on cue, it turned its head toward them, the rusted metal groaning with every inch of movement, and the flame inside its helmet flared a deeper blue. It dragged its greatsword through the ice as it began to move, the frozen ground splitting in a jagged line behind it, and the temperature around them plummeted so sharply that even Soren felt the first sting of true cold against his skin.
"Ryan!" Soren felt a grin spread across his face. "Wanna go all out?"
"Yes!"
Ryan shouted back, taking a combat stance.
"Good, then let’s do it!"
Soren felt his heart hammer against his ribs, not from fear, but from the thrill of finally facing something worthy of his full strength.
"Attack!"

chapters.title: Chapter 244: The Frostfen Hollow [3]
paragraphs: Name: Hollow Warden
Rank: 3rd Circle (Peak Stage)
Type: Undead Guardian (Boss)
Affinity: Ice / Decay

[Description]: The remnants of a knight who failed to protect his charge. His body was claimed by the marsh and reforged by centuries of accumulated mana. The flame inside his helmet is the last ember of his soul, twisted into an endless vigil over a kingdom that no longer exists.
[Abilities]:
- Frostbound Aura (Passive): Maintains a freezing zone within a 30-meter radius, causing all enemies to suffer gradual stamina drain and slowed movement.
- Bone Cleaver: The greatsword deals high physical damage and inflicts lingering frostbite wounds. The blade also carries a trace of decay that slows natural and magical healing.
- Glacial Stomp: Slams the ground to create a cone of ice spikes.
- Warden’s Call: Summons Frostbound Husks to assist.
- Frozen Reaving: When health is low, it enters an enraged state. Attack power and speed boost, and greatsword swings create lingering freezing mist that hampers movement.
- Soul Chill (Hidden): Prolonged exposure causes mental fatigue. Those without sufficient mental defenses may experience despair or hesitation.
[Harvest Value]: Warden’s Core | Frozen Plate Fragments | Bone Greatsword
’Whoa, it really deserves to be the boss.’ Soren muttered inwardly as he quickly inspected Hollow Warden using Advanced Appraisal. ’But-!’
[Quick Step]
Swoosh-!

He narrowly dodged the greatsword as it came crashing down, the frozen ground where he had been standing exploding into a spray of ice shards. The shockwave rattled his teeth even from a few meters away.

Ryan circled wide, his sword blazing as he channeled mana through Star-Fall Edge. He darted in low and slashed at the back of the Warden’s knee, but the rusted plate turned the blow aside with a screech of metal.

The Warden pivoted with surprising speed, bringing its greatsword around in a horizontal sweep. Ryan dropped flat, the blade passing inches above his head, and rolled away before the follow-up stomp could pin him.

Soren used the opening. He thrust Nightfrost into the Warden’s exposed side, aiming for the gap between the chest and shoulder plates. The tip punched through a weakened seam and bit into something solid beneath.
"Grr..." The Warden’s flame flared, and it swung its free arm in a backhanded strike. Soren caught it on Winter’s Barrier; the ice wall shattered but absorbed the impact.
"It’s tough," Soren called out, skidding backward. "Just aim for the leg joints.
"On it." Ryan’s sword flared brighter, and he pressed the attack. ’Amplification!’

The light along Star-Fall Edge faded, the blade pulling the surrounding mana into itself until only a thin line of darkness remained along its edge. Ryan closed the distance in three quick strides, feinting high before dropping into a crouch and bringing the sword down in a blistering vertical arc.
[Sunless Severance!]

The blade sliced seamlessly through the Warden’s leg just below the knee, dividing rusted plate, frozen sinew, and black ice in one smooth motion. The severed limb hit the ice with a dull crunch, and the Warden pitched forward, its balance gone.

Soren was already in motion as frost coiled along Nightfrost’s edge, spiraling from the shaft to the tip in a tightening coil of pale blue energy. While the Warden struggled to remain upright, Soren moved into its blind spot and swung the spear in a wide crescent arc.
[Glacial Sweep!]

A trail of frost followed the blade’s path, freezing the air itself as Nightfrost carved through the remaining leg. The Warden crashed forward, but before it could fall completely, it drove its greatsword deep into the ice and let out a roar that shook the entire clearing.
"ROOOAR!"
Soren’s eardrums throbbed as the sound slammed into him. His mana flared, coating his ears just in time to stop the worst of it. Ryan shook his head as his own mana flickered.
Crackle~ Crackle~
A hand burst through the surface near Soren’s foot. Then another, a few meters away. Pale fingers curled over the edges of the broken ice, pulling up arms, shoulders, heads.
"Husks?" Ryan became alarmed.
"I’ve got this." Soren drove Nightfrost into the ground and activated one of its skills.
[Glacial Chasm!]

The black ice spread across the clearing like spilled ink, swallowing the emerging Husks mid-climb. They froze, limbs locked in place, faces caught in silent anguish as darkness enveloped them entirely.
Soren kicked off the ground, Nightfrost raised above him. Ryan followed without a word, Star-Fall Edge igniting in his grip, the flames along the blade burning black.
[Glacial Descent!]
Soren fell first, his spear trailing frost as he plunged toward the Warden’s skull.
[Event Horizon!]

Ryan came a heartbeat behind, his sword drawing in the surrounding light until the edge blazed with condensed darkness. Together they struck, frost and black flame crashing into the Warden’s helmet. The blue flame inside shrieked and guttered, and the armored giant went still.

Cracks spidered across its frame, ice and shadow spreading through every joint until the Hollow Warden shattered into a cascade of lifeless metal, splintered bone, and black ice, then collapsed into the slush with a hollow thud.
The force of the dual impact blew away the surrounding fog, leaving the clearing completely still.

Soren landed lightly on his feet, spinning Nightfrost once before driving the pommel into the muddy ground to steady his breath. Beside him, Ryan brought Starfall Edge down in a slow arc, the dark flames clinging to his blade gradually dispersing into the cold air.
Silence settled over the marsh.
"That was good."
Soren chuckled as his gaze swept over the surroundings.
Just then, a familiar sound echoed in his head, followed by numerous notification windows.
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Hollow Warden]
[Stake: 57%]
[Dividend: +700 Refined Mana]

’...So many.’ Soren scrolled through the windows, tallying the numbers in his head. Between the Lurkers, the Stalkers, the Husks, and now the Warden, the total mana earned from this single raid has surpassed ten thousand. That was more than he would normally get from cultivating for a day.
’Coming here was definitely the right call.’
He dismissed the last of the notifications and turned to Ryan. "It was a bit weaker than we expected, huh."
Ryan let out a short laugh, resting Star-Fall Edge across his shoulder as he looked down at the pile of shattered armor. "Only because we didn’t give it a chance to unleash its full power."
"Mm." Soren nodded.

He had told Ryan to aim for the legs for a reason. If the Warden had been allowed to use Glacial Stomp freely and enter Frozen Reaving, the fight would have dragged on twice as long. Taking out its mobility first was the safest play, and it paid off.
"Let’s loot and take our leave." He added, already moving toward the fallen warden. "We have to reach our next destination on schedule."

The blue flame inside shrieked and guttered, and the armored giant went still.

Cracks spidered across its frame, ice and shadow spreading through every joint until the Hollow Warden shattered into a cascade of lifeless metal, splintered bone, and black ice, then collapsed into the slush with a hollow thud.
The force of the dual impact blew away the surrounding fog, leaving the clearing completely still.
Soren landed lightly on his feet, spinning Nightfrost once before driving the pommel into the muddy ground to steady his breath.
Beside him, Ryan brought Starfall Edge down in a slow arc, the dark flames clinging to his blade gradually dispersing into the cold air.
Silence settled over the marsh.
"That was good."
Soren chuckled as his gaze swept over the surroundings.
Just then, a familiar sound echoed in his head, followed by numerous notification windows.
[Equity Stake Liquidated]
[Target: Hollow Warden]
[Stake: 57%]
[Dividend: +700 Refined Mana]
’...So many.’ Soren scrolled through the windows, tallying the numbers in his head.
Between the Lurkers, the Stalkers, the Husks, and now the Warden, the total mana earned from this single raid has surpassed ten thousand.
That was more than he would normally get from cultivating for a day.
’Coming here was definitely the right call.’
He dismissed the last of the notifications and turned to Ryan.
"It was a bit weaker than we expected, huh."
Ryan let out a short laugh, resting Star-Fall Edge across his shoulder as he looked down at the pile of shattered armor.
"Only because we didn’t give it a chance to unleash its full power."
"Mm." Soren nodded.
He had told Ryan to aim for the legs for a reason.
If the Warden had been allowed to use Glacial Stomp freely and enter Frozen Reaving, the fight would have dragged on twice as long.
Taking out its mobility first was the safest play, and it paid off.
"Let’s loot and take our leave." He added, already moving toward the fallen warden.
"We have to reach our next destination on schedule."

chapters.title: Chapter 245: One Step at a Time
paragraphs: After clearing the Frostfen Hollow Gate, they raided two more Third Circle Gates. Soren received about twenty-one thousand Refined Mana in total, along with 2.5 million credits after selling all the cores and other loot. Unfortunately, he didn’t get any abilities, but considering the odds, it was understandable.

He then returned home and ate dinner with Ethea, Aunt Clara, and Emperor Hector. After that, he learned the new technique the Emperor promised to teach him. It was perfectly tailored to his style, a thrusting art designed to pierce through layered defenses by concentrating all his mana into a single point at the tip of the spear. The Emperor called it Glacial Fang and told him to use it as a finishing move.
Soren spent the rest of the night drilling the movements until his arms burned, committing every step and breath to memory.
Once he got back to the bedroom, he planned a schedule for the next week.

He would train with the Emperor twice a day, in the morning and at night. Similarly, he would learn from Aunt Clara and practice taking care of Ethea until he could handle everything smoothly on his own. The rest of the day would be split between clearing Gates with Ryan or other parties to accumulate more mana and credits, and spending time with Ethea. He would also have to track his ongoing investments and make more if there was a chance. At night, he would sleep for two hours and spend the rest cultivating mentally.
It was a packed schedule, but that was exactly what he needed.
However, there were also matters regarding the monolith and Malakor. He planned to have another meeting with the panther and ask him a few things, especially about Raine.

’If there is a chance, I should also invest in Ryan again.’ Soren added in his mind. ’Since both of his darkness and fire affinities are now SSS rank, it shouldn’t matter which element the magic beast aligns with. Either one would work. But I should ask him first before making any moves.’
He made a mental note to bring it up the next time they met.
’Wait... I think we should also increase our Hunter ranks while we have the chance.’

President Craig was willing to help them while they were still here, so it was a perfect opportunity to push through the rank-up exams. He and Ryan had already cleared multiple Third Circle Gates together, which was more than enough to qualify for a promotion. A higher hunter rank meant access to better resources, higher-paying contracts, and less scrutiny when moving through major cities.
’I’ll talk to Ryan about it tomorrow. We can schedule the exams before the week ends.’
Satisfied with the plan, he let out a slow breath and leaned back. But as his mind began to settle, another thought surfaced.
’Father-in-law...’

They hadn’t heard from him since that visit, and Soren had no idea if he was still in the city or had already left. For all he knew, the man could just be monitoring them with those spirits of his or waiting for them to change their minds. Whatever the case, he and Ethea had already decided to reject his invitation to return to the capital with him. He would send a message tomorrow to make that clear. However...
’We still haven’t decided what to do and where to go yet...’
He glanced at Ethea’s sleeping face and sighed inwardly.
’Should we go straight to the Tower or take a detour in the Temur Empire...’

Both paths had their merits. The Tower promised rapid growth and the resources they desperately needed, but it also meant throwing themselves into the most dangerous proving ground in the world. As for the Temur Empire, he could set up a long-term investment there and save his sister along the way, but they might lose time or even put her in danger.
’Urgh... should we just do both then?’
He rubbed his temples. However, it wasn’t a decision he could make alone.
’I’ll talk to Ethea about it tomorrow. And... The curse...’

He had asked Hector about it earlier, but the Emperor admitted he still hadn’t spoken with his acquaintances. Contacting them was difficult, he had said, and the process would take time. He promised to notify Soren the moment he received any answers.
’Time...’
Everything seemed to hinge on that word lately. Time to grow stronger. Time to find answers. Time to prepare before the curse tightened its grip or their enemies made their move...
’Sigh... Let’s just rest for now...’

He closed his eyes and let the tension drain from his body. There was no point in dwelling on things he couldn’t control. The schedule was set, the goals were clear, and whatever came next, he would face it one step at a time.
Some time later...

Hector sat alone in the underground chamber beneath the villa, surrounded by walls etched with numerous runes and barriers. A mysterious magic circle was drawn beneath him, its faint silver lines pulsing softly in the dark.

He took a deep breath and let his perception sweep over the whole city. Then he looked at the ordinary silver ring on his hand, rubbed it once, and closed his eyes before speaking the incantation in his mind.

A few moments later, a familiar pull tugged at his chest, and his spiritual body slipped free of his flesh like a hand withdrawing from a glove. Time passed, darkness behind his eyelids stretched and tore.
When he opened his eyes, he was no longer in the chamber.

He was standing in a large hall that resembled a palace from a forgotten era. Pillars of dark marble rose toward a ceiling painted with faded constellations, their gold leaf peeling in places. Tall windows lined the walls, letting in pale starlight that pooled on the polished floor like water. At the far end of the hall, a single throne sat on a raised dais, its seat empty.
’Still not here, huh.’
Sighing in disappointment, Hector crossed the hall and took his usual seat at one of the lower chairs arranged before the throne.
Time stretched.
The starlight crept across the floor in slow inches. Hector watched it without really seeing, his thoughts drifting back to the conversation with Soren.
’...I hope someone shows up this time.’

chapters.title: Chapter 246: Their Fate
paragraphs: Hector didn’t know how much time had passed, but eventually, the doors at the far end of the hall swung open, and a figure stepped through.
He quickly looked over and stood up immediately as recognition crossed his features. He pressed a fist to his chest as he bowed his head. "Lady Herald."

The woman who entered moved with a grace that made the starlight itself seem to follow her. Her hair flowed white as fresh snow, cascading past her shoulders in soft waves. A cloth of pale silk covered her eyes, wrapped gently around her head, yet she navigated the hall without the slightest hesitation. Her presence carried a purity that filled the chamber like the first breath of winter air.
She inclined her head as she approached. "Warden Hector. Forgive me for making you wait. The threads of fate do not always weave themselves into convenient patterns."
"It is no trouble at all. I would have waited longer if needed."
A faint smile touched her lips. With a single step, she crossed the length of the hall and appeared at the seat opposite his. She gestured gracefully toward his chair. "Please. Sit."

Hector nodded and lowered himself back into his seat. He hesitated for a moment, then spoke. "Lady Herald, if I may ask... has the Lord Arbiter been free lately? Is there a chance I might meet with him?"

The Herald’s smile remained gentle, but there was a knowing quality to it. "Unfortunately, the Lord Arbiter is occupied with matters of great importance and cannot be disturbed. However..." She tilted her head slightly. "I should be able to answer whatever questions you carry."

"Then I’ll get straight to the point." Hector nodded, a faint smile crossing his weathered face. "I want to know why Warden Ethea was expelled from our ranks, and more importantly, why no one stepped forward to offer her support afterward."
The Herald was silent for a moment. Then she spoke, her voice softer than before.
"There was a reason for that. A rather important one. However... it is not something I can share with you, Warden Hector."
Hector’s brow furrowed. "...Is it related to the curse she bears?"
The Herald nodded slowly. "That is part of it."
"Then can we at least help her with that?" Hector leaned forward, his voice tightening. "She has been suffering for months. Surely we have resources that could-"

"Warden Hector." The Herald’s voice was gentle, but it cut through his words like a blade through silk. "I can only tell you one thing... The curse is the reason she has survived this long. To interfere with it now would be to take away the very thing that has kept her alive.
Hector looked at her with a frown, puzzled by her cryptic words.
"We should not intervene," she continued. "Because that is the only path through which she can endure what is to come."
She paused, and a faint smile returned to her lips.
"Besides... she already has the greatest helper she could ever hope for by her side."
Hector’s eyes widened. "You mean... her husband? Soren?"
The Herald’s smile remained, offering neither confirmation nor denial.
"...I understand. But... Is there really no way we can help them?"
"...Aren’t you already helping them?" The Herald replied. "You saved their life and are now helping them prepare for the future. And... While ’we’ can’t help them, it’s different for you."
"...I see," Hector whispered, seeming to understand something from the Herald’s words. "Then I will take my leave. Take care, Lady Herald."
Lady Herald nodded and watched as Hector’s body disintegrated into particles of light.
She remained seated long after he had gone, the starlight shifting slowly across the empty hall. Her fingers traced the armrest of her chair, and a sigh escaped her lips.
"...This is their fate. We can only hope for the best. As our fate is deeply tied to theirs..."

"...Done," Soren whispered as he pulled the soft hem of the tunic down, finishing dressing Ethea. He gently adjusted her position, leaning her back against the cushions until she was comfortable. "And the next is..."

He reached out and picked up the towel he had already prepared. He draped it lightly over her damp hair and began patting it dry, working slowly from the top of her head down to the ends. Once most of the moisture had been absorbed, he traded the towel for a comb and started working through the strands, beginning at the tips and gradually moving upward to avoid pulling.
Ethea kept her eyes shut the whole time, her cheeks still warm from the embarrassment of being dressed by him, yet she could not deny how much she enjoyed being taken care of by him.
It was strange, really.

When Aunt Clara or others helped her, she didn’t feel anything in particular. But when Soren did it, she became acutely aware of every little touch. The way his fingers brushed against her scalp as he dried her hair. The gentle tug of the comb as he worked through the strands. The warmth of his presence so close to her. It all made her heart beat a little faster, and she had no idea how to explain it.
She... She did know.

Deep down, she had known for a while now. But admitting it meant opening a door she wasn’t sure she was ready to walk through. Perhaps because she was afraid of what would change between them. Perhaps because it didn’t feel like the right time, not with everything hanging over their heads. Or perhaps she simply hadn’t found the courage to put those feelings into words.

So she kept them locked away, letting moments like this speak in her place. A slight tilt of her head when his fingers brushed her neck. The way she stopped holding her breath whenever he stepped into the room. Little things that she hoped he noticed without her having to explain them.
"There." Soren set the comb aside and ran his fingers through her hair one last time, smoothing it down her back. "All done."
Ethea opened her eyes and looked up at him. "...Thank you."
"Don’t mention it." Soren chuckled. "Anyway, shall we go out now? Auntie must be tired of waiting by now."
"Alright, let’s go then." Soren gently lifted her, placed her into the wheelchair, and rolled her outside. ’...I hope I passed the test.’

chapters.title: Chapter 247: Farewell [1]
paragraphs: "Good job!" Aunt Clara gave Soren a thumbs-up. "You passed the test with flying colors. But let’s hear what the lady herself has to say." She turned to Ethea and smiled. "On a scale of 1 to 10, how would you rate your husband’s performance today?"
Ethea looked stunned, the heat quickly returning to her face.
Her voice was so low Clara had to lean down to listen.
"Two?"
"...T...Ten." Ethea corrected.
"Aha!" Clara clapped her hands together. "A perfect score! Now that’s what I call a successful student. Well done, Soren."
"T-Thank you." Soren rubbed the back of his neck, his own cheeks warming. "I... I still have a lot to improve."

"That might be true, but you’ve come a long way since that first lesson. I still remember how you fumbled with the simplest tasks, your face redder than a tomato the entire time." Clara chuckled at the memory. "Now look at you, doing everything by yourself. Ethea is lucky to have you."
Soren glanced at Ethea, a soft smile crossing his face. "I’m the lucky one."
Ethea’s cheeks flushed deeper, and she looked down at her lap, unable to meet his gaze.

Clara watched the exchange with a knowing smile. But it soon turned into a reluctant and sad one, as she realized this was their last day together. Because tomorrow, Soren and Ethea would leave Kalmira, and she would probably never see them again...
"You two..." She paused, searching for the right words. "Take care of each other, alright? And... Please... Don’t forget to contact me from time to time too."
Ethea raised her head and exchanged a glance with Soren. Then they both looked at her and nodded. "We will.

"..." Clara’s lips curled up once more. A few tears slipped down her cheeks, and she quickly wiped them away with the back of her hand. "A-Anyway, let’s go. The breakfast is gonna get cold if we stand around any longer, and I didn’t wake up early just to let my cooking go to waste."

"Alright, let’s go." Soren played along with her, and they all went into the kitchen to eat. The table was set with more food than three people could reasonably finish, as if she had tried to pour everything she couldn’t say into the meal itself. She had even prepared Soren’s favorite dumplings and special cookies for Ethea.
"Auntie..."
Soren and Ethea looked at her in unison, both of them at a loss for words.
Clara waved a hand, already taking her seat. "Don’t just stand there and take a seat."
Soren nodded, placed Ethea near the table, and sat down beside her. For a while, the only sounds were the clinking of utensils and the occasional comment about the food.

The dumplings were perfectly seasoned, and the cookies melted on Ethea’s tongue. Soren ended up eating more than he usually did, partly because it was delicious and he didn’t want to waste them, and partly because he knew this might be the last time he would get to eat her cooking.
Halfway through the meal, Clara set down her spoon and looked at them.

"You know... when I first met you two, I thought you were just another young couple I would work for and part ways without any attachments. It turned out to be wrong. Because somewhere along the way, you became something more." She smiled with eyes that shimmered. "You became... family."
Soren set down his own spoon and met her eyes. "Auntie, we feel the same way as well."
"You are family," Ethea added in a gentle voice. "And it won’t change, no matter how apart we are."
"...Hick... Y-You... You two are... making me cry again." Clara sniffled as she spoke.
A few tears escaped from Ethea’s eyelids as well.
Soren quickly took out tissues and handed one to Clara, then turned to gently dab at Ethea’s cheeks.
As for why he didn’t cry, well...

He stopped doing that many years ago, back when he was still a child. Because crying only brought more beatings and trouble. But, looking at the two women beside him, he could feel the sensation coming back again.

Fortunately, he managed to hold it back till they calmed down. In fact, it disappeared soon after when they started laughing when Aunt Clara tried to make an excuse that it was because her tea was too bitter, which made her cry.
Since the mood was lifted, the rest of the meal passed with lighter conversation and promises to stay in touch.
"See you tomorrow~"
Clara waved as she got into the car.
Soren waved back with both hands in place of Ethea. "Take care."
He then nodded at Uncle Ben, who had finally recovered and got back to being Auntie’s ’exclusive driver’.
"Let’s head out as well, shall we?"
Soren smiled and led Ethea back into the villa. They soon came out in a car and headed to their own destination: Ryan’s house.

After much discussion, they had finally decided to go to the Temur Empire first. The Tower would come after. They also agreed to travel separately from Ryan and his family, since there was a real chance that Soren and Ethea could be attacked along the way. If that happened, having Ryan’s family nearby would only put them in danger. It was safer for everyone if they moved on their own.
However, they still wanted to bid them farewell before leaving.

There were also two weeks before Ryan finished this semester, so the timing didn’t match properly either. They also wanted to give Ryan enough time to wrap up his affairs in Kalmira and travel at his own pace. Rushing him would only cause problems for his family, and that was the last thing Soren wanted.
In fact, this was a kind of test too.

To see if Ryan could manage on his own. He had grown a lot in the past two months, but traveling to a foreign empire was different from clearing gates together. He would need to handle things without Soren watching his back, and this separation would give him the chance to prove himself. Especially to his parents.

Now that’s what I call a successful student.
Well done, Soren."
"T-Thank you." Soren rubbed the back of his neck, his own cheeks warming.
I still have a lot to improve."
"That might be true, but you’ve come a long way since that first lesson.
I still remember how you fumbled with the simplest tasks, your face redder than a tomato the entire time." Clara chuckled at the memory.
"Now look at you, doing everything by yourself.
Ethea is lucky to have you."
Soren glanced at Ethea, a soft smile crossing his face.
"I’m the lucky one."
Ethea’s cheeks flushed deeper, and she looked down at her lap, unable to meet his gaze.
Clara watched the exchange with a knowing smile.
But it soon turned into a reluctant and sad one, as she realized this was their last day together.
Because tomorrow, Soren and Ethea would leave Kalmira, and she would probably never see them again...
"You two..." She paused, searching for the right words.
"Take care of each other, alright?
And...
Please...
Don’t forget to contact me from time to time too."
Ethea raised her head and exchanged a glance with Soren.
Then they both looked at her and nodded.
"We will.
"..." Clara’s lips curled up once more.
A few tears slipped down her cheeks, and she quickly wiped them away with the back of her hand.
"A-Anyway, let’s go.
The breakfast is gonna get cold if we stand around any longer, and I didn’t wake up early just to let my cooking go to waste."
"Alright, let’s go." Soren played along with her, and they all went into the kitchen to eat.
The table was set with more food than three people could reasonably finish, as if she had tried to pour everything she couldn’t say into the meal itself.
She had even prepared Soren’s favorite dumplings and special cookies for Ethea.
"Auntie..."
Soren and Ethea looked at her in unison, both of them at a loss for words.
Clara waved a hand, already taking her seat.
"Don’t just stand there and take a seat."
Soren nodded, placed Ethea near the table, and sat down beside her.
For a while, the only sounds were the clinking of utensils and the occasional comment about the food.
The dumplings were perfectly seasoned, and the cookies melted on Ethea’s tongue.

Soren ended up eating more than he usually did, partly because it was delicious and he didn’t want to waste them, and partly because he knew this might be the last time he would get to eat her cooking.
Halfway through the meal, Clara set down her spoon and looked at them.
"You know... when I first met you two, I thought you were just another young couple I would work for and part ways without any attachments.
It turned out to be wrong.
Because somewhere along the way, you became something more." She smiled with eyes that shimmered.
"You became... family."
Soren set down his own spoon and met her eyes.
"Auntie, we feel the same way as well."
"You are family," Ethea added in a gentle voice.
"And it won’t change, no matter how apart we are."
Y-You...
You two are... making me cry again." Clara sniffled as she spoke.
A few tears escaped from Ethea’s eyelids as well.
Soren quickly took out tissues and handed one to Clara, then turned to gently dab at Ethea’s cheeks.
As for why he didn’t cry, well...
He stopped doing that many years ago, back when he was still a child.
Because crying only brought more beatings and trouble.
But, looking at the two women beside him, he could feel the sensation coming back again.
Fortunately, he managed to hold it back till they calmed down.
In fact, it disappeared soon after when they started laughing when Aunt Clara tried to make an excuse that it was because her tea was too bitter, which made her cry.
Since the mood was lifted, the rest of the meal passed with lighter conversation and promises to stay in touch.
"See you tomorrow~"
Clara waved as she got into the car.
Soren waved back with both hands in place of Ethea.
"Take care."
He then nodded at Uncle Ben, who had finally recovered and got back to being Auntie’s ’exclusive driver’.
"Let’s head out as well, shall we?"
Soren smiled and led Ethea back into the villa.
They soon came out in a car and headed to their own destination: Ryan’s house.
After much discussion, they had finally decided to go to the Temur Empire first.
The Tower would come after.
They also agreed to travel separately from Ryan and his family, since there was a real chance that Soren and Ethea could be attacked along the way.
If that happened, having Ryan’s family nearby would only put them in danger.
It was safer for everyone if they moved on their own.
However, they still wanted to bid them farewell before leaving.
There were also two weeks before Ryan finished this semester, so the timing didn’t match properly either.
They also wanted to give Ryan enough time to wrap up his affairs in Kalmira and travel at his own pace.
Rushing him would only cause problems for his family, and that was the last thing Soren wanted.
In fact, this was a kind of test too.
To see if Ryan could manage on his own.
He had grown a lot in the past two months, but traveling to a foreign empire was different from clearing gates together.
He would need to handle things without Soren watching his back, and this separation would give him the chance to prove himself.
Especially to his parents.

chapters.title: Chapter 248: Farewell [2]
paragraphs: They were welcomed warmly by Ryan’s family. And, as Soren expected, his mother and little sister surrounded Ethea the moment they entered the house and took their seats. Helpless, Soren could only join Ryan’s father’s side.

Looking at the table, Soren was immediately hit with a sense of dejavu. Because it was also filled with more food than they could possibly eat. Plates of sliced fruits, fresh dumplings and bread, small pastries, and a steaming pot of tea sat waiting for them.
Soren raised a hand politely. "Thank you, but we just had breakfast. We really can’t-"
"Nonsense." Ryan’s mother waved off his protest before he could finish. "You are guests in our home. Sit, eat. Even if it’s just a little."
Soren hesitated, then glanced at Ryan, who gave him a look that said arguing was pointless. With a small sigh and a smile, Soren picked up a piece of bread. "It’s tasty!"
"Then eat more! You will need a lot of energy for a long journey."
The conversation drifted naturally toward the Temur Empire and the Etenia Academy. Ryan’s parents asked question after question.
Like... Was the Temur Empire safe? How long would the journey take? And was it really true that their son had received a recommendation to the Etenia Academy? Who was this mysterious benefactor?
And so on.
However, that made it obvious how worried they were about their child.

So, Soren answered each one patiently, explaining what he knew and reassuring them where he could. From across the room, Ryan shot him a grateful glance, and Soren responded with a subtle nod before turning back to the next question.

"Thank you for being patient and answering our questions, Mr. Soren," Ryan’s mother said, her voice warm but tinged with emotion. "And thank you for helping our son all this time. He has changed so much since he met you."

Soren smiled and shook his head. "There’s no need to thank me. Ryan has helped me just as much. Honestly, he is far more mature than any kid his age I have ever met. You should be proud of him. And you don’t need to worry too much, too. He knows what he’s doing."
Ryan’s parents exchanged a look, and his mother nodded slowly, some of the tension leaving her shoulders. His father placed a hand on Ryan’s head, ruffling his hair without a word.
Soren glanced at the clock and stood. "We should take our leave now."
"Already?" Ryan’s mother stood as well. "Please, stay a little longer. You haven’t even eaten any dessert yet.
"I’m sorry," Soren replied, "but we still have a few more places to go before the day ends."
Reluctantly, they accepted.
Ryan’s family walked them to the door, and after a final round of farewells, Soren took Ethea outside and made their way back to the car.
"See you in a month~" Soren waved at Ryan, who had come out to see them off.
Ryan nodded. "I wish you safe travels. Goodbye, Brother Soren and Sister-in-law!"
"Goodbye."

With that final farewell, Soren pressed the accelerator and pulled away from the curb. Ryan stood at the edge of the driveway, watching the car grow smaller until it rounded the corner and slipped out of sight.
"Till we meet again..."
"...You are here."
"Yes, sorry to make you wait." Soren apologized as he greeted Director Elenaria.
"You don’t have to apologize." Elenaria shook her head and gestured for him to follow her. "By the way, I heard from the president that you’re leaving the city?"
"Ah, yes, we are departing tomorrow evening," Soren replied casually. "Why do you ask, though?"
"Well, I just wanted to test something, but it seems like I won’t be able to." Elenaria sighed in disappointment.
Soren tilted his head. "Test what?

"...When a bonded magic beast dies, it takes some time before the wielder can form a new bond. I was going to help you check whether your bond with Raine had truly been severed. And perhaps..." She glanced at him. "If the bond is gone, you could have tried to bond with the Aurora Kitsune again."

Soren went silent for a moment. Then he spoke, his voice quieter than before. "Thank you for worrying about me, Director. But... I actually saw it... her death... when I visited Malakor the other day."
Elenaria stopped walking. "...Malakor showed it to you?"
Soren nodded, keeping his expression sad and guilty.

Elenaria closed her eyes briefly and exhaled. "I see. Then I am truly sorry for your loss, Mr. Soren." She paused, as if searching for the right words. "Even though I never met her, I can tell she was a remarkable magic beast. To willingly sacrifice herself for you..."
She let the sentence hang, then shook her head and looked back at him.
"...Then, should I keep the Kitsune reserved for you, Mr. Soren? In case you return to Kalmira?"

"...I would appreciate that." Soren nodded slowly. Even if he couldn’t bond with another magic beast himself, there was still Ethea. Her core might recover one day, and when it did, she would be able to form a bond again. Keeping the Kitsune as a potential partner for her was worth it. "But if someone worthy shows up before we return, don’t hold it on our account. The little Kitsune deserves a good partner."
Elenaria studied him for a moment, then smiled faintly. "You really are different from most humands, Mr. Soren."
"You flatter me, Director." Soren shook his head. "...Director, actually, I have been meaning to ask you something for a long time."
Elenaria tilted her head. "Oh? Go ahead."
Soren hesitated for a brief moment, then met her eyes. "I was wondering if you could check something for me. Have there been any spirits around me or my wife? Either now or in the past?"
Elenaria paused, her gaze shifting to Ethea for a brief moment before returning to Soren.
"There are indeed spirits around you right now, Mr. Soren. But I assume they are not the ones you are referring to."
"...You are right."

chapters.title: Chapter 249: Farewell [3]
paragraphs: Now was the perfect opportunity to find out if his father-in-law was using his spirits to monitor them. He couldn’t ask the first time because he had been too shaken by Raine’s ’death’, and the other day, Ethea hadn’t been with him.

Director Elenaria paused for a moment, her eyes shimmering with a subtle silver glow as she observed their surroundings. She reexamined Soren with increased scrutiny before turning her attention to Ethea, studying her intently for several seconds. When she finally shifted her gaze back to him, her face had grown more solemn.
"...There is a faint trace. A spirit of darkness has been near your wife, probably a few times. And... It’s probably a darkness spirit."
"I see..." Soren muttered. ’So I was right...’
"Then, is there a way to ward them off? Something that can prevent spirits from approaching us or protect against them? Or a method to sense or see them?"
Elenaria fell silent, her brow furrowing as she considered the question.

"Unless one has an affinity for spirits, it is usually impossible to see them," she said at last. "But there are some artifacts that allow one to sense spirits, interact with them, or even protect against them. But they are really rare and hard to find even for me."

She tapped her chin lightly with her finger. "There is another way. High-ranking spirits can reveal themselves willingly if they choose to. But that requires the spirit to recognize you, and most spirits are not interested in the affairs of mortals."
"...I see," Soren whispered. "Thank you, Director. This has been more helpful than you know."

Elenaria studied him for a moment, as if sensing there was more he wasn’t saying. But she didn’t press. "If you wish to learn more or find such artifacts, you could visit the Elven Dominion. There are many scholars and powerful spirit mages there that might be able to help you."
Soren nodded. "I’ll remember that."

"Hmm... Actually, Malakor might be useful for your situation. He’s a magic beast of darkness and an S-rank one at that. And magic beasts tend to have senses far sharper than humans, especially when it comes to their own element. A darkness spirit would be hard for him to miss."
"Oh, I didn’t know that."

"It’s natural. And... you are making the right choice by taking him with you. Although your first encounter with him was nothing short of terrible, I’m sure he will be a great help to you in your future endeavors. After all, his life is in your hands."
"...Right.

"One more thing..." Elenaria’s voice grew solemn. "I advise you to never reveal he is your slave. Treat him as your bond partner instead, both in public and even in private. You may hold the seal, but that does not mean you have to act like a master. Show him the same respect you would give a true bond, and in time, he may return it. A relationship built on trust will always be stronger than one built on fear, and it will make working together far easier for both of you."
She paused, letting the words settle before continuing.

"Beyond that, a magic beast of his rank is rare enough to draw attention on its own. If word spreads that you hold an S-rank creature under a slave seal, it will attract the kind of people you do not want to meet. But if the world believes he is your bond, they will see a talented hunter and his loyal partner. The difference could save your life one day."
Soren nodded slowly. "I will heed your advice, Director. Thank you."
Elenaria offered a faint smile. "Though I am sure you already knew most of this. I simply wanted to remind you before you left."
She gestured ahead, where the familiar doors of Malakor’s chamber had come into view. "Now then, he is waiting for you inside."
"..." Soren wheeled Ethea inside and saw Malakor sitting not far from the door, the chains from the previous time completely gone.
"This lowly slave greets his master." He bowed his head respectfully.

"..." Soren squinted at him. "...We are leaving. I am taking you with me. But first, I need to know. Can you enter my soul space? Or become smaller? It would be troublesome to walk around with a massive panther following me everywhere."
"I will simply stay in your shadow, Master. It will be far easier to protect you that way."
Soren nodded. "Do it."
"As you wish."

Malakor’s form began to dissolve, his massive body unraveling into streams of darkness that flowed across the floor like spilled ink. The shadows pooled at Soren’s feet, then sank into his own, merging seamlessly until nothing remained but a faint shimmer along the edges of his silhouette.
Soren watched the process with a calm expression, then turned to Elenaria. "We will take our leave now, Director."
Elenaria nodded and walked them to the exit of the sanctuary. At the door, she paused and turned to face them one last time.
"I wish you both safe travels, Mr. Soren, Mrs. Everly. If fate allows, we will meet again."
"Thank you for all your help as well, Director." Soren placed a hand over his chest and gave a small bow. "Nae g’onen."
Elenaria’s eyes widened slightly, genuine surprise flickering across her usually composed features. Then her expression softened into a warm smile.
"You know our tongue..." She returned the gesture, her voice carrying a note of respect. "Nae vue g’onen, Soren. May the stars guide your path."
Soren smiled and turned, pushing Ethea toward the exit. As the doors closed behind them, her voice echoed in his mind.
’You know the elven language?’

Soren chuckled inwardly. ’Only the basics. An elf coworker taught me a few things back when I worked at the restaurant. I was just curious at the time. Didn’t expect it to actually come in handy like this.’
’...You worked in a restaurant?’
’Ah, yes, though only for a few months.’
’...Can you tell me more about it on the way?’
’Sure, but you will tell me about your past too. Deal?’
’...Deal.’

chapters.title: Chapter 250: Farewell [4]
paragraphs: "President, thank you for all your support until now." Soren hung his head. "And... I apologize for any inconvenience we have caused so far."

Craig shook his head, a faint smile flashing across his worn face. "Don’t worry about any of that. None of it was your fault anyway. You were caught up in things that were beyond your control, and you did the best you could with them."
"Soren..." He moved closer, putting a hand on Soren’s shoulder. "I hope you both have a safe journey, no matter where you’re headed. I hope you are able to overcome any dangers you might face."
"Thank you, President." Soren straightened and met his eyes. "I won’t forget everything you’ve done for us."
Craig nodded, his face warm but burdened, like someone who had said goodbye too often. "Goodbye, Soren."
"Take care, President." Soren nodded one last time and wheeled Ethea outside.
Craig stood still for a few moments after the door clicked shut. He then walked back to his chair and sat down.
"Sigh..."
He leaned back, staring at the ceiling for a long moment before turning his head toward the empty space beside his desk. "Are you finally gonna leave as well?"
The air rippled, and a voice emerged from the stillness.
"...What do you mean? I already left a week ago."

Craig didn’t bother to look surprised. "Whatever you say." He studied the empty space for a moment. "But are you sure about this? Weren’t you planning to take them to the capital with you? And... why did you let them find out about the spirit?"
"...Well, let’s say I changed my mind. As for the other matter, I have no idea what you’re talking about."
Craig let out a scoff. However, his expression soon became solemn. "You... You know you’re playing a dangerous game, right?"
"Of course."
"Then you should also know how easily it can all fall apart."
"I know."
"..." Craig turned his gaze back to the door where Soren and Ethea had left. "Do they really have to go through all this? Isn’t there any better way?"
"...I wish there was."
"...Sigh. Alright, I won’t pry any further. Just... make sure you don’t regret it."
"You there?"
"...This f*cker." Craig cursed out loud, though his lips were turned upward into a grin. "He always leaves like this."

Three figures cut through the night sky, silhouettes against a sea of stars. The clouds parted around them like waves against a ship’s bow, and far below, the lights of Kalmira had long since faded into the darkness. Only the moon and the endless stretch of stars bore witness to their passage.

Soren held Ethea against his chest, her arms linked loosely around his neck as she gazed out at the sea of clouds drifting beneath them. Emperor Hector was above them with his hands clasped behind his back, his mana enveloping them in an invisible barrier.
’Are you cold?’
’...A little.’
Soren quickly adjusted his grip, pulling her closer, and let his body heat seep through the fabric of her cloak.
Perhaps noticing their exchange, Hector glanced down at them. "Are you both ok?"
"Y-Yes, thank you. Don’t worry about us, Sir." Soren replied hurriedly, though he was still not quite used to being carried through the sky like this.
’Perhaps, we should have departed in the morning?’ He thought but quickly dismissed the idea. ’...No, we are doing the right thing.’

It had been his own idea to leave under the cover of darkness, when the odds of being followed were at their lowest. As for the talk about leaving tomorrow evening, it had obviously been a lie, a small deception meant to throw off anyone who might be watching. A necessary precaution, even if it meant sacrificing a night of rest.

They had actually slipped out of the city shortly after dinner, with only the Emperor being aware since he was their escort. Now, hours later, they moved across the night sky like shadows escaping the dawn.
Soren glanced down at the clouds drifting past beneath them. The journey ahead was long, and there was still much he didn’t know about where they were going. He looked up toward the Emperor.
"Sir, how long until we reach the border?"
"At this speed, we will arrive by dawn," Hector replied without turning. "We will stop briefly to rest, then continue toward the first waypoint. From there, you will travel on your own."

Soren nodded. The Emperor had already made it clear he wouldn’t accompany them the entire way. He had his own work to do in Kalmira, and escorting them this far was already more than Soren had expected.
"I understand. Thank you for taking us this far.

Hector inclined his head slightly but said nothing more. The silence that followed was comfortable, filled only by the rush of wind beyond the barrier and the soft rhythm of Ethea’s breathing against his chest.
’...Malakor.’
’Yes, master?’
’Are we... being followed?’
’...No, Master. There is no one within my sensory range. Whatever tracks you may have left, no one has picked them up yet.’
’I see. Keep watching then and let me know the moment anything changes.’
’Understood.’
Soren let out a relieved sigh and shifted his grip on Ethea.
’...Let’s take a look, just in case.’
He glanced down at Ethea, intending to use Advanced Appraisal, but his eyes met hers before he could activate it. And just like that, his mind went blank.
The stars above, the clouds below, the wind rushing past the barrier. All of it faded. He became lost in her gaze, caught in the quiet depths of her eyes without meaning to be.
’...Beautiful.’
A few seconds passed.
Ethea’s eyes widened, and she quickly looked away, her cheeks coloring.
’...’ Soren blinked, realizing he had been staring, and felt heat creep up his own neck. He cleared his throat and activated the ability, fixing his gaze ahead, where a status window was floating.
It served as a nice distraction as he slowly inspected the lines. Until...
[Mental State: Embarrassed, Self-Conscious, Hyper-Aware]
’...Gulp.’
